Prior to its release, ''[[Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine]]'' and ''[[PlayStation: The Official Magazine|PlayStation Magazine]]'' praised ''Beyond Good & Evil'' at [[E3]] 2003 and described it as one of the best titles on display.<ref name="OPM-71"/><ref>{{cite magazine| magazine = [[PlayStation: The Official Magazine|PlayStation Magazine]]| title = E3 2003| publisher = [[Future plc|Future Publishing]]| issue = 74| page = 48|date=August 2003}}</ref>

''Beyond Good & Evil'' received "generally favorable" reviews from critics, according to [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MCXBOX" /><ref name="MCGC" /><ref name="MCPS2" /><ref name="MCX360" /><ref name="MCPS3" /><ref name="MCPC" />

The game's graphics were generally well received. In reviewing the GameCube version, ''[[Game Informer]]'' wrote that "Every moment of ''Beyond Good & Evil'' looks as good as a traditional [[Role-playing game|RPG]] [[cutscene]]" and that the game's effects and character animations were "amazing".<ref name="gi-gc review">{{cite web|url=http://www.gameinformer.com/NR/exeres/D989B470-043B-4A32-9CA9-DEB773C849DA.htm?CS_pid=220353|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012135808/http://gameinformer.com/NR/exeres/D989B470-043B-4A32-9CA9-DEB773C849DA.htm?CS_pid=220353|archive-date=October 12, 2007 |title=Beyond the Norm|publisher=[[Game Informer]]|url-status=dead|access-date=April 29, 2010}}</ref> On the other hand, Jon Hicks of ''PC Format'' wrote that while some effects were excellent, the game's otherwise unspectacular graphics were unwelcome reminders of the game's console roots.<ref name="pc format-review">{{cite news|url=http://www.pcformat.co.uk/reviews/default.asp?pagetypeid=2&articleid=28625&subsectionid=680|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080206144725/http://www.pcformat.co.uk/reviews/default.asp?pagetypeid=2&articleid=28625&subsectionid=680|archive-date=February 6, 2008|title=Beyond Good and Evil|last=Hicks|first=Jon|year=2004|work=PC Format|access-date=May 3, 2010}}</ref> ''[[1UP.com]]'' and ''Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine'' cited glitches such as [[frame rate]] as irksome, because the game did not appear to tax the console's hardware.<ref name="1up-ps2 review">{{cite web|author=Staff |url=http://www.1up.com/reviews/beyond-good-evil_7 |title=Beyond Good and Evil (PS2) Reviews; Beyond good gameplay, with some really evil glitches |publisher=[[1UP.com]] |access-date=January 20, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160204085801/http://www.1up.com/reviews/beyond-good-evil_7 |archive-date=February 4, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ops2m-review">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.playstationmagazine.com/article2/0,4364,1372587,00.asp |title=Beyond Good and Evil (PS2) |last=Steinman |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031231232454/http://www.playstationmagazine.com/article2/0%2C4364%2C1372587%2C00.asp |archive-date=December 31, 2003 |first=Gary |date=November 4, 2003 |magazine=[[Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine]] |access-date=May 3, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

{{quote box| quoted=true |width = 35%| quote = From this day forth, Michel Ancel is no longer 'the creator of Rayman'. From now on, he is 'the genius that brought us ''Beyond Good & Evil''{{'}} [...] Cast out amongst a slew of Christmas blockbusters, ''BG&E'' rises above them all and leaves an indelible impression.| source = Tom Bramwell of ''[[Eurogamer]]''<ref name="eurogamer review">{{cite web|author=Bramwell, Tom|date=November 23, 2003|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/r_beyondgoodandevil_ps2|title=Beyond Good & Evil|publisher=[[Eurogamer]]|access-date=March 18, 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002061805/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/r_beyondgoodandevil_ps2|archive-date=October 2, 2012}}</ref>}}

''[[Edge (magazine)|Edge]]'' commended the game for its storytelling and design, but criticized its plot as unable to "match Jade's initial appeal," becoming "fairly mundane" without "the darkness and moral ambiguity suggested by the title", with Jade's [[everyman]] appeal undermined by the revelation of her "mysterious hidden identity". Dan Toose of ''[[Sydney Morning Herald|SMH]]'' called the game's setting "dark, baroque and earthy, a far cry from the squeaky-clean action of the ''[[Final Fantasy]]'' games," and described the game as "a very European take on the role-playing genre" and "one of the best adventure games in years".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2003/12/05/1070351782307.html|title=Die Hard|last=Toose|first=Dan|date=December 6, 2003|publisher=Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=March 19, 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105205705/http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2003/12/05/1070351782307.html|archive-date=November 5, 2012}}</ref> Star Dingo of ''[[GamePro]]'' commented that the game was a "[[jack of all trades, master of none]]" that "never really lives up to its title", adding that its vision could have been more focused.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamepro.com/article/reviews/31690/beyond-good-and-evil/|title=Beyond Good and Evil|last=Dingo|first=Star|date=November 12, 2003|publisher=[[GamePro]]|access-date=March 20, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091202052524/http://www.gamepro.com/article/reviews/31690/beyond-good-and-evil/|archive-date=December 2, 2009}}</ref> Among complaints were control issues and a lack of gameplay depth. ''Game Informer''{{'}}s Lisa Mason wrote that the game's controls were serviceable, but simplistic, and that she wished she could do more with the character.<ref name="gi-xbox review">{{cite web|url=http://www.gameinformer.com/NR/exeres/9456448C-E2A6-441C-A535-9DE82371A66B.htm?CS_pid=210427|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071214001648/http://www.gameinformer.com/NR/exeres/9456448C-E2A6-441C-A535-9DE82371A66B.htm?CS_pid=210427|archive-date=December 14, 2007|title=Beyond Good and Evil|last=Mason|first=Lisa|publisher=[[Game Informer]]|url-status=dead|access-date=May 3, 2010}}</ref> ''[[PC Gamer]]''{{'}}s Kevin Rice found most of the gameplay and its exploration refreshing, but called hovercraft races "not much fun" and felt combat was the game's weakest element.<ref name="pc gamer-review">{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080203035934/http://www.pcgamer.com/archives/2005/06/beyond_good_evi.html|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/archives/2005/06/beyond_good_evi.html |archive-date=February 3, 2008|title=PC Gamer: Beyond Good & Evil |first=Kevin|last=Rice|work=PC Gamer|access-date=April 29, 2010}}</ref> ''Edge'' called the gameplay interaction "hollowed out", as an unintended consequence of Ancel's attempt to streamline the game.<ref name="Edge"/>

=== Sales ===
''Beyond Good & Evil'' was not a commercial success. The game saw poor sales upon its release in the 2003 [[Christmas and holiday season]]. Retailers quickly decreased the price by up to 80&nbsp;percent. ''Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine'' staff attributed the poor sales of the game—among many other 2003 releases—to an over-saturated market, and labeled ''Beyond Good & Evil'' as a commercial "disappointment".<ref name="OPM-78">{{cite magazine| magazine = [[Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine]]| publisher = [[Ziff Davis]]| title = Spin: Bad Timing| issue = 78| pages = 30–31|date=March 2004}}</ref> In retrospect, Ancel noted that consumers at the time were interested in established franchises and technologically impressive games. Coupled with the number of "big titles" available, he stated that the market was a poor environment for ''Beyond Good & Evil'' and that it would take time to be appreciated.<ref name="Ubi-Uncensored"/> The ''Official U.S. PlayStation Magazine'' staff further commented that the lack of marketing from Ubisoft and the game's odd premise naturally reserved it to obscurity.<ref name="OPM-78"/> Part of the disappointing sales stemmed from Ubisoft not knowing how to market the title,<ref>{{cite web|author=IGN AU Staff|date=February 19, 2009|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2009/02/17/beyond-good-evil-2-what-to-expect|title=Beyond Good & Evil 2: What to Expect|page=1|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=May 8, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090220012314/http://xbox360.ign.com/articles/954/954480p1.html|archive-date=February 20, 2009}}</ref> something that Ubisoft North America CEO Laurent Detoc labeled as one of his worst business decisions.<ref name="Development">{{cite web|last=Detoc|first=Laurent|date=August 23, 2005 |title=Executive Profile |work=[[American City Business Journals|San Francisco Business Times]]|url=http://sanfrancisco.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/stories/2007/11/05/tidbits2.html |access-date=December 4, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091120185035/http://sanfrancisco.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/stories/2007/11/05/tidbits2.html|archive-date=November 20, 2009}}</ref> At the time, Ubisoft's marketing efforts were more focused on the release of ''[[Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time]]''.<ref name="OPM-78"/> Ubisoft's former North American vice-president of publishing, Jay Cohen, and its European managing director, Alaine Corre, attributed the commercial failure of the game to a lack of marketing. "The game play was there, the technical excellence was there but perhaps the [[target audience]] was not there," Corre told the [[BBC]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Feldman|first=Curt|date = May 11, 2004 |url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/qanda-ubisofts-jay-cohen/1100-6096617/ | title = Q&A: Ubisoft's Jay Cohen | work = [[GameSpot]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] | access-date =November 8, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071020015358/http://www.gamespot.com/news/6096617.html |archive-date=October 20, 2007}}</ref><ref name="bbc-innovation">{{cite news|last=Waters|first=Darren|date=June 14, 2004|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/technology/3798237.stm|title=Game firms urged to take risks|work=[[BBC]]|access-date=March 15, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051115174656/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/technology/3798237.stm|archive-date=November 15, 2005}}</ref> Corre later commented that the Xbox 360 release (in 2011) "did extremely well", but considered this success "too late" to make a difference in the game's poor sales.<ref name="Ubi-Uncensored"/> The game was intended to be the first part of a trilogy, but its poor sales placed those plans on hold at the time.<ref name="sequel">{{cite web |last=Bramwell |first=Tom|date=August 23, 2005|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/news230805bgne |title=It would be 'good to finish' BG&E&nbsp;— Michel Ancel |publisher=[[Eurogamer]] |access-date=December 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219120228/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/news230805bgne |archive-date=December 19, 2013}}</ref>

===Awards and legacy===
''Beyond Good & Evil'' was nominated for and won many gaming awards. The [[International Game Developers Association]] nominated the title for three honors at the 2004 [[Game Developers Choice Awards]]: "Game of the Year", "Original Game Character of the Year" (Jade) and "Excellence in Game Design".<ref>{{cite web|date=February 25, 2004|url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/game-platforms/igda-announces-nominees-more-award-winners|title=IGDA Announces Nomineses; More Award Winners|last=Jenkins|first=David|work=[[Gamasutra]]|publisher=[[UBM TechWeb]]|access-date=December 29, 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114040729/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/3485/IGDA_Announces_Nominees_More_Award_Winners.php|archive-date=November 14, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamedaily.com/games/beyond-good-and-evil/xbox/game-news/nominees-for-game-developers-choice-awards/139/5581/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20080906153906/http://www.gamedaily.com/games/beyond-good-and-evil/xbox/game-news/nominees-for-game-developers-choice-awards/139/5581/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 6, 2008|title=Nominees for Game Developers Choice Awards|last=Viscel|first=Mike|date=February 25, 2004|publisher=[[GameDaily]]|access-date=October 2, 2009}}</ref> Ubisoft titles garnered six of eleven awards at the 2004 IMAGINA Festival in France, with ''Beyond Good & Evil'' winning "Best Writer" and "Game of the Year Team Award".<ref name="imagina">{{cite web |title=Ubisoft Rewarded For Their Creativity At The Imagina Festival |url=http://www.gamezone.com/news/02_11_04_12_28PM.htm |publisher=GameZone |date=February 11, 2004 |access-date=October 2, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617033410/http://www.gamezone.com/news/item/ubisoft_rewarded_for_their_creativity_at_the_imagina_festival|archive-date=June 17, 2011}}</ref> In ''[[IGN]]''{{'}}s "The Best of 2003", the PlayStation 2 (PS2) version won "Best Adventure Game", while the GameCube version received "Best Story".<ref>{{cite web |title=IGN.com presents The Best of 2003 - Best Adventure Game (PS2) |url=http://bestof2003.ign.com/ps2.html |work=[[IGN]] |author=IGN Staff |access-date=2010-12-20|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080406001345/http://bestof2003.ign.com/ps2.html |archive-date = April 6, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IGN.com presents The Best of 2003 - Best Story (GC) |url=http://bestof2003.ign.com/gcn.html |work=[[IGN]] |author=IGN Staff |access-date=2010-12-20|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080220221755/http://bestof2003.ign.com/gcn.html |archive-date = February 20, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''Beyond Good & Evil''{{'}}s audio was also recognized. The game was nominated for the "Audio of the Year", "Music of the Year", "Best Interactive Score", and "Best Sound Design" awards at the second annual [[Game Audio Network Guild Awards|Game Audio Network Guild awards]].<ref name="GANGawards">{{cite web|url=http://www.music4games.net/n_gang_awards_2003_nominees.html|title=Game Audio Network Guild Announces 2nd Annual G.A.N.G Awards/Nominees |publisher=Music4Games|access-date=2010-03-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051217011555/http://www.music4games.net/n_gang_awards_2003_nominees.html| archive-date=2005-12-17}}</ref> During the [[7th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards]], the [[Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences]] nominated the game for outstanding achievement in "[[D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Animation|Animation]]", "[[D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Story|Character or Story Development]]", "[[D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Original Music Composition|Original Music Composition]]", and "[[D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Audio Design|Sound Design]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.interactive.org/games/video_game_details.asp?idAward=2004&idGame=321 |title=D.I.C.E. Awards By Video Game Details Beyond Good & Evil |publisher=[[Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences]] |website=interactive.org |access-date=27 July 2023}}</ref> At the 3rd Annual National Academy of Video Game Trade Reviewers Awards, the game was nominated for the following categories: "Game Design"; "Original Adventure Game"; "Control Design", winning 2 ("Game Design" and "Original Adventure Game").

In 2007, ''Beyond Good & Evil'' was named 22nd-best Xbox game and 12th-best GameCube game of all time by ''IGN''.<ref name="22nd">{{cite web | last1=Perry|first1=Douglass C.|last2=Brudvig|first2=Erik|last3=Miller|first3=Jonathan | date=March 16, 2007 | url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2007/03/17/the-top-25-xbox-games-of-all-time | title=The Top 25 Xbox Games of All Time GameCube Games" list.<ref name="GI-189">{{cite magazine| magazine = [[Game Informer]]| publisher = GameStop| title = Classic GI: Top 25 GameCube Games| page = 85| issue = 189|date=January 2009}}</ref> ==Legacy==
===Sequel or prequel===
Ancel stated his desire to produce a sequel to the game.<ref name="sequel"/> Ubisoft announced at the Ubidays [[2008 in video gaming|2008]] opening conference that there would be a second game.<ref name="GI-184">{{cite magazine| magazine = [[Game Informer]]| publisher = GameStop| title = Connect: Going Beyond Good & Evil| page = 20| issue = 184|date=August 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Ransom-Wiley | first=James | title=Beyond Good & Evil 2 revealed at Ubidays 2008| publisher=Joystiq | url=http://www.joystiq.com/2008/05/28/beyond-good-and-evil-2-revealed-at-ubidays-2008/ | date=May 28, 2008 | access-date=January 10, 2007 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080529043932/http://www.joystiq.com/2008/05/28/beyond-good-and-evil-2-revealed-at-ubidays-2008/ | archive-date=May 29, 2008}}</ref> A sequel, tentatively titled ''[[Beyond Good and Evil 2]]'', is currently in development,<ref name="GI-184"/> although the project was temporarily halted to focus on ''[[Rayman Origins]]''.<ref name="Ubi-Uncensored"/> Michel Ancel has hinted that Jade would have a new look for the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/beyond-good-and-evil-2-director-teases-new-look-for-jade/1100-6418998/|title=Beyond Good and Evil 2 director teases new look for Jade|last=Hindes|first=Daniel|date=April 14, 2014|work=GameSpot|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=June 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140415073157/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/beyond-good-and-evil-2-director-teases-new-look-for-jade/1100-6418998/|archive-date=April 15, 2014}}</ref> In early 2016, [[Destructoid]] published a rumor that the game was being funded by Nintendo as an exclusive to their upcoming console codenamed "NX" (later officially unveiled as the [[Nintendo Switch]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.destructoid.com/rumor-nintendo-funding-beyond-good-and-evil-sequel-346059.phtml|title=Rumor: Nintendo funding Beyond Good and Evil sequel|date=March 3, 2016|access-date=June 17, 2017|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304094843/http://www.destructoid.com/rumor-nintendo-funding-beyond-good-and-evil-sequel-346059.phtml|url-status=live}}</ref> On September 27, 2016, Michel Ancel posted an image to Instagram with the caption "Somewhere in system 4 ... - Thanks #ubisoft for making this possible !". On October 4, Ancel stated that ''Beyond Good and Evil 2'' was in pre-production. Ubisoft confirmed Ancel's claim on October 6, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-10-04-beyond-good-and-evil-2-is-almost-definitely-in-development-but|title=Beyond Good & Evil 2 is almost definitely in development|last=Matulef|first=Jeffrey|date=2016-10-06|website=Eurogamer|language=en-UK|access-date=2016-10-13|archive-date=2016-10-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013215929/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-10-04-beyond-good-and-evil-2-is-almost-definitely-in-development-but|url-status=live}}</ref> Ubisoft showed the first new trailer for ''Beyond Good and Evil 2'' during their [[E3 2017]] conference and was announced as a prequel to the first game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hussain |first1=Tamoor |last2=Knezevic |first2=Kevin |date=12 June 2017 |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/e3-2017-beyond-good-and-evil-2-trailer-finally-sho/1100-6450825/ |title=E3 2017: Beyond Good & Evil 2 Trailer Finally Shown |website=[[GameSpot]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=12 June 2017}}</ref> During E3 2017, Ancel confirmed that the 2008 and 2009 trailers were from initial work as a narrative sequel to ''Beyond Good & Evil'', but during development they opted to change direction and make it a prequel, and thus the work previously shown was from an effectively different game.<ref name="verge e317">{{cite web | url = https://www.theverge.com/2017/6/14/15801280/beyond-good-evil-2-preview-michel-ancel-interview-e3-2017 | title = Beyond Good & Evil 2 is wildly ambitious, but it's still at 'day zero' of development | first = Andrew | last = Webster | date = 14 June 2017 | access-date = 14 June 2017 | work = [[The Verge]] | publisher = [[Vox Media]] | archive-date = 15 June 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170615031743/https://www.theverge.com/2017/6/14/15801280/beyond-good-evil-2-preview-michel-ancel-interview-e3-2017 | url-status = live }}</ref> There had been rumors that it would have been released as a timed exclusive for the Nintendo Switch in the prior year,<ref>{{cite web |last=Kate Date |first=Laura |date=3 March 2016 |url=https://www.destructoid.com/rumor-nintendo-funding-beyond-good-and-evil-sequel-346059.phtml |title=Rumor: Nintendo funding Beyond Good and Evil sequel |website=[[Destructoid]] |access-date=3 March 2016 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304094843/http://www.destructoid.com/rumor-nintendo-funding-beyond-good-and-evil-sequel-346059.phtml |url-status=live }}</ref> but Ancel confirmed this was not the case. The "Space Monkey Program" lists the game for [[Microsoft Windows]], [[PlayStation 4]] and [[Xbox One]], however Michel Ancel stated that the platforms have not been announced yet, and that the listing was due to a bug.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.vg247.com/2017/06/14/beyond-good-and-evil-2-switch-timed-exclusive-rumours-squashed-platforms-confirmed-by-space-monkey-program/ | title = Beyond Good and Evil 2 Switch timed-exclusive rumors squashed, platforms confirmed by Space Monkey Program | first = Shabana | last = Arif | date = 14 June 2017 | access-date = 14 June 2017 | work = [[VG247]] | archive-date = 14 June 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170614220539/http://www.vg247.com/2017/06/14/beyond-good-and-evil-2-switch-timed-exclusive-rumours-squashed-platforms-confirmed-by-space-monkey-program/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Ancel later told ''Kotaku'' that the game is designed to run on many platforms.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://kotaku.com/what-beyond-good-evil-2-is-now-and-what-its-creators-1796116469|title=What Beyond Good & Evil 2 Is Now, And What Its Creators Dream It Can Be|last=Totilo|first=Stephen|date=14 June 2017|work=[[Kotaku]]|publisher=[[Gizmodo Media Group]]|access-date=24 January 2023|archive-date=28 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628065638/http://kotaku.com/what-beyond-good-evil-2-is-now-and-what-its-creators-1796116469|url-status=live}}</ref>

When Ancel announced his departure from Ubisoft in September 2020, he stated that both the project and ''[[Wild (video game)|Wild]]'' were in capable hands.<ref>{{cite web |last=Phillips |first=Tom |title=''Rayman'' creator Michel Ancel quits video games to work on wildlife sanctuary |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2020-09-18-rayman-creator-michel-ancel-quits-video-games-industry-to-work-on-wildlife-sanctuary |website=[[Eurogamer]] |date=September 18, 2020 |access-date=September 19, 2020 |archive-date=September 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919081232/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2020-09-18-rayman-creator-michel-ancel-quits-video-games-industry-to-work-on-wildlife-sanctuary |url-status=live }}</ref> The French newspaper ''[[Libération]]'', which have been following on Ubisoft's troubles with [[Ubisoft#2020 sexual misconduct accusations and dismissals|mid-2020 series of sexual misconduct allegations]] raised against many high-level members of the company, learned that members of Ancel's team found Ancel's leadership on the project to be unorganized and at times abusive, causing the game's development to have many restarts and accounting for the delay since its 2010 announcement. The Montpellier team had reported these concerns to leadership of Ubisoft as early as 2017 but Ancel's close relationship with Yves Guillemot prevented any major corrections to occur until the 2020 internal evaluations that led to Ancel's departure.<ref>{{cite web |last=Olson |first=Mathew |date=September 25, 2020 |title=Report: Michel Ancel Accused of Abusive, Disruptive Practices on ''Beyond Good & Evil 2'' |url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/report-michel-ancel-beyond-good-and-evil-2-abuse-mismanagement-liberation |access-date=September 25, 2020 |work=[[USGamer]] |archive-date=November 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201121154933/https://www.usgamer.net/articles/report-michel-ancel-beyond-good-and-evil-2-abuse-mismanagement-liberation |url-status=live }}</ref> Ubisoft stated that Ancel "hasn't been directly involved in ''BG&E2'' for some time now" when he left the company.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chalk |first=Andy |date=18 September 2020 |title=''Beyond Good & Evil'' creator Michel Ancel quits videogames to work in an animal sanctuary |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/beyond-good-and-evil-creator-michel-ancel-quits-videogames-to-work-in-an-animal-sanctuary/ |website=[[PC Gamer]] |access-date=24 January 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220611150430/https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/beyond-good-and-evil-creator-michel-ancel-quits-videogames-to-work-in-an-animal-sanctuary/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In July 2021, Ubisoft stated in a financial report that development was "progressing well" but did not answer a question about its release date.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ubisoft confirms ''Beyond Good & Evil 2'' is still in development |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/uk/ubisoft-confirms-beyond-good-and-evil-2-still-in-development/ |website=[[GamesRadar+]] |first=Jordan |last=Gerblick |date=20 July 2021 |access-date=24 January 2023 |archive-date=1 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211201150639/https://www.gamesradar.com/uk/ubisoft-confirms-beyond-good-and-evil-2-still-in-development/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On February 9, 2022, ''[[Bloomberg News]]'' reported that the sequel "remains in pre-production after at least five years of development".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-02-09/ubisoft-plans-new-assassin-s-creed-game-to-help-fill-schedule?srnd=technology-vp|title=Ubisoft Plans New Assassin's Creed Game to Help Fill Its Schedule|last=Schreier|first=Jason|date=2022-02-09|website=Bloomberg|language=en-US|access-date=2022-03-01|archive-date=2022-03-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220301163941/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-02-09/ubisoft-plans-new-assassin-s-creed-game-to-help-fill-schedule?srnd=technology-vp|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2022, the prequel broke the record held by ''[[Duke Nukem Forever]]'' (2011) for the longest development for a video game, at more than 15 years.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wolens |first=Joshua |date=October 3, 2022 |title=''Beyond Good and Evil 2'' has broken ''Duke Nukem Forever''{{'}}s record for longest game development time |language=en |work=[[PC Gamer]] |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/beyond-good-and-evil-2-has-broken-duke-nukem-forevers-record-for-longest-game-development-time/ |access-date=October 4, 2022 |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004183755/https://www.pcgamer.com/beyond-good-and-evil-2-has-broken-duke-nukem-forevers-record-for-longest-game-development-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Other media===
In late July 2020, streaming service company [[Netflix]] announced a [[live-action animated film]] adaptation based on the video game is in development with ''[[Detective Pikachu (film)|Detective Pikachu]]'' director [[Rob Letterman]].<ref>{{Cite web|title='Detective Pikachu' Director and Netflix Tackling 'Beyond Good & Evil' Adaptation (Exclusive)|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/detective-pikachu-director-netflix-tackling-ubisofts-beyond-good-evil-film-adaptation-1305407|website=The Hollywood Reporter|date=31 July 2020|language=en|access-date=31 July 2020|archive-date=30 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210330014445/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/detective-pikachu-director-netflix-tackling-ubisofts-beyond-good-evil-film-adaptation-1305407|url-status=live}}</ref> No further updates have been given for the film since the announcement.

Jade and Pey'j appear as characters in the 2023 Netflix animated series ''[[Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix]]'', voiced by Courtney Mae-Briggs and [[Glenn Wrage]] respectively. In the series, they are depicted as captive rebels and love interests who are recruited into a team led by the eponymous character.<ref name="Cast 02">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/captain-laserhawk-a-blood-dragon-remix-gets-official-release-date-new-cast-members|title=Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix Gets Official Release Date, New Cast Members|last=Bankhurst|first=Adam|publisher=[[IGN]]|date=September 27, 2023|access-date=September 27, 2023}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Control (video game)

'''''Control''''' is a 2019 [[action-adventure game]] developed by [[Remedy Entertainment]]. It follows [[Jesse Faden]], the new Director of the Federal Bureau of Control (FBC), a [[List of fictional secret police and intelligence organizations|secret U.S. government agency]] that investigates and contains phenomena that violate the normal laws of reality. As Jesse, the player explores the Oldest House–the FBC's headquarters–and uses paranormal abilities and a shapeshifting gun known as the "Service Weapon" to combat the Hiss, a hostile, otherworldly entity that has invaded and corrupted the FBC. Players unlock new powers by locating Objects of Power, mundane objects imbued with energies from another dimension. The Oldest House has four sectors that can be explored at a nonlinear pace, and players are free to complete side quests and explore hidden areas.

''Control'' was completed within three years with a €30 million budget. Its gameplay is significantly more open than Remedy's past games; the developers drew inspiration from [[role-playing game|role-playing]] and [[Metroidvania]] games. The game was written by [[Sam Lake]] and was inspired by paranormal stories about the fictional [[SCP Foundation]], based on the [[new weird]] genre. To demonstrate the game's [[destructible environment]]al systems, the Oldest House is designed in the [[brutalist architecture|brutalist]] style common in [[Cold War|Cold-War-era]] government buildings. The game's voice cast includes [[Courtney Hope]] as Faden, and [[James McCaffrey (actor)|James McCaffrey]], [[Matthew Porretta]], and [[Martti Suosalo]]. The music was composed by Petri Alanko and [[Martin Stig Andersen]]. ''Control'' uses Remedy's in-house [[Northlight Engine]] and was among the first games to use [[real-time ray tracing]] built [[Ray-tracing hardware|into the hardware]] of modern [[video card]]s.

[[505 Games]] published ''Control'' for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox One]] in August 2019 and for the [[PlayStation 5]] and [[Xbox Series X and Series S|Xbox Series X/S]] in February 2021. Remedy Entertainment began self-publishing the game in 2025. ''Control'' received generally positive reviews; critics praised its setting, art direction, gameplay, and characters, although its main story received mixed responses. The game sold over 6 million units by March 2026, and was nominated for several end-of-year accolades, including [[List of Game of the Year awards|Game of the Year]] at [[The Game Awards 2019]] and the [[23rd Annual D.I.C.E. Awards]]. Two [[expansion pack]]s were released, the second of which, ''AWE'', being a crossover between ''Control'' and ''[[Alan Wake]]'', forming part of a [[shared universe]] named the "Remedy Connected Universe". A sequel, ''[[Control Resonant]]'', was released in 2026, and a [[multiplayer]] spin-off, ''[[FBC: Firebreak]]'', was released in 2025.

==Gameplay==
[[File:Control gameplay screenshot.jpg|thumb|left|Jesse gains psychokinetic powers, such as [[Levitation (physics) |levitation]], over the course of the game. She is also armed with a "Service Weapon", a shapeshifting gun.]]

''Control'' is an [[action-adventure]] video game that is played from a [[third-person perspective]]. The player assumes control of [[Jesse Faden]], who is searching for her missing brother, as she arrives at the Oldest House, a featureless Brutalist skyscraper in [[New York City]] that houses the headquarters of the fictional Federal Bureau of Control (FBC). Most enemies in ''Control'' are human FBC agents who are possessed by the Hiss, an otherworldly force that is attempting to cross through a dimensional barrier into this reality. Enemies range from firearm-carrying humans to heavily mutated variants with superpowers.<ref name="differ"/>

To combat these threats, Jesse is equipped with the "Service Weapon", a modular firearm that can shapeshift into five forms: Grip, Spin, Shatter, Pierce, Charge, and Surge.<ref name="service weapon1"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/control/control-gun-service-weapon |title=In Control, your gun is basically Excalibur |first=Julian |last=Benson |work=[[PCGamesN]] |date=June 13, 2018 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=14 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614053307/https://www.pcgamesn.com/control/control-gun-service-weapon |url-status=live}}</ref> Each form has unique gameplay properties, ranging from a close-range, shotgun-like blast to a long-range, sniper-like form.<ref name="service weapon1">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/07/19/control-every-weapon-form-explained-ign-first |title=Control: Every Weapon Form Explained - IGN First |first=Joe |last=Skrebels |work=[[IGN]] |date=July 20, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811175722/https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/07/19/control-every-weapon-form-explained-ign-first |url-status=live}}</ref> Players can equip and swap between two weapon forms at any given time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/i-didnt-love-remedys-control-but-i-am-in-love-with-its-transforming-gun/ |title=I didn't love Remedy's Control, but I am in love with its transforming gun |first=Wes |last=Fenlon |work=[[PC Gamer]] |date=March 26, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2026}}</ref> Jesse also interacts with Objects of Power to gain psychokinetic abilities. These abilities include "Launch", which allows her to telekinetically hurl objects from the environment as projectiles at enemies; "Evade", a quick dash to avoid attacks; "Shield", which pulls rubble from the ground to block incoming attacks; "Seize", used to briefly turn enemies into allies; and "Levitate", which enables Jesse to fly.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/control-objects-of-power/ |title=Control Objects of Power and how to unlock every ability |first=Jordan |last=Oloman |work=[[GamesRadar]] |date=March 14, 2024 |accessdate=January 24, 2026}}</ref> Outside of combat and transportation, the powers are essential for solving environmental puzzles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/after-an-hour-of-playing-it-control-seems-extraordinary |title=After an hour playing it, Control seems extraordinary |first=Chris |last=Tapsell |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=June 13, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2026}}</ref> Three of the five base powers are optional, and may only be obtained through exploration or completion of  side quests.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/control-abilities-mods-skill-tree-levitate/ |title=Control abilities: how to get and master them all |first=Dave |last=Meikleham |date=September 6, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=4 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251204211823/https://www.pcgamer.com/control-abilities-mods-skill-tree-levitate/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The use of the Service Weapon and Jesse's psychokinetic powers is governed by two cooldown systems, allowing players to alternate between these combat options.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2019/08/review-control-is-remedys-best-game-yet-and-a-ray-tracing-masterpiece/ |title=Review: Control is Remedy's best game yet—and a ray tracing masterpiece |first=Sam |last=Machkovech |work=[[Ars Technica]] |date=August 26, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=6 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106132103/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2019/08/review-control-is-remedys-best-game-yet-and-a-ray-tracing-masterpiece/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The game lacks a traditional [[cover system]]; players must remain mobile because defeated enemies drop [[health (gaming) |health]] that is necessary for Jesse's survival.<ref name="sense of place">{{cite web |url=https://www.redbull.com/ca-en/control-tips-guide |title=Master Control with these expert tips from the game's designer |first=Bex |last=April May |work=[[Red Bull]] |date=April 20, 2020 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=2 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502031706/https://www.redbull.com/ca-en/control-tips-guide |url-status=live}}</ref>

The Oldest House has an interior far larger than its exterior; the building is an enormous, constantly shifting supernatural realm that defies the laws of physics. ''Control'' is built in the [[Metroidvania]] format; the Oldest House has four sectors that can be explored at a nonlinear pace.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/control-guide/2019/8/29/20837459/hidden-location-discovered-sector-executive-maintenance-research-containment-ability-point/ |title=Control guide: All Hidden Locations |first=Jeff |last=Ramos |work=[[Polygon (website) |Polygon]] |date=October 4, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=3 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250503164805/https://www.polygon.com/control-guide/2019/8/29/20837459/hidden-location-discovered-sector-executive-maintenance-research-containment-ability-point |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="differ"/> Throughout the building, players encounter Control Points, which are unlocked by clearing enemies and serve as hubs for [[fast travel]], skill upgrades, weapon modifications, and outfit changes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pushsquare.com/guides/control-tips-and-tricks-for-beginners |title=Control - Tips and Tricks for Beginners |first=Liam |last=Croft |date=June 28, 2021 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |work=[[Push Square]] |archive-date=13 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240913214842/https://www.pushsquare.com/guides/control-tips-and-tricks-for-beginners |url-status=live}}</ref> Reaching a Control Point will heal Jesse without resetting the level.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/control-tips/ |title=10 Control tips to master your journey through the Oldest House |first=Jordan |last=Oloman |work=[[GamesRadar]] |date=March 14, 2024 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=3 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403030742/https://www.gamesradar.com/control-tips/ |url-status=live}}</ref> As players progress, Jesse's security-clearance level will increase and players will gain new skills, allowing them to access previously locked rooms or reach hidden areas.<ref name="differ"/> The game's campaign is divided into 10 acts that are supplemented with 18 side quests.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/control-length-how-long-takes-beat-main-campaign-many-missions-7045 |title=Control length: How long it takes to beat the main campaign and how many missions there are |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250310231609/https://www.eurogamer.net/control-length-how-long-takes-beat-main-campaign-many-missions-7045 |url-status=live}}</ref> There are also "Board |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710044803/https://www.pcgamer.com/control-tips-guide/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and timed challenges named "Bureau Alerts".<ref name="BA">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/07/31/control-your-questions-answered-by-the-developers-a-ign-first |title=Control: Your Questions Answered by the Developers – IGN First |first=Joe |last=Skrebels |work=[[IGN]] |date=August 1, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=12 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112220423/https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/07/31/control-your-questions-answered-by-the-developers-a-ign-first |url-status=live}}</ref> The Oldest House is filled with hidden documents, audio recordings, [[full-motion video]] (FMV) and television shows that provide context about the game's world and its backstory.<ref name="sense of place"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/07/10/control-is-smart-savage-and-batst-crazy-ign-first |title=Control Is Smart, Savage and Bats**t Crazy - IGN First |first=Joe |last=Skrebels |work=[[IGN]] |date=July 16, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=4 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240304123450/https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/07/10/control-is-smart-savage-and-batst-crazy-ign-first |url-status=live}}</ref> An [[artificial intelligence]] (AI) system known as the Encounter Director controls interactions with enemies based on the player's level and their location in the Oldest House.<ref name="differ">{{cite magazine |last1=Favis |first1=Elise |title=How Control's Gameplay Differs From Past Remedy Games |url=https://gameinformer.com/2019/03/11/how-controls-gameplay-differs-from-past-remedy-games |magazine=Game
