Players can further strengthen the Service Weapon and Jesse's [[stats (RPG)|attribute]]s by equipping mods, with a maximum of three Weapon and three Personal mods allowed at once. Players can also craft their own mods through the Astral Construct system using materials and Source Energy, the latter of which is collected through killing the Hiss or decommissioning unwanted mods. Mods are divided into levels of rarity; more-rare mods offer greater power but require more resources to produce.<ref name="astral construct">{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/control-weapon-mods-personal-mods-astral-constructs-6043 |title=Control - Weapon Mods and Personal Mods, including Astral Constructs explained |first=Lottie |last=Lyn |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=February 1, 2021 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=16 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416002438/https://www.eurogamer.net/control-weapon-mods-personal-mods-astral-constructs-6043 |url-status=live}}</ref> Source Energy is essential for upgrading the forms of the Service Weapons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/control-unlocking-upgrading-service-weapon-forms-6043 |title=Control - Weapon Forms list, how to unlock and upgrade Special Weapon Forms |first=Lottie |last=Lyn |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=February 1, 2021 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=12 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250612152056/https://www.eurogamer.net/control-unlocking-upgrading-service-weapon-forms-6043 |url-status=live}}</ref> Completion of quests rewards players with Ability Points, which can be spent to upgrade Jesse's psychokinetic powers, increasing its damage, adjust its properties, and widen its use. They can also increase Jesse's maximum health, Energy, which dictates how frequently she can use her powers, and the strength of her melee attacks. Spending sufficient Ability Points grants players additional Milestone Rewards, which typically unlock additional mod slots for further customization.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/control-upgrading-abilities-milestone-rewards-ability-points-6043 |title=Control - Upgrading Abilities explained, including Milestone Rewards and Ability Points |first=Lottie |last=Lynn |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=February 1, 2021 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=17 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250417162307/https://www.eurogamer.net/control-upgrading-abilities-milestone-rewards-ability-points-6043 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Synopsis==
===Setting===
''Control'' revolves around the Federal Bureau of Control (FBC), a clandestine U.S. government agency that investigates supernatural Altered World Events (AWEs). These AWEs affect the human [[collective unconscious]] and have "paranatural" effects, including manipulating reality through extradimensional spaces called Thresholds, and the creation of archetypal but powerful items called Objects of Power. Objects of Power are connected to the Board, a black, pyramid-shaped entity that exists within the [[Astral Plane]], an alternate dimension. The individual chosen by the Board to wield the Service Weapon, an Object of Power, is considered by default to be the director of the FBC.<ref name="vice mythos">{{cite web |url = https://www.vice.com/en/article/control-the-board-pyramid/ |title = The Mysterious "Board" in 'Control' Is One of the Game's Best, Most Unsettling Ideas |first = Cameron |last=Kunzelman |date=4 September 2019 |access-date=4 September 2019 |work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |archive-date=4 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904181339/https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/j5ypj3/control-the-board-pyramid |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Control'' takes place within the Oldest House, a [[Brutalist]] skyscraper in New York City that houses the headquarters of the FBC. The Oldest House is a Place of Power with several paranatural characteristics: it resists being noticed by anyone other than FBC members and individuals with an innate sensitivity to the paranatural, its interior is larger than its exterior, and its internal architecture is prone to shifting and rearranging in unpredictable ways. The FBC can stabilize portions of the Oldest House for its use by harnessing nexuses of resonance called Control Points.

The protagonist of ''Control'' is Jesse Faden ([[Courtney Hope]]), whom the Board has chosen as the director of the FBC to replace the recently deceased Zachariah Trench ([[James McCaffrey (actor)|James McCaffrey]]). Seventeen years prior, Jesse and her younger brother Dylan (Sean Durrie) were involved in an Altered World Event in their hometown of Ordinary, Maine. After discovering an Object of Power in the form of a slide projector, the two children accidentally unleashed paranatural forces that caused Ordinary's adult population to vanish. Jesse and Dylan were rescued by Polaris, a mysterious telepathic entity. Shortly thereafter, the FBC arrived in Ordinary, capturing Dylan and the slide projector, while Jesse fled with Polaris. In the present day, Jesse arrives at the Oldest House seeking her brother.

Other notable characters in ''Control'' include missing Head of Research Dr. Casper Darling ([[Matthew Porretta]]), research specialist Emily Pope ([[Antonia Bernath]]), security chief Simon Arish (Ronan Summers), Head of Operations Helen Marshall ([[Jade Anouka]]), Panopticon supervisor Frederick Langston (Derek Hagen), and a mysterious Finnish janitor named Ahti ([[Martti Suosalo]]).

===Plot===
In October 2019,<ref name="game date">{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/23942363/alan-wake-2-biggest-twist-analysis-control-2-theories |title =Alan Wake 2's biggest twist has huge implications for future Remedy games |first=Toussaint |last=Egan |date=2 November 2023 |accessdate=12 November 2023 |work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |archive-date=12 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231112220133/https://www.polygon.com/23942363/alan-wake-2-biggest-twist-analysis-control-2-theories |url-status=live }}</ref> after receiving a telepathic message from Polaris, Jesse Faden arrives at the Oldest House in search of her kidnapped brother Dylan. Inside the building, Jesse discovers Trench's deceased corpse and Polaris instructs her to pick up his fallen Service Weapon. The weapon translocates Jesse to the Astral Plane, where the Board appoints her the new director of the FBC as Trench's replacement. Exiting Trench's office, Jesse is attacked by FBC agents possessed by an entity she dubs "the Hiss". Jesse learns the Oldest House is under emergency lockdown following the Hiss's spread, and that the Hiss has possessed everyone in the building except those wearing Hedron Resonance Amplifiers (HRAs), devices built by missing Bureau scientist Dr. Casper Darling. Jesse agrees to help the surviving agents reclaim the building and contain the Hiss in exchange for information on Dylan's whereabouts.

Using an Object of Power known as the Hotline, Jesse communicates with the deceased Trench and learns his former management team knows the secrets of the Bureau. After lifting the building's lockdown in the Maintenance Sector, Jesse enters the Research Sector in search of Helen Marshall, one of Trench's management team, whom she helps secure the production of more HRAs by reactivating Dr. Darling's HRA machine and later retrieving Black Rock Prisms from the Quarry. Marshall reveals Dylan, known to the Bureau as Prime Candidate 6 (P6), was being groomed to succeed Trench as the Bureau's director due to his immense supernatural abilities. After killing several Bureau agents, however, Dylan was deemed too dangerous and locked in the Containment Sector. Jesse rushes to the sector to find Dylan, only to learn he has escaped and surrendered to the Bureau in the Executive Sector. Dylan reveals to Jesse he has embraced the Hiss, and that the Hiss infiltrated the Oldest House through the slide projector, an Object of Power the Bureau recovered from Ordinary.

Searching for the projector in the Containment Sector, Jesse discovers the Bureau had been conducting experiments to recreate the AWE in Ordinary, while tracking her whereabouts as a potential candidate for Director of the Bureau. After finding the projector had been moved by Dr. Darling to Dimensional Research, she seeks the aid of Ahti, a paranatural entity who manifests as the Oldest House's janitor, and he gifts Jesse a cassette player that enables her to navigate an elaborate and shape-shifting maze protecting the projector's location. At Dimensional Research, Jesse discovers the power source of the HRAs to be an enormous, hexagonal entity dubbed Hedron by Trench and Dr. Darling after they discovered it in an alternate dimension known as Slidescape-36 via the projector. Jesse recognizes it as Polaris but her attempts to free it inadvertently invites Hiss attacks that destroy Hedron. With Polaris defeated, Jesse's mind is invaded by the Hiss, where she learns Trench too had been possessed by the Hiss during expeditions to Slidescape-36 and manipulated into releasing it onto the Oldest House. Discovering parts of Polaris still remained in her being, Jesse successfully repels the Hiss and chases down Dylan, who attempts to enter the Astral Plane through the slide projector and overtake the Board. She deactivates the slide projector and seemingly cleanses the Hiss from Dylan, closing the portal but leaving Dylan in a coma. In the aftermath, the Oldest House remains infested by the Hiss and under lockdown to prevent its escape, but Jesse has come to terms with her new role as director and decides to find a solution with the FBC's surviving personnel.

==Development==
[[File:Control_rtx_example.jpg|thumb|''Control'' was one of the first games to support graphics cards with real-time [[Ray tracing (graphics)|ray tracing]]. Here, the bottom image, with ray-tracing enabled, shows reflections of light and other surfaces in the marble floor, compared to the more traditionally rendered version shown on top.]]

''Control'' was developed by Finnish studio [[Remedy Entertainment]] as its first major release since its 2017 [[initial public offering]] (IPO) and separation from [[Microsoft]] as a publishing partner. ''Control'' was developed using more efficient development strategies to reduce costs and development time. The game was completed within three years with a €30 million budget, a lower cost than that for a typical [[triple A (video gaming) |triple-A]] game.<ref name="gi.biz people 2019">{{cite web |url=http://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2019-12-04-people-of-the-year-2019-remedy-entertainment |title=People of the Year 2019: Remedy Entertainment |first=Matthew |last=Handrahan |date=4 December 2019 |access-date=4 December 2019 |work=[[GamesIndustry.biz]] |archive-date=4 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191204183115/http://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2019-12-04-people-of-the-year-2019-remedy-entertainment |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Control'' was directed by Mikael Kasurinen, who worked on ''Alan Wake'' as lead gameplay designer and ''[[Quantum Break]]'' as lead director; and [[Sam Lake]] was the writer and creative director. Lake created the game's story and characters during the pre-production stage, and narrative lead Anna Megill developed its content.<ref name="ExCalibur"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://venturebeat.com/2017/07/05/remedys-sam-lake-on-21-years-of-game-storytelling-and-transmedia/ |title=Remedy's Sam Lake on 21 years of game storytelling and transmedia |first=Dean |last=Takahashi |work=[[VentureBeat]] |date=5 July 2017 |access-date=13 June 2018 |archive-date=13 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613112016/https://venturebeat.com/2017/07/05/remedys-sam-lake-on-21-years-of-game-storytelling-and-transmedia/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/e3-2018/2018/06/11/remedy-announces-gravity-bending-shooter-control |title=Remedy Announces Gravity-Bending Shooter, Control |first=Brian |last=Shea |magazine=[[Game Informer]] |date=11 June 2018 |access-date=13 June 2018 |archive-date=13 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613180243/https://www.gameinformer.com/index.php/e3-2018/2018/06/11/remedy-announces-gravity-bending-shooter-control |url-status=live}}</ref>

''Control'' was developed using Remedy's proprietary Northlight Engine, which was first used on its previous game, ''Quantum Break''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.redbull.com/se-en/control-interview |title=How Remedy are shaping their future with Control |first=Damien |last=McFerren |work=[[Red Bull]] |date=March 25, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=29 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240429080754/https://www.redbull.com/se-en/control-interview |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Control'' was one of the first major games to be released after the introduction of [[graphics card]]s that support real-time [[ray tracing (graphics)|ray-tracing]] through [[DirectX Raytracing]], and was the first major game with a nearly full implementation of all available [[Nvidia RTX]] features and support for Nvidia's [[DLSS]] for resolution upscaling on supported graphics cards.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/control-is-the-best-most-complex-implementation-of-ray-tracing-in-a-game-so-far/ |title=Control is the best, most complex implementation of ray tracing in a game so far |first=Jarred |last=Walton |date=30 August 2019 |access-date=30 August 2019 |work=[[PC Gamer]] |archive-date=30 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830230413/https://www.pcgamer.com/control-is-the-best-most-complex-implementation-of-ray-tracing-in-a-game-so-far/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Gameplay===
Gameplay was one of Remedy's development priorities for ''Control''.<ref name="ExCalibur">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/remedys-sam-lake-opens-up-about-having-the-freedom/1100-6459988/ |title=Remedy's Sam Lake Opens Up About Having The Freedom To Be Weird Again |first=Peter |last=Brown |work=[[GameSpot]] |date=June 22, 2018 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=13 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113100636/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/remedys-sam-lake-opens-up-about-having-the-freedom/1100-6459988/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Whereas earlier Remedy games explore supernatural themes, ''Control'' is the first game in which the protagonist wields supernatural powers. The powers were designed to be easily recognizable and grounded in reality; the developers avoided adding magical abilities that would feel outlandish in the game's setting.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gameinformer.com/2019/03/08/a-look-at-every-supernatural-ability-in-remedys-control |title=A Look At Every Supernatural Ability In Remedy's Control |first=Brian |last=Shea |work=[[Game Informer]] |date=March 8, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=27 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327060054/https://www.gameinformer.com/2019/03/08/a-look-at-every-supernatural-ability-in-remedys-control |url-status=live}}</ref> The telekinetic powers were designed to feel intuitive: players do not need to manually target the environment to pick up objects, and grabbed objects can be hurled to deliver devastating damage. To achieve this, Remedy replaced the [[Havok (software)|Havok]] physics in Northlight with [[PhysX]].<ref name="pcgpreview"/><ref name="vgc masurinen">{{cite web |url=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/features/the-best-game-ive-ever-made-how-remedy-made-control/ |title='The Best Game I've Ever Made': How Remedy Made Control |first=Andy |last=Robinson |date=27 August 2019 |access-date=3 September 2019 |work=[[Video Games Chronicle]] |archive-date=29 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829075612/https://www.videogameschronicle.com/features/the-best-game-ive-ever-made-how-remedy-made-control/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

The abilities and the Service Weapon are designed to complement each other in combat. One resource slowly recharges while the other is in use, encouraging players to strategically switch between them. The Service Weapon was designed as a highly capable tool for dispatching enemies. The [[artificial intelligence]] (AI) of the enemies in the game was designed to be aggressive, forcing players to use all of the skills in their toolset.<ref name="service weapon">{{cite web |url=https://gameinformer.com/video-feature/2019/03/13/remedys-control-only-has-one-gun-heres-why-its-awesome |title=Remedy's Control Only Has One Gun. Here's Why It's Awesome |work=[[Game Informer]] |date=March 13, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=27 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327055429/https://www.gameinformer.com/video-feature/2019/03/13/remedys-control-only-has-one-gun-heres-why-its-awesome |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="mashable"/> Internally, the Service Weapon was compared to [[Excalibur]]; whoever wields the gun became the director of the FBC.<ref name="ExCalibur"/> Remedy considered ''Control'' to be a challenging experience; Thomas Puha, Remedy's head of communications, compared the game to ''[[Dark Souls]]''.<ref name="VG247DS">{{cite web |url=https://www.vg247.com/control-dark-souls-vibe-combat-story |title=Control is a tough, complex game with a "Dark Souls vibe" in its combat and storytelling |first=James |last=Billcliffe |work=[[VG247]] |date=June 11, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=7 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707065327/https://www.vg247.com/control-dark-souls-vibe-combat-story |url-status=live}}</ref> The developers wanted to give players more options in combat and introduced enemy variants that force players to instantly change strategy because different enemies have different vulnerabilities.<ref name="differ"/> Mods expand gameplay variety by allowing diverse builds. Players often need to adapt their approach to combat encounters based on their available equipment mods and weapon forms.<ref name="service weapon"/>

To give players more agency, Kasurinen wanted the game to be non-linear, and adopted elements from [[sandbox]] games, role-playing games and [[Metroidvania]] games.<ref name="vgc masurinen"/><ref name="pcgpreview">{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/inside-control-remedys-mind-bending-shooter-where-anything-seems-possible/ |title=Inside Control, Remedy's mind-bending shooter where anything seems possible |first=Andy |last=Kelly |work=[[PC Gamer]] |date=November 1, 2018 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=11 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251111024748/https://www.pcgamer.com/inside-control-remedys-mind-bending-shooter-where-anything-seems-possible/ |url-status=live}}</ref> It was a response to ''Quantum Break'', a linear action game that took five years to develop but only took players about eight hours to complete.<ref name="controversial">{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/in-control-remedys-weird-new-world-feels-brilliant-to-play |title=Back in Control: Remedy's weird new world feels brilliant to play |first=Tom |last=Phillips |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=March 27, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=26 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250426153525/https://www.eurogamer.net/in-control-remedys-weird-new-world-feels-brilliant-to-play |url-status=live}}</ref> This design meant ''Control'' became less curated; as a result, the developers adopted a minimalist [[head-up display]] and removed waypoints. The mission logs only inform players about locations of interest, and players must find their way there. This approach avoided funneling players toward a particular direction and lets players immerse themselves in the game's world, encouraging exploration.<ref name="vgc masurinen"/> Areas in the game are interconnected, and each FBC sector has a large, central area with multiple exits that lead players in different directions.<ref name="pcgpreview"/><ref name="mundane"/> In-game signage was created to guide players to different rooms in a sector.<ref name="sense of place"/> Making some of the in-game powers optional created a unique challenge for the developers designing combat encounters and level layouts because they did not know what powers the [[player character]] would have during a combat encounter. As a result, the team spent a lot of time in the [[quality assurance]] (QA) process to ensure players would not accidentally exploit the game and venture to unintended areas using Jesse's powers.<ref name="mashable">{{cite web |url=https://mashable.com/article/control-gameplay-preview |title='Control' designer digs into the supernatural abilities that shape the game |first=Kellen |last=Beck |work=[[Mashable]] |date=August 9, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026}}</ref> Early versions of the game included [[cooperative multiplayer]], which was eventually cut from the game.<ref name="variety"/>

===Setting===
[[File:33_Thomas_Sidewalk_View.JPG|thumb|left|upright|[[33 Thomas Street]] served as inspiration for the Oldest House.]]

The Oldest House setting is based on [[brutalist architecture]], a style using large concrete blocks popularized in the 1950s and used in many contemporaneous government buildings. The game's world-design director Stuart Macdonald described brutalism as a good science-fiction setting because it has "this sense of power, weight, strength and stability to it".<ref name="eurog art">{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-09-03-remedys-control-is-built-on-concrete-foundations |title=Remedy's Control is built on concrete foundations |first=Ewan |last=Wilson |date=3 September 2019 |access-date=4 September 2019 |work=[[Eurogamer]] |archive-date=20 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200520041757/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-09-03-remedys-control-is-built-on-concrete-foundations |url-status=live }}</ref> The clean, utilitarian design of the Oldest House provides juxtaposition against the Hiss, a supernatural, otherworldly being that reconfigures the building's architecture to suit its needs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gameinformer.com/2019/03/15/uncovering-the-mysteries-of-controls-the-oldest-house |title=Uncovering The Mysteries Of Control's The Oldest House |first=Brian |last=Shea |work=[[Game Informer]] |date=March 15, 2019 |accessdate=January 26, 2026 |archive-date=27 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327060048/https://www.gameinformer.com/2019/03/15/uncovering-the-mysteries-of-controls-the-oldest-house |url-status=live}}</ref> Among the Oldest House's real-world influences is [[33 Thomas Street]], formerly known as the AT&T Long Lines Building, a windowless building in the center of New York City. Macdonald used this building as a modern example of brutalism and created the Oldest House as a "bizarre, brutalist monolith" to house the FBC.<ref name="eurog art"/> [[Boston City Hall]], the Andrews Building at the [[University of Toronto Scarborough]], and the [[Met Breuer]], among others, also served as inspiration for the Oldest House.<ref name="eurog art"/> The relatively flat colors of the background walls make the Oldest House an ideal canvas for showcasing design and lighting effects; it works well with the telekinesis powers because the concrete walls are used in lieu of a target object when the player uses telekinesis to throw debris at foes. The initially pristine spaces eventually show the results of a large, destructive battle.<ref name="eurog art"/> Ultimately, it made environmental destruction visually easy to communicate to readers.<ref name="mundane">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/exploring-the-world-driven-game-design-of-i-control-i- |title=Exploring the world-driven game design of Control |first=Bryant |last=Francis |work=[[Game Developer (magazine) |Game Developer]] |date=April 10, 2020 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=8 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251108045801/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/exploring-the-world-driven-game-design-of-i-control-i- |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="differ"/>

The work of other real-world architects inspired the game's structures. [[Carlo Scarpa]]'s work was heavily used in designing stairways that ascend with other parts of the structure, while [[Tadao Ando]]'s focus on lighting and spiritual spaces is reflected in other parts.<ref name="eurog art"/> The Oldest House's interior design drew inspiration from the [[Yale Center for British Art]], particularly [[Louis Kahn]]'s blend of concrete and wood, as well as the office designs of [[Kevin Roche]] and efficiency pioneer [[Frederick Winslow Taylor]]. Both Roche and Taylor emphasize compartmentalized layouts that prioritize productivity and operational efficiency.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/art/the-real-buildings-that-inspired-i-control-i-s-oldest-house |title=The real buildings that inspired Control's Oldest House |first=Phil |last=Cameron |work=[[Game Developer (magazine) |Game Developer]] |date=October 14, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=8 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251108045743/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/art/the-real-buildings-that-inspired-i-control-i-s-oldest-house |url-status=live}}</ref> The design team also took inspiration from films, such as those of [[Stanley Kubrick]], particularly ''[[A Clockwork Orange (film) |A Clockwork Orange]]'', as well as films featuring oppressive government agencies such as ''[[The Shape of Water]]''.<ref name="eurog art"/> Other films, like ''[[Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (film)|Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy]]'', evoke the concept of repetition, process, and ritualism in these agencies, and that was used to define some of the internal artwork and architecture.<ref name="eurog art"/> Art director Janne Pulkkinen stated they looked at churches and other places where ritual is common because lighting and design of those spaces are often used to draw attention to points of interest.<ref name="eurog art"/>

Unlike previous Remedy games, ''Control'' departs from common tropes of genre fiction. Kasurinen said it allowed the developers to retain "Remedy quirkiness without the setting limiting it", and to incorporate elements that are "a lot stranger".<ref name="pcgpreview"/> Because ''Control'' was Remedy's [[intellectual property]] (IP), the studio was willing to be controversial with it.<ref name="controversial"/> The gathered writings of the fictional [[SCP Foundation]] website were a major influence on ''Control''. Stories on the SCP Foundation's site are based on singular objects with strange, paranormal impacts, and are narratively linked by the common format of reports written by the fictional SCP Foundation, which catalogs and studies the objects. ''Control'' was built atop this mythos, having the Objects of Power and Altered Items, along with collectible writings about these objects.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.co.uk/article/control-game-scp-foundation |title=The web's creepiest fictional wiki is now a mind-bending video game |first=Aron |last=Garst |date=27 August 2019 |access-date=2 September 2019 |magazine=[[Wired UK]] |archive-date=28 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728210255/https://www.wired.co.uk/article/control-game-scp-foundation |url-status=live }}</ref> The developers fixed the story in the genre of the [[new weird]], a modern variant of [[weird fiction]], with stories that combine science fiction and fantasy, often involving a bureaucratic government agency. In ''Control'', the developers reversed the role to place the bureaucracy at the center of the story; the game's narrative designer Brooke Maggs said an oppressive bureaucracy in a corporate office environment contributes to an unnerving experience.<ref name="ign new weird">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/10/07/control-confronts-us-with-a-very-specific-type-of-horror-a-lack-of-control |title=Control Confronts Us With A Very Specific Type of Horror: A Lack of Control |first=Tauriq |last=Moosa |date=7 October 2019 |access-date=7 October 2019 |work=[[IGN]] |archive-date=7 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007221221/https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/10/07/control-confronts-us-with-a-very-specific-type-of-horror-a-lack-of-control |url-status=live }}</ref> Kasurinen said the Hiss was also inspired by the genre; he described it as a disease trying to invade a human body, and that it will slowly try to corrupt and take over its host.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/control-influences-annihilation-new-weird/ |title=How Control Was Influenced by Annihilation and the New Weird |first=Megan |last=Crouse |work=[[Den of Geek]] |date=September 25, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205141101/https://www.denofgeek.com/games/control-influences-annihilation-new-weird/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

According to Kasurinen, one of the game's core themes is the "conflict of collision of strange and mundane". ''Control'' is filled with familiar, commonplace objects that seem innocuous until players discover their altered, often horrifying or incomprehensible, nature through paranatural phenomena.<ref name="narrative design"/> According to the developers, unease and tension emanate from knowing even the most-ordinary items, such as a fridge, a floppy disc or a Merry-Go-Round horse, could be immensely powerful and dangerous.<ref name="ign new weird"/> Typical of new weird stories, the FBC will never know the true purposes or the extent of power of these commonplace items, and the FBC's approach of applying scientific theories to them would not have worked.<ref name="BA"/> Maggs said ''Control'' is not a terrifying experience; instead, the game builds tension, and creates a sense of dread and a sense of awe due to the unknowable and elusive nature of the threat.<ref name="ign new weird"/> Works of [[David Lynch]], the [[Southern Reach Series]] (including ''[[Annihilation (VanderMeer novel)|Annihilation]]''), ''[[2001: A Space Odyssey]]'', ''[[Mr. Robot]]'', ''[[Inception]]'', ''[[Stalker (1979 film)|Stalker]]'', and ''[[Legion (TV series)|Legion]]'', were cited as sources of inspiration for the game.<ref name="inspirations"/><ref name="trust"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/control-director-drew-inspiration-david-lynchs-unexpected-unsettling-work-1240518/ |title='Control' Game Director Drew Inspiration From David Lynch's "Unexpected, Unsettling" Work |first=Trilby |last=Beresford |work=[[Hollywood Reporter]] |date=September 17, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=6 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250806153626/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/control-director-drew-inspiration-david-lynchs-unexpected-unsettling-work-1240518/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Narrative design===
[[File:Sam Lake-MichaelFörtsch.jpg|thumb|upright=0.6|[[Sam Lake]] served as ''Control''{{'}}s creative director who developed its original story.]]

Mikael Kasurinen envisioned a Remedy game that broke from tradition, one that emphasizes world-building rather than being character-driven.<ref name="variety">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2018/gaming/features/control-interview-1202850869/ |title='Control' Was Inspired by the New Weird of 'Annihilation,' Themes of 'Alan Wake' |first=Brian |last=Crecente |work=[[Variety (magazine) |Variety]] |date=June 19, 2018 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=18 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250118010209/https://variety.com/2018/gaming/features/control-interview-1202850869/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The developers first created a vision for the game's world, rather than building its world around a screenplay.<ref name="vgc masurinen"/> The first concept was creating the FBC, a realistic setting that would serve as a basis for paranormal events and a catalyst for the story.<ref name="vgc masurinen"/> This enabled Remedy to consider stories they could tell about the player-character and other individuals in the FBC, but this created the challenge of presenting the stories of the other characters in the open-world format. As a result, the developers relied less on [[cutscene]]s and focused more on creating in-game conversations with [[non-playable character]]s (NPCs). Kasurinen wanted to give players the autonomy to figure out its mystery to create a more gripping and haunting experience.<ref name="vgc masurinen"/> He again cited ''Dark Souls'' as an inspiration for ''Control''{{'s}} approach to storytelling,<ref name="VG247DS"/> and said some story threads are intentionally left open for players to interpret.<ref name="trust">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/how-remedys-control-will-trust-players-to-figure-o/1100-6468007/ |title=How Remedy's Control Will Trust Players To Figure Out Its Unreal Story |first=Alessandro |last=Fillari |work=[[GameSpot]] |date=August 27, 2020 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=3 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250903100812/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/how-remedys-control-will-trust-players-to-figure-o/1100-6468007/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Whereas the main story focuses on Jesse's personal arc, the side stories focus on the game's world and its inhabitants.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gameinformer.com/2019/03/22/how-remedy-is-approaching-side-missions-in-control |title=How Remedy Is Approaching Side Missions In Control |first=Brian |last=Shea |work=[[Game Informer]] |date=March 22, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=9 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251209051446/https://gameinformer.com/2019/03/22/how-remedy-is-approaching-side-missions-in-control |url-status=live}}</ref> The development team used [[environmental storytelling]] to spark players' interest in optional content, rewarding curiosity and exploration with additional narrative and new playable powers.<ref name="narrative design"/> These areas are not necessarily tied to the main narrative.<ref name="mundane"/>

Many of ''Control''{{'s}} voice cast also appear in Remedy's previous games. [[Courtney Hope]] stars as Jesse Faden, [[James McCaffrey (actor)|James McCaffrey]] plays Zachariah Trench, and [[Matthew Porretta]], who plays Casper Darling. is featured in voice roles and live-action videos.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dwan |first1=Hannah |title=Alan Wake and Max Payne's voice actors are going to appear in Remedy's next game, Control |url=https://www.vg247.com/2018/10/15/remedy-control-voice-actors-alan-wake-max-payne/ |website=VG24/7 |date=15 October 2018 |access-date=15 October 2018 |archive-date=15 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181015225322/https://www.vg247.com/2018/10/15/remedy-control-voice-actors-alan-wake-max-payne/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="usg dlc">{{cite web |url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/control-postmortem-exploring-the-story-lore-and-dlc-possibilities-with-remedy |title=Control Postmortem: Exploring the Story, Lore, and DLC Possibilities With Remedy |first=Mike |last=Williams |date=4 September 2019 |access-date=5 September 2019 |work=[[USGamer]] |archive-date=5 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190905163943/https://www.usgamer.net/articles/control-postmortem-exploring-the-story-lore-and-dlc-possibilities-with-remedy |url-status=live }}</ref> Jeremiah Trench was the first character created for ''Control''; according to Lake, Trench represented the FBC and its questionable morals, and he was "a man of action" and "a cynic" who had "suffered a great tragedy". The development team designed Jesse as an FBC outsider with insider connections. This concept forms the basis of a key plot point concerning the FBC's involvement in a tragedy during Jesse's childhood.<ref name="pcgpreview"/> Jesse faced the crisis with a sense of relief; the unfolding events confirm her childhood memories of the incident are not a delusion but reality.<ref name="usg dlc"/> Hope was inspired by [[Vera Farmiga]]'s performance in ''[[The Conjuring]]'' and the way her character remains calm in extraordinary situations.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/interviews/3581498/interview-control-star-courtney-hope-scares-games-horror-vera-farmiga-inspired-performance/ |title=[Interview] 'Control' Star Courtney Hope on What Scares Her, the Game's Horror, and How Vera Farmiga Inspired Her Performance |first=Andrew |last=King |work=[[Bloody Disgusting]] |date=August 30, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=11 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250311134343/https://bloody-disgusting.com/interviews/3581498/interview-control-star-courtney-hope-scares-games-horror-vera-farmiga-inspired-performance/ |url-status=live}}</ref> As with ''[[Max Payne]]'', self-narration forms a part of the ''Control''{{'s}} narrative, allowing players to know more about Jesse's true feelings about the world and characters around her.<ref name="inspirations"/> There was a desire to make the game feel less "American";<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/what-making-control-taught-remedy-about-itself/1100-6472398/ |title=What Making Control Taught Remedy About Itself |first=Tamoor |last=Hussain |work=[[GameSpot]] |date=January 5, 2020 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=17 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240917091656/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/what-making-control-taught-remedy-about-itself/1100-6472398/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Lake said he had been yearning to add his native Finland to one of their games. Finnish actor [[Martti Suosalo]] voices the janitor Ahti, one of the game's supporting characters. The game's music score includes a [[Finnish tango]] Lake wrote, Petri Alanko composed, and Suosalo sang.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://venturebeat.com/2019/11/27/sam-lake-interview-how-storytelling-can-create-so-much-value-in-games/ |title=Sam Lake interview — How storytelling creates value in games |first=Dean |last=Takahashi |date=27 November 2019 |access-date=22 April 2020 |work=[[Venture Beat]] |archive-date=28 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728225717/https://venturebeat.com/2019/11/27/sam-lake-interview-how-storytelling-can-create-so-much-value-in-games/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://egmnow.com/new-york-tango-how-finnish-music-and-culture-define-control/ |title=New York Tango: How Finnish Music and Culture Define Control |first=Sari |last=Kivijärvi |work=[[Electronic Gaming Monthly]] |date=November 8, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205123501/https://egmnow.com/new-york-tango-how-finnish-music-and-culture-define-control/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The game also includes a voice cameo by [[Hideo Kojima]] and his English translator Aki Saito in a side mission.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/2019/8/28/20836789/hideo-kojima-control-easter-egg-voiceover-aki-saito-credits-ps4-pc-xbox-one |title=Hideo Kojima is in Control, narrating a very weird mission |first=Owen |last=Good |date=28 August 2019 |access-date=29 August 2019 |work=[[Polygon (website) |Polygon]] |archive-date=28 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190828205853/https://www.polygon.com/2019/8/28/20836789/hideo-kojima-control-easter-egg-voiceover-aki-saito-credits-ps4-pc-xbox-one |url-status=live }}</ref>

Remedy used fewer live-action elements in ''Control'' than in ''Quantum Break''; most of the live-action footage in ''Control'' is of Casper Darling explaining parts of the Oldest House and Objects of Power within it. According to Lake, these videos were designed to be "slightly crude, clumsy, amateurish by design", and "slightly awkward and clumsy" because they were intended for internal training of FBC agents.<ref name="inspirations">{{cite web |url=https://gameinformer.com/2019/03/18/the-wonderfully-weird-fiction-of-control |title=The Wonderfully Weird Fiction Of Control |first=Elise |last=Favis |work=[[Game Informer]] |date=March 18, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=27 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327060044/https://www.gameinformer.com/2019/03/18/the-wonderfully-weird-fiction-of-control |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Control'' also includes short episodes of a fictional show called "The Threshold Kids", a puppet-based show seemingly aimed at children who may reside in the Oldest House.<ref name="ign new weird"/> Extra story elements are delivered through environmental objects, such as audio recordings and documents, or via live-action video footage played on in-game televisions. Given the game's heavy emphasis on environmental destruction, these methods allowed the developers to organically convey backstory without interruption, avoiding disruptive cinematics that could pull players out of the experience.<ref name="narrative design">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/-i-control-i-freak-inside-the-narrative-design-of-remedy-s-least-linear-game |title=Control freak: Inside the narrative design of Remedy's least linear game |first=Diego |last=Argüello |date=September 18, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |work=[[Game Developer (magazine) |Game Developer]] |archive-date=8 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251108045804/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/-i-control-i-freak-inside-the-narrative-design-of-remedy-s-least-linear-game |url-status=live}}</ref>

The core game includes [[Easter egg (media)|Easter eggs]] referring to ''Alan Wake'', which shares paranormal themes with ''Control''; one such Easter egg discusses the aftermath of ''Alan Wake'' as part of the FBC's case files, which reveals events that occurred in Bright Falls, the primary location of ''Alan Wake'', to have been an AWE.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vg247.com/2019/08/27/alan-wake-easter-egg-control/ |title=Here's the brilliant Alan Wake easter egg in Control and how to find it |first=Kirk |last=McKeand |date=29 August 2019 |access-date=29 August 2019 |work=[[VG247]] |archive-date=29 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829171859/https://www.vg247.com/2019/08/27/alan-wake-easter-egg-control/ |url-status=live }}</ref> A secret area includes a vision of Alan Wake. A [[backmasking|backmasked]] track in the credits sequence of ''[[Alan Wake: American Nightmare]]'' alludes to a past event in the town of Ordinary.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kotaku.com/control-fans-believe-alan-wake-takes-place-in-the-same-1837840844 |title=Control Is Packed With Alan Wake References |first=Gita |last=Jackson |date=3 September 2019 |access-date=3 September 2019 |work=[[Kotaku]] |archive-date=3 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903174627/https://kotaku.com/control-fans-believe-alan-wake-takes-place-in-the-same-1837840844 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="gamespot wake connnections"/> Kasurinen said the inclusion of such references helps establish a continuity between its games, elements to be found and shared by its player community, but these are not necessarily meant to establish a shared universe.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/controls-remedy-wants-a-continuity-between-its-games/ |title=Control's Remedy wants 'a continuity' between its games |first=Andy |last=Robinson |date=31 August 2019 |access-date=3 September 2019 |work=[[Video Games Chronicle]] |archive-date=3 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903195006/https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/controls-remedy-wants-a-continuity-between-its-games/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="TP">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/if-you-liked-the-weirdness-of-annihilation-then-re/1100-6462683/ |title=If You Liked The Weirdness Of Annihilation, Then Remedy's Control May Be For You |first=Randolph |last=Ramsay |work=[[GameSpot]] |date=October 19, 2018 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=2 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240302180824/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/if-you-liked-the-weirdness-of-annihilation-then-re/1100-6462683/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Sam Lake later confirmed the existence of a shared universe between ''Alan Wake'' and ''Control'' that is known as the Remedy Connected Universe.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-next-remedy-connected-universe-game-is-already-in-development/ |title=The next 'Remedy Connected Universe' game is already in development |first=Andy |last=Chalk |date=7 August 2020 |access-date=7 August 2020 |work=[[PC Gamer]] |archive-date=11 December 2021 release of the [[Control_downloadable_content#AWE|''AWE'']] expansion, directly bringing characters and events of ''Alan Wake'' into ''Control''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/remedy-entertainment-is-working-on-a-game-set-in-the-control-and-alan-wake-connected-universe |title=Remedy Entertainment Is Working On a Game Set in the Control and Alan Wake Connected Universe |first=Adam |last=Bankhurst |work=[[IGN]] |date=October 15, 2021 |accessdate=January 25, 2026}}</ref>

===Music===
The game's soundtracks were composed by Petri Alanko and [[Martin Stig Andersen]]. Alanko worked on the main themes and cutscenes in ''Control'', while Andersen worked on the themes of exploration and combat. Alanko regularly joined Remedy's meetings to stay informed about the game's story to better understand the emotional materials he had to work with. To create the haunting sound of the Hiss, Alanko used a microphone that can record [[electromagnetic radiation]] to record sounds of heavy wood being dragged across a floor. He also burnt a piano and destroyed electronic equipment to record its sound. These sounds were then processed to hearing range, generating cacophonous [[Drone (sound)|droning sounds]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.inverse.com/article/59452-control-video-game-petri-alanko-interview-hiss |title=Why 'Control's composer burned a piano to make the game's haunting music |first=Corey |last=Plante |work=[[Inverse (website) |Inverse]] |date=September 23, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=15 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251015094255/https://www.inverse.com/article/59452-control-video-game-petri-alanko-interview-hiss |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lacedrecords.co/blogs/blog/interview-how-alan-wake-composer-petri-alanko-established-control |title=Interview: How Alan Wake composer Petri Alanko established Control |first=Thomas |last=Quillfeldt |date=November 26, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |work=Laced Records |archive-date=7 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007202635/https://www.lacedrecords.co/blogs/blog/interview-how-alan-wake-composer-petri-alanko-established-control |url-status=live}}</ref> The Hiss's main, six-note [[leitmotif]] was created very early in the game's development; Alanko used old choral recordings and processed the voices to strip away their normal pitch, creating a discordant sound to connote the otherworldly nature of the Hiss.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2019/10/interview_taking_the_hiss_with_control_composer_petri_alanko |title=Interview: Taking the Hiss with Control Composer Petri Alanko |first=Graham |last=Banas |work=[[Push Square]] |date=October 9, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=5 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250305174255/https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2019/10/interview_taking_the_hiss_with_control_composer_petri_alanko |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Poets of the Fall]], an alternative rock group that are close friends of Remedy, provided songs, including "Take Control"; these songs are stated in-game to be by the fictional band "Old Gods of Asgard", an allusion to ''Alan Wake''.<ref name="gamespot wake connnections">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/gallery/control-is-full-of-details-about-alan-wakes-fate/2900-3029/ |title=Control Is Full Of Details About Alan Wake's Fate |first=Phil |last=Hornshaw |date=23 September 2019 |access-date=7 October 2019 |work=[[GameSpot]] |archive-date=7 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007221223/https://www.gamespot.com/gallery/control-is-full-of-details-about-alan-wakes-fate/2900-3029/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Remedy used "Take Control" as part of the "[[Ashtray Maze]]", a section in which Jesse fights her way through an ever-changing set of rooms. Remedy worked with Poets of the Fall so they could dynamically incorporate the song as the player progresses through sections of the maze.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/see-how-controls-incredible-ashtray-maze-was-creat/1100-6472494/ |title=See How Control's Incredible Ashtray Maze Was Created |first=Tamoor |last=Hussain |date=5 January 2020 |access-date=5 January 2020 |work=[[GameSpot]] |archive-date=5 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200105225220/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/see-how-controls-incredible-ashtray-maze-was-creat/1100-6472494/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Music from Poets of the Fall's album, including the track "[[My Dark Disquiet]]", is also featured in the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gamingbolt.com/control-will-feature-music-from-poets-of-the-fallen |title=Control Will Feature Music From Poets Of The Fall |first=Landon |last=Wright |work=GamingBolt |date=August 22, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=23 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123161534/https://gamingbolt.com/control-will-feature-music-from-poets-of-the-fallen |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Release==
In May 2017, Remedy announced it had partnered with [[505 Games]] to publish ''Control'', then codenamed "P7". 505 provided marketing and publishing support, and €7.75 million to assist the development, while Remedy retained the intellectual property rights to ''Control''. In a press release, Remedy said ''Control'' would have complex gameplay mechanics and that it would be a "longer term experience" than its previous games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-05-03-505-games-will-publish-remedy-entertainments-new-game |title=505 Games will publish Remedy Entertainment's new game |first=Matthew |last=Handrahan |work=Gameindustry.biz |date=3 May 2018 |access-date=13 June 2018 |archive-date=28 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728075419/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-05-03-505-games-will-publish-remedy-entertainments-new-game |url-status=live}}</ref> ''P7'' was being worked on by Remedy alongside two other projects.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/remedys-upcoming-third-person-action-game-codenamed-p7-will-be-out-in-2019/ |title=Remedy's upcoming third-person action game, codenamed P7, will be out in 2019 |first=Samuel |last=Horti |work=[[PC Gamer]] |date=18 February 2018 |access-date=13 June 2018 |archive-date=13 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613111712/https://www.pcgamer.com/remedys-upcoming-third-person-action-game-codenamed-p7-will-be-out-in-2019/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Control'' was officially revealed at [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]'s [[E3 2018]] press conference.<ref name="release date">{{cite web |url=http://www.gamerevolution.com/news/396643-e3-2018-new-remedy-game-control |title=E3 2018: New Remedy Game Control Announced at Sony Conference |first=Bradley |last=Russell |work=[[Game Revolution]] |date=11 June 2018 |access-date=13 June 2018 |archive-date=14 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614085824/http://www.gamerevolution.com/news/396643-e3-2018-new-remedy-game-control |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Downloadable content ===
{{Main|Control downloadable content}}
Remedy supported ''Control'' with post-launch content, including two expansions that were set after the main game; in these, Jesse takes on her role as the FBC Director.<ref name="usg dlc"/> The first expansion, "The Foundation", was released on 26 March 2020 for PS4 and Windows, and for Xbox One on 25 June 2020.<ref name="first dlc"/> It takes place in the Foundation of the Oldest House, a cave system in which the Astral Plane is set to collide with reality. "The Foundation" introduced new enemy types and side quests, a new character ability named "Shape" that allows Jesse to create platforms using crystals, and a weapon skill named "Fracture" that allows them to destroy said crystals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/control-foundation-dlc-walkthrough-the-nail-7045 |title=Control Foundation DLC walkthrough: Explore the Foundation and investigate the Nail explained |first=Lottie |last=Lyn |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=February 1, 2021 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=21 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721050949/https://www.eurogamer.net/control-foundation-dlc-walkthrough-the-nail-7045 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://primagames.com/news/control-the-foundation-expansion |title=Control: The Foundation expansion's brain-melting new features revealed |work=[[Prima Games]] |date=March 16, 2020 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=19 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250519181140/https://primagames.com/news/control-the-foundation-expansion |url-status=live}}</ref> The second expansion, "AWE", was released on 27 August 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/control-the-awe-expansion-which-ties-into-alan-wak/1100-6481482/ |title=Control: The AWE Expansion, Which Ties Into Alan Wake, Is Available Now |first=James |last=O'Conner |date=26 August 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020 |work=[[GameSpot]] |archive-date=22 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022015250/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/control-the-awe-expansion-which-ties-into-alan-wak/1100-6481482/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This expansion is a [[Crossover (fiction)|crossover]] between ''Control'' and [[Remedy Entertainment]]'s previous game ''[[Alan Wake]]'', which takes place in Bright Falls, Washington, United States. It explores the events of ''Alan Wake'', establishing a shared universe.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.shacknews.com/article/119649/controls-awe-expansion-leaves-players-awestruck-in-three-weeks |title=Control's Awe expansion leaves players awestruck in three weeks |first=Ozzie |last=Meija |work=[[Shacknews]] |date=August 6, 2020 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=29 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129153402/https://www.shacknews.com/article/119649/controls-awe-expansion-leaves-players-awestruck-in-three-weeks |url-status=live}}</ref> It also introduces a new Service Weapon form known as "Surge" that functions similarly to a [[grenade launcher]], allowing Jesse to launch explosives at enemies and manually detonate them.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamerevolution.com/guides/657460-how-to-unlock-the-control-surge-weapon-in-the-awe-dlc |title=How to unlock the Control Surge weapon in the AWE DLC |first=Michael |last=Leri |work=[[Game Revolution]] |date=August 27, 2020 |accessdate=January 24, 2026 |archive-date=7 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207132358/https://www.gamerevolution.com/guides/657460-how-to-unlock-the-control-surge-weapon-in-the-awe-dlc |url-status=live}}</ref>

Smaller, non-narrative content has also been released.<ref name="usg dlc"/> [[Photo Mode]] for the game was released in October 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/control-getting-photo-mode-tomorrow-free-expeditions-mode-later-this-year |title=Control getting Photo Mode tomorrow, free Expeditions mode later this year |first=Matt |last=Wales |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=October 15, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=8 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250208165828/https://www.eurogamer.net/control-getting-photo-mode-tomorrow-free-expeditions-mode-later-this-year |url-status=live}}</ref> "Expeditions", which presents standalone missions of various difficulty with [[power-up]] items for their character, was released as a free update on 12 December 2019.<ref name="first dlc">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/12/13/control-dlc-out-now-first-expansion-release-date-announced |title=Control DLC Out Now, First Expansion Release Date Announced |first=Matthew |last=Adler |date=12 December 2019 |access-date=12 December 2019 |work=[[IGN]] |archive-date=13 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213025504/https://www.ign.com/articles/2019/12/13/control-dlc-out-now-first-expansion-release-date-announced |url-status=live }}</ref> There are three difficulty tiers, the most-difficult tiers provide better rewards, and each run lasts for up to 25 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/control-new-game-mode-expeditions/ |title=Control has a new free game mode called Expeditions and it's available now |first=Alyssa |last=Mercante |date=December 13, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026}}</ref> A free update that was released alongside "AWE" increased the number of control points or hard checkpoints where saving is possible, adding control points before boss fights, as well as several "soft" checkpoints where players can restart without having to return to a control point should Jesse die. A new "assist mode" was added to allow the player to have more control over customizing the difficulty; Remedy intended this update to make game completion possible for novice players.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/control-first-15-mins-of-alan-wake-expansion-shown/1100-6480947/ |title=Control: First 15 Mins Of Alan Wake Expansion Shown, And A Big Free Update Is Coming |first=James |last=O'Conner |date=13 August 2020 |access-date=13 August 2020 |work=[[GameSpot]] |archive-date=23 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200823061610/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/control-first-15-mins-of-alan-wake-expansion-shown/1100-6480947/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 27 August 2020, the first anniversary of its release, ''Control: Ultimate Edition'' was released via [[Steam (service)|Steam]], including the base game, the "Foundation" and "AWE" expansions, and additional free updates.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/control-is-coming-to-steam-this-month-with-an-ultimate-edition |title=Control is coming to Steam this month with an ''Ultimate Edition'' on PlayStation 4 or Xbox One were able to update their version on the newer consoles for no cost.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/control-coming-to-nextgen-consoles/1100-6478347/ |title=Control Coming To Next-Gen Consoles |first=James |last=Carr |date=11 June 2020 |access-date=11 June 2020 }}</ref> 505 Games stated while they searched for a free upgrade path that would work for all users, there was "some form of blocker and those blockers meant that at least one group of players ended up being left out of the upgrade for various reasons".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/2020/8/20/21377188/control-ultimate-edition-upgrade-505-games-xbox-series-x-ps5-explanation According to [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]], ''Control'' received "generally favorable" reviews from critics for most platforms, except for the [[Nintendo Switch]] version, which received "mixed or average" reviews.<ref name="MCPC">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/control/critic-reviews/?platform=pc |title=Control for PC Reviews |publisher=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=26 August 2019 |archive-date=8 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108000343/https://www.metacritic.com/game/pc/control |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="MCPS4">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/control/critic-reviews/?platform=playstation-4 |title=Control for PlayStation 4 Reviews |publisher=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=26 August 2019 |archive-date=12 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112014250/https://www.metacritic.com/game/playstation-4/control |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="MCXONE">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/control/critic-reviews/?platform=xbox-one |title=Control for Xbox One Reviews |publisher=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=26 August 2019 |archive-date=1 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101212328/https://www.metacritic.com/game/xbox-one/control |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Control: Ultimate Edition Reviews |url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/control-ultimate-edition/ |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=[[Metacritic]] |language=en |archive-date=28 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128145515/https://www.metacritic.com/game/control-ultimate-edition/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Ben Reeves from ''[[Game Informer]]'' described ''Control''{{'s}} setting as "bizarrely fascinating" and an "eerie, dreamlike experience" players will remember even after finishing the game.<ref name="GIRev"/> Andrew Webster from ''[[The Verge]]'' similarly lauded the game's unsettling atmosphere, writing the Oldest House feels both surreal and authentic, and commended Remedy's world-building.<ref name="webster"/> Peter Brown from ''[[GameSpot]]'' praised the game's art direction, writing it instills a sense of dread and awe.<ref name="GSpotRev"/> Sam Loveridge from ''[[GamesRadar]]'' called the Oldest House a "captivating" and innovative setting that serves as a "character of its own".<ref name="GRadarRev"/> In ''[[The Guardian]],'' Steve Boxer described ''Control'' as an "immaculately conceived paranormal fantasy" that "manages to feel simultaneously believable and beyond bizarre".<ref name="TGRev"/> Several critics considered ''Control'' on PC to potentially be a "killer app" for Nvidia's [[Nvidia RTX |RTX]] graphics cards, citing the hardware's capacity to enhance the game's visual style.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/2019/9/2/20844751/control-pc-ray-tracing-video |title=Why Control looks so much better on PC |last=Plante |first=Chris |date=2 September 2019 |website=Polygon |language=en |access-date=25 February 2020 |archive-date=6 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200406091133/https://www.polygon.com/2019/9/2/20844751/control-pc-ray-tracing-video |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/digitalfoundry-2019-control-pc-a-vision-for-next-gen-rendering |title=Control PC: a vision for the future of real-time rendering? |last=Battaglia |first=Alex |date=31 August 2019 |website=Eurogamer |language=en |access-date=25 February 2020 |archive-date=14 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214185249/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/digitalfoundry-2019-control-pc-a-vision-for-next-gen-rendering |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2019/08/review-control-is-remedys-best-game-yet-and-a-ray-tracing-masterpiece/ |title=Review: Control is Remedy's best game yet—and a ray tracing masterpiece |first=Sam |last=Machkovech |work=[[Ars Technica]] |date=August 26, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=6 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106132103/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2019/08/review-control-is-remedys-best-game-yet-and-a-ray-tracing-masterpiece/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The gameplay received generally positive reviews. Reeves said Jesse's psychic power, in particular her Launch ability, is central to the game's combat, adding their controls are intuitive but that other psychic powers are underwhelming in comparison. James Davenport from ''[[PC Gamer]]'' noted ''Control'' has the strongest gunplay in a Remedy game to date, and liked the gameplay cycle of switching between the Service Power and Jesse's powers. Davenport compared ''Control'' to ''[[Doom (2016 video game)|Doom]]'' (2016), especially the way they reward players for playing aggressively.<ref name="PCGRev"/> Dave Tach from ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' wrote the combat is "bombastic and satisfying", and said the game's world interactivity is its "most impressive technical achievements".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/reviews/2019/8/26/20829631/control-review-pc-ps4-xbox-one-ray-tracing/ |title=Control review: a technical marvel, and an artistic achievement |first=Dave |last=Tach |work=[[Polygon (website) |Polygon]] |date=August 26, 2019 |accessdate=January 26, 2026 |archive-date=15 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215181707/https://www.polygon.com/reviews/2019/8/26/20829631/control-review-pc-ps4-xbox-one-ray-tracing/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Several critics felt the progression system to be lacking because they failed to evolve the experience in the latter part of the game, because the upgrades did not significantly change the experience,<ref name="GIRev"/><ref name="PCGRev"/> and the game does not have enough enemy types, forcing players to change strategy.<ref name="IGNRev"/> Andrew Webster from ''The Verge'' found the gunplay to be generic, and said the gameplay is not varied enough because it almost entirely relies on combat. He, however, found the telekinetic powers to be exhilarating.<ref name="webster">{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/8/26/20832997/control-review-creators-thriller-ps4-xbox-pc |title=Control is an excellent supernatural thriller with hints of Metroid |first=Andrew |last=Webster |work=[[The Verge]] |date=August 26, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=16 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116031456/https://www.theverge.com/2019/8/26/20832997/control-review-creators-thriller-ps4-xbox-pc |url-status=live}}</ref> Critics generally liked the game's Metroidvania elements; some said this gameplay structure makes narrative sense in the context of the game's story.<ref name="EuroGRev"/><ref name="webster"/> Boxer compared the game to ''[[Prey (2017 video game) |Prey]]'' (2017), noting the addition of superpowers make exploration even more rewarding and fun.<ref name="TGRev"/> The in-game signage was also praised for being surprisingly helpful for navigation.<ref name="EuroGRev">{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/control-review-mid-century-postmodernism |title=Control review: Mid-century postmodernism |first=Christian |last=Donlan |work=[[Eurogamer]] |date=August 27, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=29 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250529001631/https://www.eurogamer.net/control-review-mid-century-postmodernism |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="GSpotRev"/> The in-game map, however, was criticized for being confusing to read.<ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref name="GRadarRev"/>

The story received mixed reviews. Matthew Gault from ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' said Faden's story kept him engaged from start to finish.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://time.com/5669954/control-game-review/ |title='Control' Feels Like What Would Happen if David Lynch Made a Video Game |first=Matthew |last=Gault |work=[[Time (magazine) |Time]] |date=September 6, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=12 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250612225102/https://time.com/5669954/control-game-review/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Reeves liked the way the story slowly reveals Jesse's backstory, but he found the motives of some characters to be unclear and excessively vague, resulting in plot points that can be confusing.<ref name="GIRev"/> Brown liked Remedy's restrained storytelling and its handling of strange themes, writing: "obfuscation is part of what makes ''Control'' so spellbinding".<ref name="GSpotRev"/> According to Davenport, the narrative is inaccessible at first but the game excels at making mundane objectives "fascinating and sinister".<ref name="PCGRev"/> Loveridge liked the story's strangeness and praised Remedy for telling a "surreal narrative that's capable of making even the ordinary feel extraordinary".<ref name="GRadarRev"/>  The game's characters and their voice performances were praised.<ref name="IGNRev"/><ref name="GSpotRev"/> Jonathon Dornbush from ''[[IGN]]'' described the cast as "eclectic" and liked the way each character has an "engrossing" personality. While he praised the quality of Remedy's writing, he said Jesse's main story is an "afterthought".<ref name="IGNRev"/> Davenport found Jesse's personality to be "vapid" and disliked the way her story seemed quite disconnected from the rest of the cast.<ref name="PCGRev"/> Several critics noted the game ends abruptly, though they recognized its side quests help extend the game's length even after the campaign has ended.<ref name="GRadarRev"/><ref name="GIRev"/><ref name="PCGRev"/>

=== Sales ===
During its debut week, ''Control'' was the fourth-best-selling game in the United Kingdom, behind ''[[Astral Chain]]'', ''[[Wreckfest]]'', and ''[[Man of Medan]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gamingbolt.com/astral-chain-debuts-on-top-of-uk-charts-control-takes-fourth-spot |title=Astral Chain Debuts on Top of UK Charts, Control Takes Fourth Spot |first=Shubhankar |last=Parijat |work=GamingBolt |date=September 2, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=13 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250713011811/https://gamingbolt.com/astral-chain-debuts-on-top-of-uk-charts-control-takes-fourth-spot |url-status=live}}</ref> In the United States, ''Control'' failed to debut in the top 20 best-selling games in August 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gamingbolt.com/new-releases-disappoint-during-slow-month-as-madden-nfl-20-tops-august-npd-charts |title=New Releases Disappoint During Slow Month As Madden NFL 20 Tops August NPD Charts |first=Shubhankar |last=Parijat |work=GamingBolt |date=September 12, 2019 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=17 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250117113608/https://gamingbolt.com/new-releases-disappoint-during-slow-month-as-madden-nfl-20-tops-august-npd-charts |url-status=live}}</ref> In Japan, the PlayStation 4 version sold 10,336 physical units, making it the 13th best-selling retail game during its first week of release.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-12-18 |title=Famitsu Sales: 12/09/19 – 12/15/19 [Update] |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2019/12/famitsu-sales-12-09-19-12-15-19 |access-date=2023-07-21 |website=Gematsu |language=en-US |archive-date=21 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220821141254/https://www.gematsu.com/2019/12/famitsu-sales-12-09-19-12-15-19 |url-status=live}}</ref>

By December 2020, ''Control'' had sold over 2 million copies, and Remedy said it was their fastest-growing intellectual property since ''Max Payne''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2020-12-09-control-has-sold-more-than-2m-units |title=Control has sold more than 2m units |first=James |last=Batchelor |date=9 December 2020 |access-date=9 December 2020 |work=[[GamesIndustry.biz]] |archive-date=17 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210717155028/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2020-12-09-control-has-sold-more-than-2m-units |url-status=live}}</ref> While Remedy was happy with the game's performance, CEO Tero Virtala said ''Control'' had not been "a major hit in our industry" in terms of sales.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/beyond-control-whats-next-for-remedy |title=Beyond Control: What's next for Remedy? |first=James |last=Batchelor |work=[[Gameindustry.biz]] |date=March 5, 2021 |accessdate=January 25, 2026 |archive-date=5 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005095051/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/beyond-control-whats-next-for-remedy |url-status=live}}</ref> By August 2021, Remedy announced that over 10 million people had played ''Control'', accounting for those who played it through [[Xbox Game Pass]] and other non-sales routes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/over-10-million-players-have-checked-out-i-control-i- |title=Over 10 million players have checked out Control |first=Bryant |last=Francis |date=13 August 2021 |access-date=14 August 2021 |work=[[Gamasutra]] |archive-date=13 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813193922/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/386809/Over_10_million_players_have_checked_out_Control.php |url-status=live}}</ref> By February 2024, ''Control'' had sold over 4 million units and had earned over {{euro|100 million|long=no}} in revenue.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/alan-wake-2-battles-through-the-dark-place-to-become-remedys-fastest-selling-game-with-over-1-million-copies-sold-although-a-happy-ending-remains-unwritten-as-it-is-yet-to-turn-a-profit/ |title=Alan Wake 2 battles through the Dark Place to become Remedy's fastest-selling game with over 1 million copies sold, although a happy ending remains unwritten as it is yet to turn a profit |first=  Rick |last= Lane |date=February 16, 2024 |accessdate=February 16, 2024 |work=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> By November, the game had sold over 4.5 million units and reached over 19 million lifetime players.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-19 |title=Control sales top 4.5 million |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2024/11/control-sales-top-4-5-million |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=Gematsu |language=en-US |archive-date=19 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241119140128/https://www.gematsu.com/2024/11/control-sales-top-4-5-million |url-status=live}}</ref> By June 2025, it had sold over 5 million units.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Writer |first=Sophie McEvoy Staff |date=2025-08-12 |title=Remedy Q2 sales jump 63.5% to €16.9m |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/remedy-q2-sales-jump-635-to-169m |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |language=en}}</ref> By March 2026, it had sold over 6 million units.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Writer |first=Sophie McEvoy Staff |date=2026-05-05 |title=Remedy reports "stable" Q1 performance despite decreases in revenue and operating profit |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/remedy-reports-stable-q1-performance-despite-decreases-in-revenue-and-operating-profit |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |language=en}}</ref>
