======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Famiclone
======================================================================

{{Short description|Hardware clones of the NES home video game console}}
{{More citations needed|date=April 2023}}

In [[Glossary of video game terms|video game parlance]], a '''famiclone''' (portmanteau of '''''Famicom''''' and '''''clone''''')<ref name="rjfc">{{Cite web|url=https://www.retrojunk.com/a/qo8sjo_B1R/the-fc-twin-in-depth-review|title=The FC Twin - In-depth review &#124; Retro Junk|website=www.retrojunk.com}}</ref> is a [[clone console|hardware clone]] of the [[Nintendo Entertainment System|Family Computer/Nintendo Entertainment System]].<ref name="rjfc"/> They are designed to replicate the workings of, and play games designed for, the Famicom and NES. Hundreds of unauthorized clones have been made available since the height of the NES popularity in the late 1980s. The technology employed in such clones has evolved over the years: while the earliest clones feature a [[printed circuit board]] containing custom or third party [[integrated circuit]]s (ICs), more recent (post-1996) clones utilize single-chip designs, with a custom [[Application-specific integrated circuit|ASIC]] which simulates the functionality of the original hardware and often includes one or more on-board games. Most devices originate in [[China]] and [[Taiwan]], and less commonly [[South Korea]]. Outside China and Taiwan, they are mostly widespread across [[emerging market]]s of [[developing countries]].

In some locales, such as former [[Eastern Bloc]], former [[Post-Soviet states|Soviet countries]] (especially [[Russia]]), [[South America]], [[Middle East]], several [[Asia|Asian countries]] and [[Africa]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://superjumpmagazine.com/the-nintendo-famicom-clone-craze-ebbf69bdd403|title=The Nintendo Famicom Clone Craze|date=4 September 2020|access-date=10 May 2021|archive-date=10 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510092646/https://superjumpmagazine.com/the-nintendo-famicom-clone-craze-ebbf69bdd403|url-status=dead}}</ref> such systems could occasionally be found side by side with official Nintendo hardware, but clones were cheaper and had wider availability of software<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.computinghistory.org.uk/det/60133/Ending-Man-Terminator-2/ | title=Ending Man Terminator 2 - Game Console - Computing History | access-date=2023-03-19 | archive-date=2023-03-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319170238/https://www.computinghistory.org.uk/det/60133/Ending-Man-Terminator-2/ | url-status=live }}</ref> so such clones were the easiest available console gaming systems. Elsewhere, these systems often prompted swift legal action.<ref name=nesworld>{{cite web|url=http://nesworld.com/crushed.php|title=What happens when Nintendo discovers a shipment of NES clones|first=Martin|last=Nielsen|publisher=NES World|access-date=January 15, 2011|archive-date=November 27, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101127114912/http://nesworld.com/crushed.php|url-status=live}}</ref> Many of these early systems were similar to the NES or Famicom not only in functionality, but also in appearance, often featuring little more than a new name and logo in place of Nintendo's branding. In contrast, in the [[former Yugoslavia]] NES clones often visually resembled the [[Mega Drive]], complete with the Sega logo.<ref>[http://mondo.rs/a713934/Mob-IT/Igre/Da-li-ste-przili-laznu-SEGU-Megu.html Da li ste "pržili" lažnu SEGU Megu?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617165703/http://mondo.rs/a713934/Mob-IT/Igre/Da-li-ste-przili-laznu-SEGU-Megu.html|date=2018-06-17}}, Mondo.rs. Retrieved 2015–4–9.</ref>

Few of these systems were openly marketed as "NES compatible".<ref name=pixel>{{cite journal |title= Sega Master System vs Bit 72 | journal = Pixel | issue= 72 |pages= 81}}</ref> Some manufacturers opt describing the system generically as a "TV game", "[[8-bit]] console", "multi-game system", or "[[Handheld TV game|Plug & Play]]", but even these examples generally say nothing to suggest any compatibility with NES hardware. They would often be distributed along with [[Video game piracy|pirate]] cartridges containing several different video games, known as [[Multicart|multicarts]].

==History==
{{unreferenced section|date=July 2026}}

===Origins and early clones===
Around 1987, Taiwanese tech companies successfully reverse-engineered Nintendo’s custom CPU and Picture Processing Unit. Early clone pioneers like Songtly, Bit Corporation, and TSE began manufacturing hardware that used discrete, third-party integrated circuits. But due to big consoles, it only priced about 10% cheaper than an official [[Family Computer]].

===Expansion and regional legends===
In 1992, a company named Steepler launched [[Dendy]], this elephant-branded console became a massive cultural phenomenon. It practically invented the Russian video game market. The [[Pegasus (console)|Pegasus]] ([[Poland]]/[[Balkans]]): became the gold standard in [[Central Europe]], packaged alongside pirated multi-game cartridges. The [[Terminator 2 (console)|Terminator 2]] (Asia/Easter Europe/Africa/Latin America): Designed to look like a [[Sega Mega Drive]] but housing 8-bit Famicom hardware, the Ending Man "Terminator" series became one of the most widely distributed clones in history. The Phantom System & Dynavision ([[Brazil]]): Local manufacturing laws barred imports, leading prominent Brazilian firms like Gradiente to build high-profile unlicensed clones that explicitly mimicked Western NES styling. The [[Micro Genius]] ([[Southeast Asia]]/[[Africa]]/[[Middle East]]): Produced in Taiwan, these were highly durable clones that frequently beat official hardware to market in developing regions.

===The NES-on-a-chip===
By the mid-1990s, engineers compressed the entire motherboard circuitry into a single, cheap Application-Specific integrated Circuit (ASIC). These systems were easily identified by a drop of black epoxy resin (a "glop-top") covering the microchip directly on the circuit board. The cheapness of "NES-on-a-Chip" (NOAC) allowed manufacturers to shove Famiclones into bizarre form factors. These included fake PlayStation shells ([[PolyStation]]), functional computer keyboards designed for "educational" use, and N64/Dreamcast controllers that plugged directly into a TV. Clones relied heavily on multi-carts boasting absurd claims like "999,999-in-1". These cartridges usually contained only a dozen classic titles (like [[Super Mario Bros]]., [[Contra (video game)|Contra]], and [[Duck Hunt]]) repeated with minor palette swaps or gameplay hacks.

===Legality and the modern era===
During their peak, many consumers bought Famiclones entirely unaware they were purchasing counterfeit products. [[Nintendo]] launched countless copyright lawsuits, successfully shutting down several prominent manufacturers over the years. However, as [[Nintendo]]'s original 1980s hardware patents began expiring in the 2000s, the raw hardware cloning of the NES became legal. Today, the spiritual descendants of Famiclones exist as legal retro-consoles (like [[Hyperkin]] systems) or cheap "plug-and-play" handhelds found in modern retail stores.

==Types==
Because NES clones are not officially licensed, they vary in areas such as hardware quality, available games and overall performance. Most clones are produced extremely cheaply, while a few are comparable to first-party hardware in their manufacture quality. In terms of appearance and basic build, there are four general types of clones:

===Console type===
Many clones are designed to resemble the original Famicom, but others have been produced to look like almost all other consoles from the NES, [[Super Nintendo Entertainment System|SNES]], and [[Sega Genesis|Mega Drive/Genesis]] to the [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] and [[PlayStation 3]], and others simply in a generic console shape. Usually, it is easy to tell a famiclone from the real hardware it imitates by the presence of either alternate coloring, brand names that do not match the real console's, or weak construction. Console-type clones almost always utilize cartridges, and they are usually compatible with real Famicom (60-pin) or NES (72-pin) games, as well as custom-made carts (especially multi-carts, unauthorized game cartridges which hold a multitude of games as opposed to just one, which are often included with console-type clones). Console famiclones are most popular in Asia, parts of Europe and Latin America, with few actively sold in North America due to stronger enforcement of the [[copyright]]s in the games typically packaged with a famiclone and of the [[design patent]]s in the imitated consoles.

===Multi-console type===
[[File:FC-Twin-Console-Set-H.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An example of a multi-console clone system: The FC Twin, designed to resemble a [[Super Nintendo Entertainment System (Model SNS-101)|SNES-101]]. This clone system can play both NES and SNES cartridges.]]
Consoles such as the Retron 3 include multiple consoles in one clone.

===Handheld type===
[[File:Power Joy Voyager.png|thumb|125px|Power Joy Voyager handheld famiclone]]
These types of systems contain a built-in [[Liquid-crystal display|LCD screen]] and are usually powered by [[battery (electricity)|batteries]], therefore acting as a completely portable handheld system.

One of the first handheld clones is the ''Top Guy'', although only a small number are known to exist. More widely distributed was Redant's [[Game Axe]], which was manufactured in several revisions through the 1990s. Game Theory Admiral featured an improved [[TFT LCD|TFT]] screen and closely resembled the [[Game Boy Advance]] or [[WinTech Racing|Wintech]] GOOD BOY - not to be confused with a Famicom clone also called Good Boy - designed to look like a [[Game Boy Color]].{{clarify|date=April 2023}} However, this smaller design included a smaller cartridge port; it was supplied with an adapter to allow the use of standard Famicom cartridges with the system. One of the more recent handheld clones is Gametech's [[PocketFami]], the first to be actively marketed as a portable Famicom by its manufacturers, and one of the most widely distributed thanks to the new legitimate status of Famicom clone products.

There are also a number of famiclones in the shape of a [[Game Boy]] or similar, but which can only display NES/Famicom games on a TV, and have a simple [[handheld electronic game|LCD game]] in the screen area. such an example is the NES Clone "GameKids Advance", which resembles an older [[Game Boy Advance]], and has a built-in LCD game, powered by 2 AA batteries, or the included AC adapter. However, the NES games can only be played on TV using the AC adapter. It uses a game cartridge, similar to those from a Game Boy/Game Boy Color, and also includes an adapter to play NES games.

====PocketFami====
The ''Pocket Fami'', also known as ''Pocket Famicom'' (although this name was never used by the manufacturers as Famicom is a trademark of [[Nintendo]]) and ''Pokefami'' (ポケファミ) is an unlicensed [[handheld game console|handheld]] hardware clone of the Famicom produced by GameTech and released in 2004.

The PocketFami features a standard [[D-pad]] and six buttons: the four standard NES buttons (A, B, select, and start), plus two additional "turbo" buttons. It features a 2.5 inch [[backlight|backlit]] [[Liquid crystal display|LCD]] screen capable of displaying both [[NTSC]] and [[PAL]] video. It has one [[headphone]] jack, an [[RCA connector|RCA composite output jack]], and can be powered either through 3 [[AA battery|AA batteries]] or AC adapter. Because of the different cartridge pin design of the [[Japan]]ese Famicom (60 pins) and the international NES (72 pins), international ([[North America]]n, [[Australia]]n, [[Europe]]an) cartridges cannot be played without an additional converter.

[[Nintendo]] sued GameTech over production of the PocketFami, claiming that the device violated their [[patent]]s on the Famicom's hardware. The courts found in favor of GameTech and allowed the device to be sold in Japan, as the original Famicom was first sold in 1983 and most of Nintendo's [[essential patent]]s on the system had expired.

===Controller type===
[[Image:Gunboy double super joy.jpg|thumbnail|right|Two-player Gunboy set]]

This type of hardware clone, popular in North America and western [[Europe]], is designed to hold all the console's hardware in the shape of a regular game console controller, usually the [[Nintendo 64]]'s. Also known as "[[System on a chip|NES-on-a-chip]]" due to their extremely miniaturized hardware (relative to the original NES), these controllers usually shun or at least downplay{{clarify|date=April 2023}} a game cartridge interface in favor of storing games directly in internal memory chips. These famiclones can often run on battery as well as AC power, making them popular for portable usage. These clones have become especially popular in the USA thanks to the new "[[Handheld TV game|TV-Game]]s" fad of selling legitimately emulated classic arcade games in a traditional-looking controller. ([[Atari]] games are especially common.){{Update inline|date=March 2026|reason=Language has been present since the first revision in 2004, the "new TV-game fad" is no longer new}} Controller clones can usually be found in places like flea markets, mall kiosks, or independent toy stores, and most people who sell and buy them are unaware or do not care that they are in fact illegally made. In [[Brazil]] this type of console is commercialized with the name ''GunBoy''.

The ''[[Power Player Super Joy III]]'' consoles (also known as ''Power Games'' and ''XA-76-1E'') are a line of unauthorized handheld [[Nintendo Entertainment System]]/[[Nintendo Entertainment System|Famicom]] clones manufactured by NRTRADE that are sold in [[North America]], [[Brazil]], [[Europe]], [[Asia]], and [[Australia]]. The system resembles a [[Nintendo 64 controller]] and [[Handheld TV game|attaches to a TV set]]. The second controller resembles a [[Sega Genesis]] controller, and a [[light gun]] is also included. [[NTSC]], [[PAL]] and [[SECAM]] versions are available. They all use a custom "NES-on-a-chip" (NOAC) that is an implementation of the NES's hardware (Custom 6502, PPU, PAPU, etc.). The consoles came with 76 built-in games, although marketing frequently claims to have 1,000+ ways of playing them. Most of the included games were originally released for the NES or Famicom, but some have been created by the manufacturer to expand their list of included games. Most of the games have had their title screen graphics removed to save space on the ROM chip, not to mention a company logo removal trick for reduced liability. After this product gained some popularity, the Power Player 3.5, an improved model with more games, was released.{{Citation needed|date=April 2008}} A wireless version of Power Games was also released.{{Citation needed|date=April 2008}}<ref name="sunk">Gearty, Robert.  (April 14, 2005) [[Daily News (New York)|New York Daily News]]  ''[https://web.archive.org/web/20070325035616/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/nydailynews/access/821882541.html?dids=821882541%3A821882541&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS%3AFT&date=Apr%2B14%2C%2B2005&author=ROBERT%2BGEARTY&pub=New%2BYork%2BDaily%2BNews&edition=&startpage=32&desc=VIDEO%2BGAME%2BPIRATES%2BSUNK Video game pirates sunk.]'' Section:News; Page 32</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Nintendo Applauds the FBI -- Four Arrested for Allegedly Distributing Pirated Nintendo Products |date=April 15, 2005 |work=[[Business Wire]] |via=[[FindArticles]] |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0EIN/is_2005_April_15/ai_n13612029 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080923041945/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0EIN/is_2005_April_15/ai_n13612029 |archive-date=September 23, 2008 |url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref>[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]  (November 19, 2005) '' Man gets five years in video game fraud.'' Section: LOCAL; Page 5B</ref>

''Playervision'' or ''Game Stick'' is another unauthorized [[Nintendo Entertainment System]] hardware clone built into a [[gamepad]] and sold in [[South America]], and is just one version of [[Power Player Super Joy III]], nevertheless, the name of the product varies on and in the box, user manual and the gamepad video game console itself. For example, the instruction sheet calls it "Playervision", but the system itself says "Players". This video game console has no cartridge slot, or an input for a second player controller or [[NES Zapper|Zapper]]. This means that some of the games included cannot be used because of the need of a gun (''[[Duck Hunt]]'', for example). The system includes the same 76 games as [[Power Player Super Joy III]], but some of them are repeated or are graphical hacks ([[Teletubbies]], for example, is just ''[[Mario Bros.]]'' with graphic changes).

===Computer type===
[[Image:Mega Kid Educational Computer.jpg|thumb|200px|A [[Mega Kid MK-1000]] Computer type famiclone]]
These famiclones are designed to resemble either 1980s [[home computer]]s, modern [[Computer keyboard|keyboard]]s, or the real Famicom's [[BASIC]] kit. Usually, these clones consist of the same hardware as the console type, but put inside a keyboard instead of a console lookalike. They are usually supplied with a cartridge containing some computer-style software, such as a simple [[word processor]] and a version of BASIC (most common are G-BASIC, a [[copyright infringement of software|counterfeit]] version of Family BASIC, and F-BASIC, an original but more limited version), and some "educational" typing and mathematics games. Some even include a [[Mouse (computing)|computer mouse]] and a [[Graphical user interface|GUI]]-style interface. Note that, while the interface is similar to Nintendo's [[Family BASIC]] keyboard, clone keyboards are generally not fully compatible with official software (and vice versa) due to differing key layouts.

==Software game titles==
Since none of these unlicensed clones contain the [[10NES]] authentication chip, most are capable of running games that an official NES model would not run. In addition, many modern NES clones come with a built-in selection of games, typically stored on an internal [[read-only memory|ROM]] which can range from 128 [[kilobyte|KB]] up to several [[megabyte]]s in size.

These built-in games are usually designed to complement, rather than replace, the traditional cartridge slot, although some devices omit such a slot entirely, allowing only the built-in games to be played. Typical numbers for the built-in "distinct" games range from as low as three to as high as fifty or one hundred games for more expensive products. The number of "distinct games" is important, because while many NES clones claim to have thousands of built-in games, most of these games are usually nothing more than hacks that allow the player to start the same game at different levels or with different numbers of lives.

The games are usually direct unlicensed copies of official NES and Famicom game titles, usually with copyright information removed and sometimes featuring other minor changes. The most commonly found games in NES clones are generally games below 64 K of ROM size and which can be easily split into distinct subgames or levels. As such, ''[[Track & Field (video game)|Track & Field]]'' and ''[[Circus Charlie]]'' are present in a large percentage of NES clones, usually blown up to count as 6 or 7 "distinct" games each. ''[[Duck Hunt]]'' (often with its clay shooting mode shown as a separate game) is also a common NES clone feature as they justify the existence of the [[light gun]] accessory. Other popular, although less common choices, are ''Super Mario Bros.'' hacks, ''[[Excitebike]]'', ''[[Tetris]]'', ''Magic Jewelry'' (an unlicensed clone of ''[[Columns (video game)|Columns]]''), older sports titles and miscellaneous platform games. Additionally, some clones incorporate games that, although they may initially appear to be original, are in fact counterfeit copies featuring extensive graphical (and sometimes audio) modifications. Examples of this include ''UFO Race'', based on Nintendo's ''[[F-1 Race]]'', ''Pandamar'' (also known as simply ''Panda''), based on ''[[Super Mario Bros.]]'', ''Ladangel'', based on [[Hudson Soft]]'s ''[[Challenger (video game)|Challenger]]'' and ''UFO Shoot'', based on ''[[Duck Hunt]]''.

However, some systems include legally licensed games; for example, the [[Rumble Station]]'s 15 built-in games are licensed from [[Color Dreams]], and [[Thin Chen Enterprise|Sachen]]'s Q-Boy includes only its own original titles. A growing number of recent clones, such as those marketed by Technologies in the United States, contain large numbers of original games made by developers in China.

==Hardware and software compatibility==
[[File:UMC Famiclone discrete chipset.JPG|thumbnail|right|Discrete chipset manufactured by [[United Microelectronics Corporation|UMC]] used in a 1992 famiclone]]
While most famiclones will run most original licensed Nintendo software and work with most original carts (being even more versatile than an original NES because of the lack of regional lockout chips and sometimes having a dual 60-pin and 72-pin cartridge compatibility), the degree of hardware compatibility with original NES accessories and miscellaneous hardware equipment may vary, and even software level compatibility is not always perfect.

The most common software-level incompatibility in the built-in games that some sport, is the lack of [[NVRAM|save RAM]], causing the few games that use it to fail when trying to save or load data.

[[Image:Famicom clone PCB.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The NES is replicated in a small chip underneath the black epoxy blob (silicon).]]
Since most modern Famiclones are based on the NES-on-a-chip ASIC, they automatically inherit all of its limitations, which includes graphical glitches and compatibility issues.

At a hardware level, the most common incompatibility is the lack, in some famiclones, of the original Famicom's expansion port (although it is always present, at least at a logical level, and in some clones it is internally hardwired; e.g. in computer-type famiclones it is hardwired to the built-in keyboard, even if not externally accessible).

[[File:RetroUSB-AVS-Console-FL.jpg|thumb|right|The RetroUSB AVS uses [[Field-programmable gate array|FPGA-based]] hardware emulation, achieving a high degree of compatibility.]]
Some famiclones also use standard [[Atari joystick port|Atari 9-pin]] shaped or even 15-pin joypad connectors instead of the proprietary NES connectors, and their controllers usually offer all of the functionality of a standard NES controller and sometimes features such as "slow motion" or several autofire keys with different speeds, which are not present on the standard out-of-the-box NES joypads. Despite being physically identical to Atari 9-pin, the protocol is different: Atari uses a parallel protocol where each wire carries the status of a single button,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://old.pinouts.ru/Inputs/JoystickAtari2600_pinout.shtml |title=Atari joystick pinout |publisher=Old.pinouts.ru |date=2013-08-24 |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=2013-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016141558/http://old.pinouts.ru/Inputs/JoystickAtari2600_pinout.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> whereas famiclones use the same 4021-based serial protocol the original NES used.<ref>{{cite web |author=Official NES Controllers on Unofficial Consoles |url=http://www.nintendoplayer.com/projects/official-nes-controllers-on-unofficial-consoles/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130727105345/http://www.nintendoplayer.com/projects/official-nes-controllers-on-unofficial-consoles/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-07-27 |title=NES-to-Famiclone adapter |publisher=Nintendoplayer.com |date=2013-01-24 |access-date=2013-10-17 }}</ref> Connecting standard controllers to them may result in malfunction or damage of the controller or the famiclone itself.

Lastly, like many modern consoles and other devices meant to be connected to a TV, many modern famiclones lack an [[RF modulator]] and instead only have separate audio and [[composite video]] outputs (sometimes [[S-Video]]), also to cut on the (already low) production costs.

Some manufacturers have added new [[Backward compatibility|backward-compatible]] features to their NOAC ASICs, which allow developers to add new features like an improved processor (a [[65C816]] compatible), better graphics, stereo sound (by adding another audio unit), [[PCM audio]], and a unified bus ([[OneBus]]) which lets manufacturers use a single ROM to store games instead of the two (one for program and other for graphics) the original NES and Famicom used.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://playpower.pbworks.com/f/VT02+Data+Sheet+RevisionA5_ENG__1.pdf |title=VT-02 Famiclone Datasheet |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=2013-10-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018014424/http://playpower.pbworks.com/f/VT02+Data+Sheet+RevisionA5_ENG__1.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> This hardware was primarily designed by Taiwanese companies V.R. Technology and [[United Microelectronics Corporation|UMC]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Products|url=http://vrt.com.tw/product_category.htm |access-date=2024-09-07 |website=vrt.com.tw}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-28 |title=Nerdly Pleasures: The Unofficial Enhanced NESs - Continuing On where Nintendo Left Off |url=https://nerdlypleasures.blogspot.com/2023/10/the-unofficial-enhanced-ness-continuing.html |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=Nerdly Pleasures}}</ref>

==Post-patent famiclones==
[[File:Retro-Bit-Retro-Duo-Portable.jpg|thumb|right|The Retro Duo Portable, one of the more recent famiclones made for American markets]]
Some of Nintendo's patents on the Famicom expired in 2003, followed in 2005 by NES-specific patents such as those covering the [[10NES]] lockout chip. While Nintendo still holds various related trademarks, NES hardware clones are no longer necessarily illegal on the basis of patent infringement. This matter is complicated by the effect of different patents awarded in different countries, with different expiration dates. Nintendo sued Gametech in 2005 for selling the PocketFami, despite the patent expiration. Nintendo lost this suit. However, famiclone manufacturers who incorporate copyrighted games into the unit may still be subject to legal liability on that basis, due to copyrights having much longer terms than patents (in most countries creative works such as games are automatically in copyright for many decades, sometimes up to 95 years after their creation).

While the old-style famiclones continue to be found, the newly legitimized market has seen several clones that openly advertise support for original Famicom or NES games (or sometimes both), a feature not usually publicized by previous clones, which were often marketed as cheap gifts rather than Famicom-compatible systems. Examples of these newer efforts include the Generation NEX, which resembles a flattened version of the original NES and supports both NES and Famicom games, Gametech's Neo-Fami (also released in both Famicom and NES compatible versions as the "FC Game Console" by [[Yobo Gameware]]), and the handheld PocketFami, a more ambitious, albeit still slightly flawed, successor to the older TopGuy, Game Axe, and [[Game Theory Admiral]]. However, these more legitimate clones are still based on the same NES-on-a-chip architecture as the older systems, and as such still suffer from many of the same compatibility problems.

===Generation NEX===
[[File:Genertation Nex.jpg|thumb|Generation NEX, with an NES game loaded in front and a Famicom game loaded topside]]
Generation NEX is a Nintendo hardware clone released in 2005.<ref name="Sili" /><ref name="Lemon" /> It is compatible with Japanese Famicom and North American/European NES cartridges. A front-loading slot is used for NES games, like the original console, while a top-loading slot handles Famicom games.<ref name="IGN" /> Messiah Entertainment Inc., a company based in Los Angeles,<ref name="Crave" /> announced the Generation NEX in May 2005.<ref>{{cite web |title=Messiah Debuts Generation NEX Console |url=https://www.gamezone.com/news/messiah_debuts_generation_nex_console/ |website=GameZone |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-05-23 |archive-date=2021-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211030134635/https://www.gamezone.com/news/messiah_debuts_generation_nex_console/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The console was shown at the [[Classic Gaming Expo]] that August, and was scheduled for release in September 2005.<ref name="Frosty">{{cite web |last=Weintraub |first=Steve 'Frosty' |title=Miss Your Old Nintendo 8-Bit? Check This Out |url=https://collider.com/miss-your-old-nintendo-8bit-check-this-out/ |website=Collider |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-08-17 |archive-date=2020-01-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200109012043/https://collider.com/miss-your-old-nintendo-8bit-check-this-out/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Saviors">{{cite web |last=Gitlin |first=Elle Cayabyab |title=The saviors of retro gaming, part two |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2005/06/502/ |website=Ars Technica |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-06-11 |archive-date=2020-10-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027020259/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2005/06/502/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Kohler |first=Chris |title=Retro Gamers Unite! |url=https://www.wired.com/2005/08/retro-gamers-unite/ |magazine=Wired |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-08-24 |archive-date=2020-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928232417/https://www.wired.com/2005/08/retro-gamers-unite/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The NEX is a slimmer version of the original NES, measuring an inch and a half in height.<ref name="IGN" /> The console uses a custom-designed [[integrated circuit]] based on NES-on-a-chip, which is used by most Nintendo clone consoles.<ref name="Vintage">{{cite web |last=Edwards |first=Benj |title=A False Messiah: The Generation NEX Sucks |url=http://www.vintagecomputing.com/index.php/archives/6/this-just-in-the-generation-nex-sucks |website=Vintage Computing and Gaming |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007154911/http://www.vintagecomputing.com/index.php/archives/6/this-just-in-the-generation-nex-sucks |archive-date=2013-10-07 |date=2005-11-03}}</ref> The ASIC used is known as the VT03, and is part of the OneBus family of NOACs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-28 |title=Nerdly Pleasures: The Unofficial Enhanced NESs - Continuing On where Nintendo Left Off |url=https://nerdlypleasures.blogspot.com/2023/10/the-unofficial-enhanced-ness-continuing.html |access-date=2024-10-24 |website=Nerdly Pleasures}}</ref> The NEX is compatible with approximately 95 percent of NES games,<ref>{{cite web |title=Compatibility list |url=http://www.playmessiah.com/onlinestore/gnex_faq-chart.htm |publisher=Messiah Entertainment |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060907225820/http://www.playmessiah.com/onlinestore/gnex_faq-chart.htm |archive-date=2006-09-07 |date=2006-06-27}}</ref> excluding games such as ''[[Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse]]''.<ref name="Sili" /><ref name="IGN" /> The console includes [[stereo sound]] capabilities for [[Homebrew (video games)|homebrew game]]s.<ref name="Sili">{{cite web |title=Generation NEX compatibility list |url=https://www.siliconera.com/generation-nex-compatibility-list/ |website=Siliconera |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-11-02 |archive-date=2020-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200826124443/https://www.siliconera.com/generation-nex-compatibility-list/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The NEX retailed for $59.99,<ref name="Lemon" /> and included one wired controller. Wireless 2.4 [[Hertz|GHz]] controllers were also produced, and were sold in sets of two at a cost of $50 per set.<ref name="IGN" /><ref name="Kuchera" /> The wired and wireless controllers were redesigned from the [[Nintendo Entertainment System#Controllers|original NES controller]], having an appearance more similar to the [[Super Nintendo Entertainment System#Peripherals|SNES controller]].<ref name="IGN" /> The console includes controller ports that allow the user to plug in and use original NES controllers instead, and the wireless NEX controllers are also compatible with the original NES. The NEX is also compatible with all other [[List of Nintendo Entertainment System accessories|NES accessorie]]s, such as the [[NES Zapper|Zapper gun]].<ref name="IGN" /><ref name="Saviors" /> Messiah also produced a wireless [[arcade stick]] controller.<ref name="Crave" />

The Generation NEX initially received a negative reception from user reviews and some game websites.<ref name="Kuchera" /> Complaints were made regarding the console's compatibility with NES/Famicom games, which exhibited graphical and audio issues in some cases when played on the NEX.<ref name="Lemon">{{cite web |last=Cole |first=Vladimir |title=New NES console knockoff is a lemon |url=https://www.engadget.com/2005-11-04-new-nes-console-knockoff-is-a-lemon.html |website=Engadget |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-11-04 |archive-date=2021-10-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028142037/https://www.engadget.com/2005-11-04-new-nes-console-knockoff-is-a-lemon.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Vintage" /><ref name="Grant" /> Critics also disliked the soft, squishy buttons on the redesigned controllers.<ref name="Lemon" /><ref name="IGN" /><ref name="Vintage" /><ref name="Kuchera" /> The NEX's importer, [[Lik Sang]], canceled its pre-orders in November 2005, following the console's poor reception.<ref>{{cite web |last=Grant |first=Christopher |title=Generation NEX pulled from virtual shelves |url=https://www.engadget.com/2005-11-30-generation-nex-pulled-from-virtual-shelves.html |website=Engadget |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-11-30 |archive-date=2022-04-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406234132/https://www.engadget.com/2005-11-30-generation-nex-pulled-from-virtual-shelves.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Reviewers for [[IGN]] gave a positive review. They considered the console an improved version of the original NES, while writing that the new counterpart did not present any noticeable graphic issues.<ref name="IGN">{{cite web |last=Block |first=Gerry |title=The NES Reincarnated |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/12/21/the-nes-reincarnated |website=IGN |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-12-20 |archive-date=2020-10-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201010091643/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/12/21/the-nes-reincarnated |url-status=live }}</ref> Christopher Grant of [[Engadget]] was critical of IGN's review, noting that it did not address the compatibility issues brought up in other reviews. Grant wrote, "IGN devotes the majority of the review to the pretty packaging, nice design, and wireless controllers, glossing over the compatibility. Don't they know: it's the games, stupid."<ref name="Grant">{{cite web |last=Grant |first=Christopher |title=IGN reviews Generation NEX... in alternate dimension |url=https://www.engadget.com/2005-12-22-ign-reviews-generation-nex-in-alternate-dimension.html |website=Engadget |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2005-12-22 |archive-date=2022-04-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406234145/https://www.engadget.com/2005-12-22-ign-reviews-generation-nex-in-alternate-dimension.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Shane Hirschman of [[CraveOnline]] reviewed the console a year after its release, and he also considered it an improvement over the original NES: "Given the Generation NEX's inexpensive price, high-quality, and efficient game play, gamers of all types will be pleased to see the NES is back and better than ever."<ref name="Crave">{{cite web |last=Hirschman |first=Shane |title=Review: Generation NEX |url=http://www.craveonline.com/gaming/articles/04647228/generation_nex.html |website=CraveOnline |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070216023516/http://www.craveonline.com/gaming/articles/04647228/generation_nex.html |archive-date=2007-02-16 |date=2006-12-15}}</ref> Ben Kuchera of ''[[Ars Technica]]'' also reviewed the console a year after its release, and gave a mixed review. Kuchera found few issues involving graphics and audio, but he also considered the console's $60 price too high. Kuchera preferred the feel of the original NES controllers, and considered the wireless controllers too expensive as well.<ref name="Kuchera">{{cite web |last=Kuchera |first=Ben |title=Peripheral Review: Generation NEX |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2006/11/5946/ |website=Ars Technica |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2006-11-14 |archive-date=2020-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020212756/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2006/11/5946/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Kuchera subsequently wrote that the Generation NEX "muddies the image so badly" that "you're doing yourself a disservice by playing the games so compromised."<ref>{{cite web |last=Kuchera |first=Ben |title=An NES, two clones, and the Virtual Console. Where does Mario look his best? |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2007/02/7044/ |website=Ars Technica |access-date=2020-04-15 |date=2007-02-14 |archive-date=2019-11-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191110015001/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2007/02/7044/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== My Arcade Micro Player ===
Micro Player is a series of famiclone-based miniature [[arcade cabinet]]s<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=ausretrogamer |date=2019-11-12 |title=My Arcade Micro Players - Review {{!}} AUSRETROGAMER |url=https://ausretrogamer.com/my-arcade-micro-player-review-6-inch-collectable-retro-arcade-machines/ |access-date=2024-12-03 |website=ausretrogamer.com |language=en-AU}}</ref> sold by dreamGEAR, a [[Video game accessory|video game accessories]] company based in [[Torrance, California|Torrance]], [[California|CA]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=DreamGEAR Main Website |url=https://www.dreamgear.com/}}</ref> under the My Arcade brand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nerdly » 'My Arcade Micro Player' Retro Arcade Review |url=https://www.nerdly.co.uk/2018/10/22/my-arcade-micro-player-retro-arcade-review/ |access-date=2024-12-03 |language=en-US}}</ref> Several examples of game cabinets sold under this brand are ''[[Pac-Man]]'', ''[[Dig Dug]]'', ''[[Galaga]]'', and ''[[Bubble Bobble (video game)|Bubble Bobble]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Micro Players |url=https://myarcade.com/collections/micro-player |access-date=2024-12-03 |website=My Arcade® |language=en}}</ref>

The cabinets feature artwork from the originals, and utilize licensed NES ports of the games included on them, with Nintendo copyright information removed.<ref name=":12" /> The mini arcade cabinets were relatively popular due to their low price. They also released consoles containing these games with a handheld form factor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-01-06 |title=My Arcade Pac-Man Pocket Player (and quick Namco Blast!) "look"/"review" |url=https://forums.atariage.com/topic/286782-my-arcade-pac-man-pocket-player-and-quick-namco-blast-lookreview/ |access-date=2024-12-03 |website=AtariAge Forums |language=en-US}}</ref>

DreamGEAR also manufactures several handheld consoles containing [[multicart]]s. However, since the consoles are sold in the US, they contain few pirated games, as to avoid legal action. The consoles instead contain various [[shovelware]] games by Chinese companies such as Nice Code Software, JungleTac, and Waixing Technology. Several variants contain licensed [[Data East]] games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=chrisscullion |date=2019-06-06 |title=My Arcade Pixel Player review |url=https://tiredoldhack.com/2019/06/06/my-arcade-pixel-player-review/ |access-date=2024-12-03 |website=Tired Old Hack |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Clones by region or country==

===Arabian Peninsula===
The most popular famiclone in the 1990s were ''Rinco Home Computer'' and ''Al Sagr'' distributed by Ramar International Ltd, that previously sold [[Atari 2600]] clones in the region, which also proved to be popular. Ramar translated some of the games into Arabic and published few unique bootleg games like ''The Dragon''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://hallyvorc.wixsite.com/unauthorizon/post/cut-into-the-number-of-famiclones-ever-produced-case-8-rinco-al-sagr?referral=business-feed |title=Cut into the Number of Famiclones Ever Produced - Case #8: RINCO/AL SAGR |website=wixsite.com|access-date=2025-03-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ultimateconsoledatabase.com/famiclones/home_computer_3600.htm|title=Home Computer 3600 - Ultimate Console Database at ultimateconsoledatabase.com|website=ultimateconsoledatabase.com|access-date=2023-03-22|archive-date=2023-03-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316225009/http://ultimateconsoledatabase.com/famiclones/home_computer_3600.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> In the same time, Nintendo officially distributed its products here,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://segaretro.org/History_of_Sega_in_The_Gulf#Competitors |title=History_of_Sega_in_The_Gulf#Competitors}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nintendo.com/corp/companies/middleeast.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/19980205072054/http://www.nintendo.com/corp/companies/middleeast.html | archive-date=1998-02-05 | title=Nintendo: International Distributors }}</ref> but it is unknown if they took legal actions against famiclones sellers.

===Argentina===
The ''Family Game'' was manufactured by the Argentine company Electrolab S.A.<ref name=":1">{{cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pZb5CAAAQBAJ&pg=PA51|first1=Graciela Alicia|last1=Esnaola Horacek|first2=Alejandro|last2=Iparraguirre|first3=Guillermo|last3=Averbuj|first4=María|last4=Luján Oulton|chapter=Argentina|editor-first=Mark J. P.|editor-last=Wolf|title=Video Games Around the World|date=May 2015|publisher=MIT Press|page=51|isbn=9780262527163}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite news|url=https://www.neoteo.com/la-maldicion-del-elefante-gris-clones-famicom-miserias-compartidas/|title=La Maldición del Elefante Gris: Clones de Famicom y miserias compartidas|work=NeoTeo|date=2016-11-09|access-date=2018-12-09|archive-date=2018-12-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209124622/https://www.neoteo.com/la-maldicion-del-elefante-gris-clones-famicom-miserias-compartidas/|url-status=live}}</ref> They distributed ''Super Family Electrolab Ending-Man'' (based on [[Terminator 2 (console)|Ending-Man Terminator]] clone) and ''Electrolab Family Game'' with official distribution of [[Supervision]].<ref>{{cite journal |title= Para Llegar Al Final, Hay Que Tener Muchas Vidas Y Ser Los Mejores | journal = Action Games | issue= 12 |pages= 32–33}}</ref> At the peak of its popularity, its sales amounted 95% of the argentinian console market.<ref>{{cite book |title=Piracy and Intellectual Property in Latin America: Rethinking Creativity and the Common Good|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vxbUDwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Family+game%22+nintendo+Mexico&pg=PT95|last1=Goldgel-Carballo|first1=Víctor|last2=Poblete|first2=Juan|publisher=Routledge|language=en|date=2020-03-03|access-date=2021-12-18|isbn=978-1-000-03875-0}}</ref>

According to an interview with Eddy Kiersz, CEO of Electrolab, they paid royalties to Nintendo both to sell the "famiclones" and to import the games, with the condition that they would not export them outside of Argentina. He also mentioned that Nintendo itself put them in contact with the Taiwanese company [[NTDEC]] which built the Famicom, to design the "Family Game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FCJXlXJeiEc|title=¿El PADRE del FAMILY GAME en ARGENTINA? ENTREVISTA a EDDY KIERSZ, ex dueño de Electrolab.|date=October 1, 2024|via=YouTube}}</ref> This is not true and Eddy Kiersz confused Nintendo of America with the American subsidiary of NTDEC, whose full name was Nintendo Electronic Co.<ref name=special301>{{Cite web|url=https://library.gamehistory.org/repositories/2/resources/249|title=Collection: Special 301 Comments on Video Game Piracy in Asia and Latin America &#124; Video Game History Foundation Library|website=library.gamehistory.org}}</ref>

Other known consoles are ''NTD Family Game'' (distributed by NTD Electronica Argentina),<ref>{{cite journal |title= Family Game | journal = Action Games | issue= 12 |pages= 17}}</ref> ''Son Son'',<ref>{{cite journal |title= Somos Fabricantes De Taiwan | journal = Action Games | issue= 12 |pages= 8–9}}</ref> ''Froggy Family Game'' (distributed by BTE Electronics SA<ref>{{cite journal |title= Froggy Family Game | journal = Action Games | issue= 12 |pages= 31}}</ref>), ''Rasti'' (distributed by Rasti SA<ref>{{cite journal |title= Rasti VideoGames | journal = Action Games | issue= 12 |pages= 42–43}}</ref>), ''Micro Genius'', Family Game and ''Goodboy'' (distributed by Tec Toy Argentina),<ref>{{cite journal |title= Tec Toy Argentina S.R.L | journal = Action Games | issue= 7 |pages= 59}}</ref> ''Edu Family Game'' (distributed by Videogames EDU S.A),<ref>{{cite journal |title= EDU Family Game Video Computer | journal = Action Games | issue= 8 |pages= 23}}</ref>''Turbo Game'' (distributed by La Roque S.A),<ref>{{cite journal |title= Turbo Game | journal = Action Games | issue= 2 |pages= 26–27}}</ref> ''Super Game City'' (by Top Games),<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Top Games|journal=Action Games |page=79 |issue=19}}</ref> ''Asder PC-95'' (distributed in Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay by M.S Trade and Commerce)<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Asder PC-95 |journal=Action Games |pages=2–3 |issue=55}}</ref> and ''Hyper Boy'' (by Honson Games).<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Hyper Boy |journal=Supergames |page=42 |issue=1}}</ref>

Another popular brand of famiclones were made by Bit Argentina and that is ''Bitgame'',<ref>{{cite journal |title= Parece Igual, Pero Es De Bit | journal = Action Games | issue= 12 |pages= 21}}</ref> ''Super Bitgame'' and ''Video Racer''.<ref>{{cite journal |title= Bitgame | journal = Dos Posibilidades Para la Misma Aventura| issue= 12 |pages= 4–5}}</ref> In 1992, Nintendo entered the Argentina market with H.Briones Argentina S.A. as representative<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.org/details/ClubNintendo04Ao01N04Argentina/page/n1/mode/1up|title=Club Nintendo 04 - Año 01 Nº 04 (Argentina)|date=December 1992}}</ref> and Bit Argentina was awarded as official distributor with the rights to still sell famiclones.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Bit Argentina H. Briones Argentina S.A | journal = Action Games | issue= 12 |pages= 55}}</ref>

In 1993, more than 180,000 8-bit systems sold in the country were famiclones and only 12,000 units authentic NES systems. Nintendo took legal actions against distributors of clones. Argentina was one of the countries on [[Special 301 Report|Special 301 Watch List]] from 1994 due to huge intellectual property issue and authors of the report classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Very Severe" (50%-100%).<ref name=special301 />

===Australia===
Since 1989, Centronics Systems distributed the Spica IQ-701 along with games and multicarts in custom-made boxes.<ref>{{cite journal |title= Spica Entertainment Series | journal = The Age | issue= 1989–12–12 }}</ref> Nintendo sued the distributor and the consoles were withdrawn from further sale.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/cases/cth/FCA/1992/584.html?stem=0&synonyms=0&query=title%2528nintendo%2520%2529|title=Re Centronics Systems Pty Ltd; Maurice Latin; Tiberio Salice and Fabrizio Latin v Nintendo Company Ltd [1992] FCA 584; (1992) 111 ALR 13 (1992) 24 IPR 481 (1992) 39 FCR 147 (1 December 1992)|website=austlii.edu.au|access-date=24 January 2025}}</ref> Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Moderate" (10%-25%).<ref name=special301 />

===Baltic States===
The most known clone in these countries is ''Zhiliton'' which looks like the Sega Mega Drive model I. Due to the small market of these countries, there are also other clones such as ''[[Dendy (console)|Dendy]]'', ''UFO'', ''Subor'', ''Liko'', [[Ending-Man Terminator|''Terminator 2'']] and ''Fei Hao''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spoki.lv/speles/Top-Nintendo-Entertainment-System/282647|title=Top Nintendo Entertainment System spēles|website=Spoki|date=6 February 2011|access-date=21 June 2020|archive-date=22 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200622171338/https://spoki.lv/speles/Top-Nintendo-Entertainment-System/282647|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.delfi.ee/archive/siim-avi-sund-1984-telekamang-ehk-meelelahutus-missugune?id=13822910|title=Siim Avi (sünd. 1984): Telekamäng ehk meelelahutus missugune|date=September 11, 2006|website=Delfi|access-date=June 21, 2020|archive-date=June 23, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200623221518/https://www.delfi.ee/archive/siim-avi-sund-1984-telekamang-ehk-meelelahutus-missugune?id=13822910|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title= PC vs Consoles | journal = Kiberzona| issue= 2000-05 |pages= 26–29 |url=https://archive.org/details/kiberzona-2000-05/page/n26/mode/1up}}</ref> Since 1993, Interpons company has been the supplier of Nintendo products (NES, SNES, Game Boy) in the Baltic countries, but these products were described by the local press as too expensive for the average citizen.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://adt.arcanum.com/en/view/Hommikuleht_1993_02/?query=interpons+nintendo&pg=346&layout=s |title=Jaapani firma NINTENDO vallutab maailma}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://adt.arcanum.com/en/view/RahvaHaal_1993-2/?query=interpons&pg=250&layout=s |title=Videomäng rõőmuks kogu perele}}</ref> Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Very Severe" (50%-100%).<ref name=special301 />

===Belarus===
One of the first clones that arrived to Belarus was ''Zhiliton''. Later, the ''Dendy'' was released, which was the most popular clone in this region.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sb.by/articles/igra-s-pristavkoy.html|title=Игра с приставкой|first=СБ-Беларусь|last=сегодня|date=October 12, 2013|website=www.sb.by|access-date=June 22, 2020|archive-date=June 25, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200625155241/https://www.sb.by/articles/igra-s-pristavkoy.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1994, Steepler, the producer of ''Dendy'', reached an agreement with Nintendo to sell consoles in Russia and CIS countries with relinquished its claim to Dendy sales,<ref name=secretmag>{{cite web | url=https://secretmag.ru/business/trade-secret/nintendo-so-slonom-kak-viktor-savyuk-pridumal-pristavku-dendy.htm | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142332/https://secretmag.ru/business/trade-secret/nintendo-so-slonom-kak-viktor-savyuk-pridumal-pristavku-dendy.htm | archive-date=2018-06-12 | title=Приставка Dendy: Как Виктор Савюк придумал первый в России поп-гаджет }}</ref> meaning that Nintendo did not take legal action against famiclones. Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Very Severe" (50%-100%).<ref name=special301 />

On April 18, 2025, the Belarusian government banned the import of the Dendy Junior DJ-300, one of the Russian clones of the original Dendy, due to the risk of electric shock.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telepolis.pl/tech/sprzet/bialorus-konsola-dendy-blokada|title=Białoruś zbanowała rosyjski sprzęt. "Stwarza poważne ryzyko"|website=www.telepolis.pl}}</ref>

===Benelux Union===
According to Special 301 Watch List from 1994, Benelux shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems were classified as "Severe" (25%-50%). Famiclones sold in region were Mastergames Super Com SP-72, replaced in the early 2000s by educational computers. Mastergames proudly wrote to retailers around the Europe, about selling 200,000 units only for 1 year in Germany, Benelux, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Switzerland, Austria, Greece, Algeria without trouble from Nintendo. Regional distributors worked with police and custom service to search for clone retailers.<ref name=special301 />

===Brazil===
[[File:D NQ NP 780030-MLB42114945360 062020-O.jpg|thumb|300px|Magic Computer PC-95 was released in 1995 by Dynacom as an attempt to attract players bored with 8-bit generation.]]
Since 1989, Famicom- and NES-compatible consoles were made and sold in Brazil by local companies, some of which also imported and sold original NES cartridges and consoles. The first Famicom-compatible system, called ''Dynavision 2'', was released in 1989 by Dynacom and used joysticks similar to the [[Atari 2600]].<ref name=":0" /> The next system, ''Dynavision 3'', had gamepads similar to [[Sega Mega Drive]] gamepads and had a dual slot that allowed both 60-pin and 72-pin cartridges. This was followed in the mid-1990s by ''Handyvision'', a portable system that allowed video to be broadcast to the TV with a UHF transmitter.<ref name=":0" /> Another company, Geniecom, produced a black-colored clone with headphone jacks on gamepads, and Game Genie code input. The ''NASA'' clone was similar to the original NES, but had two slots, a 72-pin on the front and a 60-pin on top. Brazilian manufacturers also produced cartridges, but ran into the problem of having two formats. Hydron company solved the issue by making two-sided cartridges - one side 60-pin, the other 72-pin.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=2021 |title=N.21 На другой стороне Земли |trans-title=N.21 On the Other Side of the Earth |journal=DF Mag. Журнал о ретро-играх. |type=magazine |language=ru |pages=73–74}}</ref>

In 1993, Nintendo themselves arrived in Brazil and released the NES with the American cartridge slot. This official version was manufactured by [[Playtronic]], a [[joint venture]] between the toy company [[Estrela (company)|Estrela]] and Gradiente.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.xda-developers.com/nes-gradiente-phantom-system/|title=The NES Gradiente Phantom System and the fight for access in Brazil's gaming underground|first=Benjamin|last=Zeman|date=April 1, 2025|website=XDA}}</ref> Nintendo worked with customs service from Brazil to stop imports of famiclones and took legal actions against clones distributors. Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Moderate" (10%-25%).<ref name=special301 />

''PolyStation'', another popular clone was distributed from 2000 by [[West]]ern businessman Ali Ahmad Zaioum, of [[Paraguayan]]-[[Lebanese people|Lebanese]] origin. He also owns around 400 patents and trademarks supposedly created by him.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2009 |title=Sony denuncia 'mega inventor' da fronteira que criou o Poly Station |url=https://www.douradosnews.com.br/noticias/sony-denuncia-mega-inventor-da-fronteira-que-criou-o-poly-station-6ed8/374193/ |access-date=2024-09-29 |website=Dourados News |language=pt-br}}</ref> However, he was accused by the Paraguayan court of falsifying documents and information in order to obtain registration with the [[Politics of Paraguay|Ministry of Industry and Commerce of Paraguay]].<ref name="tecmundo">{{cite web |last=Góis |first=Aléxis Cerqueira |date=27 March 2022 |title=PolyStation: conheça o videogame que decepcionou muita criança |url=https://www.tecmundo.com.br/voxel/235962-polystation-conheca-videogame-decepcionou-crianca.htm |access-date=27 January 2023 |website=Tecmundo |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

=== Caribbean ===
Though the official NES was distributed in most [[List of sovereign states and dependent territories in the Caribbean|Caribbean countries]] by Inversiones St. John c/o Itochu De Venezuela,<ref name=ctw386 /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Nintendo: International Distributors |url=http://www.nintendo.com/corp/companies/venezuela.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/19980610031732/http://www.nintendo.com/corp/companies/venezuela.html |archive-date=1998-06-10 |access-date=2025-08-24 |website=www.nintendo.com}}</ref> the ''Family'' clones were popular for those who could not afford it.

===Colombia===
In Colombia consoles named ''Creation'', ''Super Creation'', ''Nichi-man'' (manufactured by [[Micro Genius]]) and later on ''PolyStation'' were popular. Nintendo arrived in Colombia in the early 1990s with help of ab compufax.<ref>{{cite journal |title= Nintendo Va Contigo | journal = Club Nintendo | issue= 8/2 |pages= 2 |url=https://archive.org/details/club-nintendo-11-ano-02-no-08-colombia/page/n1/mode/2up}}</ref> Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Limited" (5%-10%).<ref name=special301 />

Also, a recent famiclone, and of the [[Nintendo Switch]], is the ''Nanica Smitch''. It has 800 [[NES]] games built in, and has removable controllers, but the controllers look like [[Joy-Con]], but instead the thumbsticks are replaced with d-pads. It was also sold as the ''Game Magic''. However, this famiclone is available just in Colombia.

===Czech Republic/Slovakia===
Most known clones sold in this country are [[Terminator 2 (console)|''Terminator 2'']], ''Bel Game'', ''PolyStation'', ''Pegasus IQ-502'', ''Video Game-GT3300'' and ''[[Micro Genius]]''.<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url=https://www.oldgames.sk/images/magazine/score/1995/22/score22-074.jpg|title=Photo|website=www.oldgames.sk|format=PDF|access-date=2020-12-12|archive-date=2022-11-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126234735/https://www.oldgames.sk/images/magazine/score/1995/22/score22-074.jpg|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{cite web|url=https://www.oldgames.sk/images/magazine/level/1995/05/level5-037.jpg|title=Photo|website=oldgames.sk|access-date=2020-12-12|archive-date=2022-11-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126234737/https://www.oldgames.sk/images/magazine/level/1995/05/level5-037.jpg|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite magazine|date=4 November 1994|title=Prodejna Atelier nabizi pocitacove hry Micro Genius|issue=5/39|magazine=ABC|publisher=Czech News Center}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hrej.cz/article/dejte-mi-jedno-polystation-pane-stankar|title=Dejte mi jedno Polystation, pane stánkař|date=November 26, 2009|website=Hrej.cz}}</ref> Nintendo entered [[Czechoslovakia|Czechoslovak]] market in 1992 with Game Boy,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Nintendo Game Boy | journal = BiT | issue= 12/92 |page= 7 |url=https://www.oldgames.sk/mag/bit-15/page/7/}}</ref> and in the next year, after split into two countries, Nintendo released SNES and NES.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Nintendo | journal = Excalibur | issue= 18 |page= 32 |url=https://www.oldgames.sk/mag/excalibur-18/page/32/}}</ref> It is unknown if distributor took legal actions against famiclones resellers. Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Moderate" (10%-25%).<ref name=special301 />

===Denmark===
In the mid-90s, many Danish markets sold Mastergames Super Com SP-72, but as in other Western countries, Nintendo quickly tracked down the distributors, sued them, and won in 1996. Most of the stock was destroyed by a [[bulldozer]] and the event was broadcast on TV as a warning to other pirates.<ref name=nesworld /> Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Limited" (5%-10%).<ref name=special301 />

=== Egypt ===
Originally, famiclones sold in Egypt were the same as the ones sold on the Arabian Peninsula primarily the ''Rinco Home Computer 3600''. Many games by [[Thin Chen Enterprise|Sachen]] were sold there, as well as in other parts of [[North Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-11-22 |title=Famicom in the Middle East |url=https://fcgamer.wordpress.com/2014/11/22/famicom-in-the-middle-east/ |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=FC Game Land |language=en}}</ref> Later on, famiclones designed to look like later generation consoles such as the ''[[PlayStation]]'' series began to be sold. There were also ones designed to look like home computers. These were often packed with multicarts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sketcz |title=Videogames of Egypt |url=http://blog.hardcoregaming101.net/2010/03/videogames-of-egypt.html |access-date=2025-03-04}}</ref>

===Finland===
Some of the games shops marketed a few famiclones with yellow carts like [[Terminator 2 (console)|''Terminator 2'']]<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|url=http://ultimateconsoledatabase.com/famiclones/endingmans7000.htm|title=Ending Man S-700 - Ultimate Console Database at ultimateconsoledatabase.com|website=ultimateconsoledatabase.com|access-date=2023-03-24|archive-date=2021-06-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613203623/http://ultimateconsoledatabase.com/famiclones/endingmans7000.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> or promoted unlicensed NES games like [[Action 52]].<ref>{{cite journal |title= Action 52 | journal = Com Club  | issue= 1992–06 |pages= 26–27 |url=https://archive.org/details/comclub199206/page/n25/mode/2up}}</ref> Nintendo took legal actions against distributors, and in 1994 the biggest seller of pirate games and consoles had to pay damages of $75,000.<ref>{{cite journal |title= Wieści ze świata grania | journal = Top Secret | issue= 33 |pages= 57 |url=https://archive.org/details/TopSecret33/page/n56/mode/1up}}</ref> Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Moderate" (10%-25%).<ref name=special301 />

Some misunderstanding was also caused by a joke article on April 1 in a Finnish and Swedish magazine about the new Scandinavian console called ''Viking X'', whose design was taken from the Micro Genius IQ-301, which is why some journalists believed it to be real.<ref>{{cite journal |title= VIKING X YLLÄTTÄÄ! | journal = Super Power | issue= 1995–04 |pages= 10 |url=https://archive.org/details/super-power-1995.04/page/n9/mode/1up}}</ref>

===Germany/Austria/Switzerland===
Few famiclones were released in the region like ''VidiTex VT-720'', sold by Ultra-Sat Vierhaus and Master Games Super Com SP-72.<ref>{{cite journal |title= VidiTex VT-720 | journal = Video Games | issue= 2/92 |pages= 34}}</ref><ref name=special301 /> Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified markets shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Moderate" (10%-25%).<ref name=special301 />

===Greater China===
[[File:小霸王学习机 SB-486D 正面.jpg|thumb|300px|Subor SB-486D]]
The market of People's Republic of China opened to the console in the late 1980s, but high customs made imported consoles such as the Famicom very expensive. This is why local companies began producing cheaper clones which created a large grey market for unlicensed consoles and games.<ref name="china history">{{cite journal | title = Japanese Console Games Popularization in China: Governance, Copycats, and Gamers | first1 = Sara X. T. | last1 = Liao | date = 2015 | doi = 10.1177/1555412015583574 | journal = [[Games and Culture]] | volume = 11 | issue = 3 | pages = 275–297 | s2cid = 147283833 | url = http://www.com.cuhk.edu.hk/images/content_people/publication/sara-journal-2016-japanese.pdf | access-date = September 20, 2019 }}</ref> Counterfeit Nintendo was sold in great quantities primarily in large cites of Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, and cities of Guandong Province. In 1994, Beijing was the place where more than 10,000 stores sold famiclones and 50% of families used to have one. Some of the stores claimed that record sales were 10,000 units of cartridges in just one day. At that time, there were already factories producing clones of Game Boy games and consoles, and the first cases of pirated games for the Super Nintendo.<ref name=special301 />

One of the most popular was ''Xiǎo Bàwáng'' or ''Little Bawang'' ([[Chinese language|Chinese]]: 小霸王; <small>[[Literal translation|lit.]]</small> 'Little Emperor or Little Tyrant') by [[Subor]], which claimed to be one of the largest producers of video games in China.<ref name=":3">{{cite web|url=https://news.17173.com/content/2012-11-28/20121128093357374.shtml |title=从巅峰到没落 小霸王做过的电子产品 |date=28 November 2012 |work=17173 |access-date=16 February 2022 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170218063136/http://news.17173.com/content/2012-11-28/20121128093357374.shtml |archive-date=18 February 2017 }}</ref> They marketed ''Super Mario Bros'' as ''Super Brothers II'', and ''Tetris'' as ''Russian Bricks II''. Another company called New Star, also claimed to be market leader with 15% shares of the Chinese market, largest distribution network of 300 retailers and more than 300 cartridges. Many brands and producers existed like Nanbeng Co. Ltd, Jichang Electronics Co., Ltd and more. Most of the local manufacturers began distributing console to other countries, which made China one of main hubs of famiclone production.<ref name=special301 /> Certain models were officially advertised by [[Jackie Chan]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2020/11/chinese_firm_which_ripped_off_the_nes_with_jackie_chans_help_has_filed_for_bankruptcy | title=Chinese Firm Which Ripped off the NES with Jackie Chan's Help Has Filed for Bankruptcy | date=11 November 2020 }}</ref>

Nintendo saw the market potential and decided to enter China in 1994, with Game Boy and Super Nintendo but it did not include NES, because according to company it was commercially impossible to market it. Due to lack copyright enforcements and border control it could not fight piracy.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://user.guancha.cn/main/content?id=153053 | title=25年后，任天堂仍然想打通"中国"这一关_风闻 }}</ref> Until late 1993, pirates manage to sell 20 million units of all type of famiclones across China and by late 1995, the number increased to 30 million.<ref>{{citation | url=https://archive.org/details/game-software-93-02/%E7%94%B5%E5%AD%90%E6%B8%B8%E6%88%8F%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B696%E4%B8%8B%E5%8D%8A%E5%B9%B4%E5%90%88%E8%AE%A2%E6%9C%AC/page/n170/mode/1up?view=theater | magazine=Game Software |title=中国软件行业协会电子游戏机分会秘书长 | issue=9/1996 |page=2}}</ref> China was one of the countries on Special 301 Watch List from 1994 due to huge intellectual property issue and authors of the report classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Very Severe" (50%-100%).<ref name=special301 />

The popularity of these devices continued in the People's Republic of China in the 2000s, due to the fact that in June 2000, the Chinese government decided to ban all video game consoles.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ign.com.cn/jiketang/33161/opinion/zou-jin-zhong-guo-jia-yong-you-xi-ji-bo-wu-guan-ji-ke-tang | title=Zou jin zhong guo jiayong-you xi ji bo wu guan ji ke tan | date=21 June 2021 }}</ref> Since the mid-1990s Chinese manufacturers have been selling the latest Famiclone models as an educational computer with a keyboard and a cartridge with simple educational games. It turned out Chinese authorities allowed the further sale of that devices, not recognizing it as console, which resulted in next clone models from other manufacturers as well as new unlicensed games, miscellaneous programmes like ''[[Windows 98]]'' or ports of newer games for 8-bit Nintendo such as ''[[Resident Evil]]'' (Bio Hazard), ''[[Tomb Raider]]'' or ''[[Final Fantasy VII]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lpoytsB5puc|title=Historia "Pegasusa z klawiaturą" -- GLK-2004 et al. &#124; (Mini) Time Warp|date=April 20, 2018|via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ews9PNEowKs|title=Final Fantasy VII... na NES-a?! -- Famicomowy Bootleg|date=June 7, 2016|via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.instalki.pl/news/rozrywka/podrabiany-windows-98-na-pegasusie-z-klawiatura-czego-to-chinczycy-nie-wymysla/ | title=Podrabiany Windows 98 na Pegasusie z klawiaturą. Czego to Chińczycy nie wymyślą | date=5 February 2021 }}</ref> The full number of clones and units sold in China is still unknown. At the same time, Nintendo adapted to new regulations and entered the market with remodeled consoles through [[iQue]].

In Taiwan, the Famicom had a limited release.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://consolevariations.com/collectibles/nintendo-famicom-console-tw | title=Nintendo Famicom Console &#91;TW&#93; | date=6 September 2021 }}</ref> Many companies, such as [[NTDEC]] or [[Micro Genius]], were established in Taiwan and sold famiclones locally and internationally. According to Special 301 Watch List from 1994, around 130 manufacturers and trading companies were breaking the law and next 70 was suspected of doing that. Many Taiwan producers move their assembly operations to Mainland China in order to import into the country key video game components. This made Taiwan one of the most important hubs for the production of clones. In order to stop it, Nintendo made dozen lawsuits against producers and retailers. It also tried to work with custom service, but system was not effective.<ref name="Nintendo of America Inc v. NTDEC">{{Cite web|url=https://openjurist.org/51/f3d/281|title=51 F.3d 281 - Nintendo of America Inc v. Ntdec|date=September 12, 1995|publisher=OpenJurist}}</ref><ref name=special301 />

Hong Kong had sold official Famicom consoles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.am730.com.hk/column/%E6%96%B0%E8%81%9E/%E9%9B%BB%E7%8E%A9%E5%A7%8B%E7%A5%96-%E7%B4%85%E7%99%BD%E4%B9%8B%E8%B7%AF-%E4%B8%AD-/213033|title=電玩始祖，紅白之路(中) &#124; am730 &#124; am730}}</ref> But piracy was spreading in the region because companies from China and Taiwan had sales agents or manufacturing plants. Infringement actions and support from customs services were present. Both Hong Kong and Taiwan were on the Special 301 Watch List from 1994 due to huge intellectual property issue and authors of the report classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Very Severe" (50%-100%).<ref name=special301 />

===Greece===
[[File:Supercom SP-72 Famiclone.jpg|thumb|300px|Super Com 72]]
From 1990, Greek Software marketed ''BIT 72'' and ''Redstone'' (which used NES cartridges) as a competitor to officially distributed [[Master System]].<ref name=pixel/><ref>{{cite journal |title=The Best Game Consoles | journal = User  | issue= 8 |pages=3 |url=https://archive.org/details/USER_08/page/n1/mode/2up}}</ref> In 1991, Nintendo entered the Greek market,<ref>{{cite journal | title= NINTENDO O KOSMOS TOU 2.000 | journal = Pixel | issue= 80 |pages= 34–39 |url=https://archive.org/details/pixel-gr-080/page/n33/mode/2up}}</ref> and took legal actions against importers, but clones were still sold in video game stores like ''Action Set - Family 52'' from 1991 by Computer Market,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Computer Market | journal = User  | issue= 18 |pages=4–5 |url=https://archive.org/details/USER_18/page/n3/mode/2up}}</ref> ''Crazy Boy'' distributed from 1993 by Multi Logi<ref>{{cite journal |title=Crazy Boy Entertainment | journal = User  | issue= 33 |pages=59 |url=https://archive.org/details/USER_33/page/n57/mode/2up}}</ref> and Mastergames Super Com SP-72. Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Severe" (25%-50%).<ref name=special301 />

===Hungary===
Nintendo entered the Hungarian market in 1991 with Game Boy and NES,<ref>{{cite book |last=Sheff |first=David |title=Game Over Press Start To Continue |year=1993 | publisher= Random House | chapter = Borders |pages= 416 }}</ref> and a lot of clones were referred to as ''Sárga Kazettás Nintendo'' (Yellow Casetted Nintendo).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://klikkout.sk/2017/01/06/a-legendas-sarga-kazettas-nintendo/ | title=A legendás sárga kazettás Nintendo &#124; Klikkout | date=6 January 2017 | access-date=22 March 2023 | archive-date=22 March 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230322163712/https://klikkout.sk/2017/01/06/a-legendas-sarga-kazettas-nintendo/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

===Iceland===
Nintendo was in this region from the early 1980s,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://timarit.is/page/4019489?iabr=on#page/n3/mode/2up/search/nintendo | title=Tíminn - 251. Tölublað (04.11.1982) - Tímarit.is | access-date=2023-03-19 | archive-date=2023-03-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319195718/https://timarit.is/page/4019489?iabr=on#page/n3/mode/2up/search/nintendo | url-status=live }}</ref> but stores distributed clones like ''Crazyboy'',<ref>{{cite web | url=https://timarit.is/page/3535435?iabr=on#page/n23/mode/2up/search/crazyboy | title=Pressan - Jólagjafahandbók (12.12.1991) - Tímarit.is | access-date=2023-03-19 | archive-date=2023-03-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319195722/https://timarit.is/page/3535435?iabr=on#page/n23/mode/2up/search/crazyboy | url-status=live }}</ref> ''Redstone'',<ref>{{cite web | url=https://timarit.is/page/2592187?iabr=on#page/n43/mode/2up/search/redstone | title=Dagblaðið Vísir - DV - Jólagjafahandbók (04.12.1991) - Tímarit.is | access-date=2023-03-19 | archive-date=2023-03-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319195720/https://timarit.is/page/2592187?iabr=on#page/n43/mode/2up/search/redstone | url-status=live }}</ref> ''NASA'' (compatible with NES),<ref name=":8">{{cite web | url=https://timarit.is/page/2592145?iabr=on#page/n1/mode/1up/search/nasa%20nintendo | title=Dagblaðið Vísir - DV - Jólagjafahandbók (04.12.1991) - Tímarit.is | access-date=2023-03-19 | archive-date=2023-03-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319195716/https://timarit.is/page/2592145?iabr=on#page/n1/mode/1up/search/nasa%20nintendo | url-status=live }}</ref> ''Action Set'',<ref>{{cite web | url=https://timarit.is/page/2608697?iabr=on#page/n41/mode/2up/search/nintendo | title=Dagblaðið Vísir - DV - 30. Tölublað - Helgarblað (06.02.1993) - Tímarit.is | access-date=2023-03-19 | archive-date=2023-03-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319195719/https://timarit.is/page/2608697?iabr=on#page/n41/mode/2up/search/nintendo | url-status=live }}</ref> ''NTDEC''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://timarit.is/page/1756674?iabr=on#page/n39/mode/2up/search/NTDEC | title=Morgunblaðið - 291. Tölublað (20.12.1991) - Tímarit.is | access-date=2023-03-19 | archive-date=2023-03-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319201328/https://timarit.is/page/1756674?iabr=on#page/n39/mode/2up/search/NTDEC | url-status=live }}</ref> etc. Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Moderate" (10%-25%).<ref name=special301 />

===India===
In 1987, Nintendo released the NES under the name [[Samurai Electronic TV Game System|Samurai]] marketed by Samurai Electronics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rediff.com/getahead/2008/sep/16wii.htm|title=Nintendo Wii and DS to launch in India|website=www.rediff.com|access-date=2020-08-02|archive-date=2022-09-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929140516/https://www.rediff.com/getahead/2008/sep/16wii.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> According to company owner Mahesh Toshniwal, despite initially good sales, China and Taiwan introduced clone consoles, priced 25% lower than Samurai, and multicarts priced 10% lower than games. Sales went down, and Samurai initiated legal action against the "Samurai" Micro Genius and informed Nintendo representatives, which did not made it better due to poor Indian law, resulting official NES sales dying out in 1993. Another version of events claims that Samurai registered the Micro Genius name by itself in 1991 and sold the clones as its own alongside the legitimate NES, but Mahesh Toshniwal refused to confirm this.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RTESo86hD98 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/RTESo86hD98 |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|title=Video |website=www.youtube.com |date=April 2015 |access-date=2020-12-12}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/video-game-history-around-world-essay-joshua-rogers|title=Video Game History Around The World: An Essay.|website=www.linkedin.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://romchip.org/index.php/romchip-journal/article/view/143|title=The Bootleg Connection: Micro Genius and the Transnational Circulation of Early Clone Consoles|first=Ian|last=Larson|date=July 29, 2022|journal=ROMchip|volume=4|issue=1|via=romchip.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://imgur.com/0BbAk6W |title=Interview with Mahesh Toshniwal (extract) | archive-url=https://archive.today/20250930172016/https://imgur.com/0BbAk6W | archive-date=2025-09-30}}</ref> This opinion can be supported by the fact that in 2008, Samurai would return in cooperation from HCL Infosystems as Nintendo dealer of Nintendo Wii and DS.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.indianvideogamer.com/news/first-party-wii-and-ds-games-will-be-available-in-india/201 |title=First-party Wii and DS games will be available in India}}</ref> It was not the first time when Nintendo cooperated with bootleg distributors in India. From 1994, Super Nintendo and Game Boy were officially distributed by Media Video (known from "Media" 8-bit clones)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://segaretro.org/History_of_Sega_in_India |title=History of Sega in India}}</ref> and from 2013 to 2017, Nintendo 3DS and WiiU were supplied by Sunder Electronics (manufacturer of "Sameo" famiclones), which until 2026 was last official Nintendo distributor in India.<ref name=sunderaboutus>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sunderelectronics.com/about-us.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130824010947/http://www.sunderelectronics.com/about-us.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-08-24 |title=Sunder Electronics - About Us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.gadgets360.com/games/features/buy-the-nintendo-switch-in-india-you-need-to-read-this-first-1650812 |title=Want to Buy the Nintendo Switch In India? You Need to Read This First}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.techinasia.com/asia-exclusive-white-mario-3ds-xl-coming-your-way-soon-we-hope |title=Asia-exclusive white Mario 3DS XL coming your way soon! (UPDATED)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gonintendo.com/contents/64485-nintendo-hosting-first-ever-event-in-india |title=Nintendo hosting first-ever event in India (UPDATE)}}</ref>

In the 1990s, the demand for 8-bit clones was very high in India. There were around 55 brands in the country at the time such as Media Entertainment System (selling ''Little Master'' and ''Wiz Kid''), Mitashi (selling ''Cricket''), Mega, Sameo and others.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|url=https://gadgets.ndtv.com/games/features/tracing-the-origins-of-gaming-in-india-8-bit-cricket-sega-and-cloning-640129|title=Tracing the Origins of Gaming in India: 8-Bit Cricket, Sega, and Cloning|website=NDTV Gadgets 360|date=26 December 2014|access-date=2 August 2020|archive-date=23 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023185036/https://gadgets.ndtv.com/games/features/tracing-the-origins-of-gaming-in-india-8-bit-cricket-sega-and-cloning-640129|url-status=live}}</ref><<ref name=sunderaboutus />

===Indonesia===
Many famiclones from various producers, compatible with NES or Famicom, were rebranded and sold by Spica.<ref>{{cite web |title=Image |url=https://images.tokopedia.net/img/cache/900/VqbcmM/2021/9/5/6cbabf27-11bc-46fc-91b4-efb7cd7317ed.jpg |website=Tokopedia |access-date=19 May 2023 |archive-date=22 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230322212340/https://images.tokopedia.net/img/cache/900/VqbcmM/2021/9/5/6cbabf27-11bc-46fc-91b4-efb7cd7317ed.jpg |url-status=live }}</ref> Special 301 Watch List from 1994 classified market shares of counterfeit 8-bit systems as "Moderate" (10%-25%).<ref name=special301 />

===Iran===
