2021|archive-date=May 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508104737/https://culturedvultures.com/best-roguelikes-roguelites-games/|url-status=live}}</ref>

McMillen later worked with James Id to develop ''[[The Legend of Bum-bo]]'', which serves as a [[prequel]] to ''The Binding of Isaac''.

''The Binding of Isaac'' has been well-received, with critics praising the game's roguelike nature to encourage repeated playthroughs. By July 2014, McMillen reported over 3 million copies had been sold. The game has been said to contribute to renewed interest in the roguelike genre from both players and developers.

== Gameplay ==
[[File:The Binding of Isaac screenshot.png|thumb|left|Gameplay screenshot of ''The Binding of Isaac'', showing Isaac attacking (center) and two enemies (top left and top right)]]

''The Binding of Isaac'' is a [[Video game graphics#Top-down perspective|top-down]] [[dungeon crawl]]er game, presented using [[Sprite (computer graphics)|two-dimensional sprites]], in which the player controls Isaac or other unlockable characters as they explore the dungeons located in Isaac's basement. The characters differ in speed, amount of health, amount of damage they deal, and other attributes.<ref name="gamespot review"/> The game's mechanics and presentation is similar to the dungeons of ''[[The Legend of Zelda (video game)|The Legend of Zelda]]'', while incorporating random, [[procedural generation|procedurally-generated]] levels in the manner of a [[roguelike]] game.<ref name="wired">{{cite magazine | url = https://www.wired.com/gamelife/2011/09/binding-of-isaac/ |title = Nightmarish Indie The Binding of Isaac Shooting Up Steam Next Week | date = September 19, 2011 | access-date = December 23, 2015 | first = Jason | last = Scheirer | magazine = [[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] }}</ref> On each floor of the basement dungeon, the player must fight monsters in a room before continuing onto the next room. This is most commonly done by the character's tears as bullets in the style of a [[twin-stick shooter]], but the player can also use a limited supply of bombs to damage enemies and clear out parts of the room.<ref name="gamespot review"/> Other methods of defeating enemies become possible as the character gains [[power-up]]s, items that are automatically worn by the player-character when picked up that can alter the character's core attributes, such as increasing health or the strength of each tear, or cause additional side effects, such as for allowing charged tear shots to be fired after holding down a controller button for a short while, or a means to fire tears behind the character. Power-ups include passive items that improve the character's attributes automatically, active power-ups that can be used once before they are recharged by completing additional rooms in the dungeon, and single-use power-ups such as pills or [[Tarot]] cards that confer a one-time benefit when used, such as regaining full health, or increasing or decreasing all attributes of the character. The effect of power-ups stack, so that the player may come into highly-beneficial power-up combinations.<ref name="gamespot review"/><ref name="pcgamer review">{{cite web | url = http://www.pcgamer.com/the-binding-of-isaac-review/ | title = The Binding of Isaac Review | first = Chris | last = Thursten | date = December 17, 2011 | access-date = April 25, 2016 | work = [[PC Gamer]] | archive-date = August 23, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170823020308/http://www.pcgamer.com/the-binding-of-isaac-review/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

Once a room is cleared of monsters, it will remain clear, allowing the player to re-trace their way through the level, though once they move onto the next level, they cannot return. Along the way, the player can collect money to buy power-ups from shopkeepers, keys to unlock special treasure rooms, and new weapons and power-ups to strengthen their chances against the enemies. The player's health is tracked by a number of hearts; if the character loses all his hearts, the game ends in [[permanent death|permadeath]] and the player must start over from a freshly-generated dungeon. Each floor of the dungeon includes a [[boss (video game)|boss]] which the player must defeat before continuing to the next level.<ref name="pcgamer review"/> On the sixth of eight floors, the player fights Isaac's mother; after defeating her, Isaac crawls into her womb. Later levels are significantly harder, culminating in a fight against the heart of Isaac's mother on the eighth floor. An optional ninth floor, [[Sheol]], contains the boss [[Satan]]. Winning the game with certain characters or by certain conditions unlocks new power-ups that might appear in the dungeon or the ability to use one of the other characters. The game tracks the various power-ups that the player has found over time which can be reviewed from the game's menus.<ref name="gamespot review"/>

== Plot ==
{{Main|The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth#Plot}}

''The Binding of Isaac''{{'}}s plot is very loosely inspired by the [[Binding of Isaac|biblical story of the same name]].<ref name="postmortem"/> Isaac, a child, and his mother live in a small house on a hill, happily keeping to themselves, with Isaac drawing pictures and playing with his toys, and his mother watching Christian broadcasts on television.

One day, Isaac's mother hears "a voice from above," which she believes is that of God Himself. The voice states that her son, Isaac, is "corrupted with sin and needs to be saved." It asks her to remove all evil from Isaac, and his mother agrees, taking away his toys, drawings, and even his clothes. The voice speaks to Isaac's mother for a second time, stating that Isaac must be cut off from all that is evil in the world. Once again, his mother agrees and locks Isaac inside his room. For the last time, the voice speaks to Isaac's mother. It states that she has done well, but it still questions her devotion and tells her to sacrifice her son. She agrees, grabs a butcher's knife from the kitchen, and walks to Isaac's room, preparing to sacrifice him. Isaac, watching through a sizable crack in his door, starts to panic. He finds a trapdoor hidden under his rug and jumps in, just as his mother bursts through his bedroom door. It is then assumed that the start of every new run is just after Isaac jumps down into the trapdoor.

Until ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth#Repentance|The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]'' expansion in the [[The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth|remake]], there is no clear conclusion, or even consistent narrative, to the story past this point. The original game features 13 possible endings, one after each major boss fight. The first ten endings serve as introductions to unlocked items and mechanics, while the final three suggest meaningful evidence to understanding the conclusion (although this is not revealed until a new game and three DLCs later).

During the game's cutscenes through two levels, or floors, Isaac is shown curled up in a ball, crying. His thoughts are visible, ranging from rejection from his mother and humiliation from his peers to a scenario involving his death.

== Development and release ==
[[File:Edmund McMillen 2012 portrait.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Edmund McMillen in 2012]]
''The Binding of Isaac'' was developed following the release of ''[[Super Meat Boy]]'', which McMillen considered a significant risk and a large time effort. When ''Super Meat Boy'' was released to both critical praise and strong sales, he felt that he no longer had to worry about the consequences of taking risks with his finances supported by its sales. He also considered he could take further risk with the concept.<ref name="postmortem"/> He had been planning to work with [[Tommy Refenes]], the co-developer of ''Super Meat Boy'', on their next game, ''[[Mewgenics]]'', but as Refenes had taken some time off, McMillen looked to develop something he considered to be "low stress" with minimal expectations such as an [[Adobe Flash]] game.<ref name="escapist 2021 interview"/>

''The Binding of Isaac''{{'}}s main concept was the result of a weeklong game jam that McMillen had with Florian Himsl; at the time, his co-contributor on ''Super Meat Boy'', Tommy Refenes, was on vacation. The concept McMillen had was two-fold: to develop a [[roguelike]] title based on the first ''[[The Legend of Zelda (video game)|The Legend of Zelda]]'' game's dungeon structure, and to develop a game that addressed McMillen's thoughts on religion.<ref name="postmortem">{{cite web | url = http://gamasutra.com/view/feature/182380/postmortem_mcmillen_and_himsls_.php | title = Postmortem: McMillen and Himsl's The Binding of Isaac | first = Edmund | last = McMillen | date = November 28, 2012 | access-date = December 20, 2015 | work = [[Gamasutra]] | archive-date = August 23, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170823204135/http://gamasutra.com/view/feature/182380/postmortem_mcmillen_and_himsls_.php | url-status = dead }}</ref> McMillen had been inspired by [[Shigeru Miyamoto]], the designer of the original ''Zelda'' games.<ref name="goodtimes"/> McMillen saw the potential of the procedural generation aspect of roguelikes including in ''[[Spelunky]]'' and ''[[Desktop Dungeons]]'', and considered that working on procedural generation would help towards development of his planned game ''Mewgenics''.<ref name="escapist 2021 interview">{{cite video | url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-X_QYumQQGk | title = Edmund McMillen on The Making of The Binding of Isaac, The Legend of Bum-Bo & More | date = February 20, 2021 | access-date = August 11, 2021 | time = 15:30 | author = [[The Escapist (magazine)|The Escapist]] }}</ref>
McMillen compares Isaac's controls to the game ''[[Smash TV]]''.<ref name="VentureBeat 2011 interview">{{cite web | url = https://venturebeat.com/community/2011/09/02/interview-with-team-meats-edmund-mcmillen/ | title = The Binding of Isaac: Interview with Team Meat's Edmund McMillen | date = September 2, 2011 | access-date = August 11, 2021 | time = 1:27 PM | author = Rachel Jagielski [[VentureBeat]] }}</ref>

Random rooms were created for each floor of the dungeon by selecting ten to twenty rooms from a pre-built library of 200 layouts, adding in the monsters, items, and other features, and then including fixed rooms that would be found on each floor, such as a boss room and treasure room.<ref name="vb"/> In expanding the gameplay, McMillen used the structure of ''Zelda''{{'}}s dungeons to design how the player would progress through the game. In a typical ''Zelda'' dungeon, according to McMillen, the player acquires a new item that helps them to progress farther in the game; he took the same inspiration to assure that each level in ''Isaac'' included at least one item and one bonus item on defeating the boss that would boost the character's attributes.<ref name="postmortem"/> McMillen also wanted to encourage players to experiment to learn how things work within ''Isaac'', mirroring how Miyamoto had done with the original ''Zelda'' game.<ref name="postmortem"/> He designed the level progression to become more difficult with the player's progression in the game, as well as additional content that became available after beating the game as to make it feel like the game was long.<ref name="postmortem"/> McMillen designed four of the selectable characters based on the main classes of ''[[Dungeons & Dragons]]''—fighter, thief, cleric and wizard.<ref name="wired"/><ref name="dtoid july2011"/><ref>{{cite web | url = http://edmundmcmillen.blogspot.com/2011/09/progression.html | title = Progression? | first = Edmund | last = McMillen | date = September 17, 2011 | access-date = April 25, 2016 | publisher = [[Blogspot]] | archive-date = October 11, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161011181613/http://edmundmcmillen.blogspot.com/2011/09/progression.html | url-status = live }}</ref>

On the story side, McMillen explained that the religious tone is based on his own experiences with his family, split between Catholics and born-again Christians.<ref name="postmortem"/> McMillen noted that while both sides born out faith from the same Bible, their attitudes were different; he found some of the Catholic rituals his family performed inspiring, while other beliefs they had were condemning of several pastimes McMillen had participated in like ''Dungeons & Dragons''.<ref name="postmortem"/> He took inspiration from that duality to create ''Isaac''{{'}}s narrative, showing how religion can both instill harmful feelings while also bringing about dark creativity.<ref name="postmortem"/> McMillen also considered the scare tactics used by the [[Christian right]] to condemn popular media of the 1980s, such as [[heavy metal music|heavy metal]] and video games.<ref name="dtoid july2011">{{cite web | url = http://www.destructoid.com/how-a-killer-christian-shmup-roguelike-came-to-steam-206601.phtml | title = How a killer Christian shmup roguelike came to Steam | work = [[Destructoid]] | first = Jonathan | last = Holmes | date = July 21, 2011 | access-date = April 25, 2016 | archive-date = May 8, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160508231437/http://www.destructoid.com/how-a-killer-christian-shmup-roguelike-came-to-steam-206601.phtml | url-status = live }}</ref> McMillen noted how many of the propaganda films from this period featured satanic cults that would sacrifice children, and he noted how many Biblical stories mirrored these concepts, subsequently building the story around that.<ref name="vb">{{Cite web | url = https://venturebeat.com/community/2011/09/02/interview-with-team-meats-edmund-mcmillen/ | title = The Binding of Isaac: Interview with Team Meat's Edmund McMillen | first = Rachel | last = Jagielski | date = September 2, 2011 | access-date = April 25, 2016 | work = [[VentureBeat]] | archive-date = August 23, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170823211115/https://venturebeat.com/community/2011/09/02/interview-with-team-meats-edmund-mcmillen/ | url-status = live }}</ref> He also stated that he also tended to like "really weird stuff" relating to [[Toilet humour|toilet humor]] and similar types of [[off-color humor]] that did not sit well with his family and which he had explored in previous games before ''Super Meat Boy''.<ref name="eurogamer">{{Cite web | url = http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2012-06-29-the-binding-of-edmund-mcmillen | title = The Binding of Edmund McMillen | date = June 26, 2012 | access-date = December 20, 2015 | first = Nathan | last = Grayson | work = [[Eurogamer]] | archive-date = December 22, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151222123017/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2012-06-29-the-binding-of-edmund-mcmillen | url-status = live }}</ref> While ''Super Meat Boy'' helped to make his reputation (including being one of the featured developers in ''[[Indie Game: The Movie]]''), he felt it was a "safe" game considering his preferred type of humor, and used ''Isaac'' to return to this form, considering that the game could easily be "career suicide" but would make a statement about what he really wanted to do.<ref name="eurogamer"/>

''The Binding of Isaac'' began as a game jam between McMillen and Florian Himsl. Within the week, they had a working game written in [[Adobe Flash]]'s [[ActionScript]] 2. The two agreed to complete it out as a game they could release on [[Steam (service)|Steam]] though with no expectations of sales. Completion of the game from the prototype to the finished state took about 3 months with part-time development.<ref name="postmortem"/> During this time, they discovered there were several limitations on the size and scope of both Flash and ActionScript that limited how much they could do with the game, but continued to use the tools as to release the title.<ref name="postmortem"/> McMillen said that because they were not worried about sales, they were able to work with Valve to release the game without fears of censorship or having to seek an [[ESRB]] rating. Releasing through Steam also enabled them to update the game freely, several times on its initial release, an aspect that they could not do with other consoles without significant cost to themselves.<ref name="postmortem"/> They did release without significant end-user testing, as it would have taken several hundreds of users to go through all the various combinations of items that a player could collect, and McMillen recognized they had released the title with their buyers being playtesters for them.<ref name="postmortem"/> A week after the Steam release, McMillen released a [[game demo|demo]] version via the website ''[[Newgrounds]]''.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.cinemablend.com/games/Binding-Isaac-Demo-Released-Big-Update-Way-35870.html | title = The Binding Of Isaac Demo Released, Big Update On The Way | first = Pete | last = Haas | date = October 9, 2011 | access-date = December 23, 2015 | work = Cinema Blend | archive-date = December 23, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151223235801/http://www.cinemablend.com/games/Binding-Isaac-Demo-Released-Big-Update-Way-35870.html | url-status = live }}</ref> Merge Games produced a physical edition that included the game, soundtrack, and a poster, for stores in the United Kingdom in 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.destructoid.com/the-binding-of-isaac-gets-a-grotesque-retail-edition-220544.phtml | title = The Binding of Isaac gets a grotesque retail edition | first = Fraser | last = Brown | date = January 28, 2012 | access-date = May 10, 2016 | work = [[Destructoid]] | archive-date = August 5, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160805022115/https://www.destructoid.com/the-binding-of-isaac-gets-a-grotesque-retail-edition-220544.phtml | url-status = live }}</ref>

AS2 was a very outdated program at the time, and caused many low-end PCs and even high-end PCs to encounter slow down at times. AS2 also lacked controller support, and Tommy Refenes had to help write an achievement program that would allow people to unlock Steam achievements. McMillen later stated that he would not have made it in Flash at all if he had known anyone would actually care about ''Isaac''.<ref name="postmortem" />

=== Soundtrack ===
Danny Baranowsky, the game's composer and who previously worked with McMillen on ''Super Meat Boy'', was involved early on with the project shortly after the completion of the first prototype. McMillen and Baranowsky worked back and forth, with McMillen providing artwork from the game and allowing Baranowsky to develop the musical themes based on that; this would often lead to McMillen creating more art to support the music as it progressed. Baranowsky had been drawn to ''The Binding of Isaac'' as though the game puts forth a dark tone, he stated it had rather silly undertones underneath and such that one could not take it too seriously.<ref>{{cite magazine | url = https://www.gamesradar.com/binding-isaac-cave-story-3d-and-crying-poop-interview-composer-danny-b/ | title = The Binding of Isaac, Cave Story 3D, and crying at poop: an interview with composer Danny B | first = Hollander | last = Cooper | date = October 24, 2011 | access-date = April 25, 2016 | magazine = [[Games Radar]] }}</ref> Some of the songs were inspired by classical choral music but modified to fit the theme of the game. Other works were inspired by boss fight songs composed by [[Nobuo Uematsu]] for the ''[[Final Fantasy]]'' series.<ref name="kotaku soundtrack"/> Baranowsky also had additional time after finishing the main songs for the game to craft short additional tracks that were used for special rooms like shops and secret areas.<ref name="kotaku soundtrack">{{cite web | url = https://kotaku.com/the-best-game-music-of-2011-the-binding-of-isaac-5870347 | title = The Best Game Music of 2011: The Binding of Isaac | first = Kirk | last = Hamilton | date = December 22, 2011 | access-date = May 10, 2016 | work = [[Kotaku]] | archive-date = November 4, 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20181104144254/https://kotaku.com/5870347/the-best-game-music-of-2011-the-binding-of-isaac | url-status = live }}</ref>

=== Cancelled Nintendo 3DS port ===
In January 2012, as the game has surpassed 450,000 units sold, McMillen stated that he was approached by a publisher that had interest in bringing the title to the [[Nintendo 3DS]] as a downloadable title through the [[Nintendo eShop]], though McMillen had reservations given Nintendo's reputation for less risque content.<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.shacknews.com/article/71868/the-binding-of-isaac-mega-expansion-incoming | title = The Binding of Isaac 'mega expansion' incoming | first = Alice | last = O'Conner | date = January 6, 2012 | access-date = December 23, 2015 | work = [[Shacknews]] | archive-date = December 24, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151224000248/http://www.shacknews.com/article/71868/the-binding-of-isaac-mega-expansion-incoming | url-status = live }}</ref> In late February, McMillen stated that Nintendo had rejected the game because of "questionable religious content". He believed this stemmed from Germany's classification board rating the existing Windows version of the game as "age 16+" due to potentially [[Blasphemy|blasphemous]] content, the first such time a game was rated in that manner in the country.<ref>{{cite web|title=16er-Einstufung wegen... Blasphemie|url=http://www.4players.de/4players.php/spielinfonews/PC-CDROM/27752/2091117/The_Binding_of_Isaac16er-Einstufung_wegen_Blasphemie.html|date=January 4, 2012|access-date=February 9, 2012|language=de|trans-title=16 rating because of... blasphemy|archive-date=February 2, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120202200859/http://www.4players.de/4players.php/spielinfonews/PC-CDROM/27752/2091117/The_Binding_of_Isaac16er-Einstufung_wegen_Blasphemie.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="postmortem"/><ref name="3DS GI">{{cite web|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2012/02/29/binding-of-isaac-blocked-from-3ds-due-to-quot-questionable-religious-content-quot.aspx|title=Binding Of Isaac Blocked From 3DS Due To 'Questionable Religious Content'|publisher=[[Game Informer]]|first=Phil|last=Kollar|date=February 29, 2012|access-date=March 1, 2012|quote=''In a follow-up tweet, McMillen confirmed that the decision was "due to the games [''sic''] 'questionable religious content.' He then took the opportunity to praise Steam for being such an open and supporting platform for independent and digitally distributed games.''|archive-date=January 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102091546/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2012/02/29/binding-of-isaac-blocked-from-3ds-due-to-quot-questionable-religious-content-quot.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="3dsdestructoid">{{cite web|url=http://www.destructoid.com/nintendo-wont-allow-the-binding-of-isaac-on-the-3ds-eshop-222917.phtml|title=Nintendo won't allow Binding of Isaac on the 3DS eShop|publisher=[[Destructoid]]|date=February 29, 2012|access-date=February 29, 2012|quote=It's a disgusting and sad situation, and I can only hope that something is done soon to change the way both Nintendo, and the industry in general, views the role between the hardware developers and software artists. [...] "''All this stuff has opened my eyes so much more to the freedom devs have with Steam. Censorship like this doesn't pop up that often in games, and there are only a handful of "banned video games" or highly censored ones. It's nice to have the freedom to publish something that speaks its mind about religion on a platform like Steam.''"|archive-date=October 25, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141025075924/http://www.destructoid.com/nintendo-wont-allow-the-binding-of-isaac-on-the-3ds-eshop-222917.phtml|url-status=dead|author-first1=Jonathan|author-last1=Holmes}}</ref><ref name="ars tech 3ds">{{cite web | url = https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2012/02/nintendo-blocks-3ds-binding-of-isaac-for-questionable-religious-content/ | title = Nintendo blocks 3DS Binding of Isaac for "questionable religious content" | date = February 29, 2012 | access-date = December 23, 2015 | first = Andrew | last = Groen | work = [[Ars Technica]] | archive-date = August 22, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170822221329/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2012/02/nintendo-blocks-3ds-binding-of-isaac-for-questionable-religious-content/ | url-status = live }}</ref> McMillen noted that Nintendo executives he spoke to before this decision had noted some blasphemous content would have been acceptable, and were more concerned with overtly religious content. He also noted that he was approached about his willingness to make some changes to the game to make it more suitable for the 3DS, but never was given a list of specific changes. McMillen speculated that Nintendo was worried about its reputation; because of the game's resemblance to ''The Legend of Zelda'', an unknowing child could potentially have downloaded the title and been shocked by the content, which would have reflected poorly on Nintendo.<ref name="mcmillen nintendo">{{cite web | url = https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2012/03/binding-of-isaac-creator-nintendo-rejection-shows-internal-divisions-over-companys-image/ | title = Binding of Isaac creator: Nintendo rejection shows internal divisions over company's image | first = Kyle | last = Orland | date = March 6, 2012 | access-date = May 10, 2016 | work = [[Ars Technica]] | archive-date = May 13, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160513010801/http://arstechnica.com/gaming/2012/03/binding-of-isaac-creator-nintendo-rejection-shows-internal-divisions-over-companys-image/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

Several game websites were outraged at Nintendo's decision.<ref name="3dsdestructoid" /><ref name="ars tech 3ds"/> Though disappointed with Nintendo's decision, McMillen did not think the loss of the 3DS port was a major issue, and saw a brief sales burst on Steam as the news was covered on gaming websites.<ref name="mcmillen nintendo"/> McMillen further praised the flexibility of the Steam platform, which does not require games to obtain [[ESRB]] ratings to be published on the service, and the freedom it gave to the publishers regardless of the game content.<ref name="3dsdestructoid" /><ref name="ars tech 3ds"/>

Nintendo would later allow the ''Rebirth'' remake to be released on both the New Nintendo 3DS and the [[Wii U]] in 2015; this came in part because Nintendo's Steve Singer (vice president of licensing), Mark Griffin (a senior manager in licensing), and Dan Adelman (the head of indie development) championed support for ''The Binding of Isaac''.<ref name="polygon new3ds">{{Cite web | url = http://www.polygon.com/2015/4/3/8341137/how-a-love-of-nintendo-finally-opened-the-door-for-the-binding-of | title = How a love of Nintendo opened the door for The Binding of Isaac and why it's only coming to New 3DS | first = Brian | last = Crecente | date = April 3, 2015 | access-date = February 7, 2016 | work = [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] | archive-date = April 15, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160415232458/http://www.polygon.com/2015/4/3/8341137/how-a-love-of-nintendo-finally-opened-the-door-for-the-binding-of | url-status = live }}</ref>

=== ''Wrath of the Lamb'' ===
{{Redirect|Wrath of the Lamb|the religious apocalypse|Book of Revelation}}

An expansion to the game, entitled ''Wrath of the Lamb'', was released through [[Steam (service)|Steam]] on May 28, 2012.<ref name="dlcdate">{{cite web|url=http://www.joystiq.com/2012/05/07/the-binding-of-isaacs-wrath-of-the-lamb-begins-may-28/|title=The Binding of Isaac's Wrath of the Lamb begins May 28|publisher=[[Joystiq]]|first=JC|last=Fletcher|date=May 7, 2012|access-date=May 7, 2012|archive-date=July 10, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120710000926/http://www.joystiq.com/2012/05/07/the-binding-of-isaacs-wrath-of-the-lamb-begins-may-28/|url-status=live}}</ref> McMillen was inspired to create the expansion not only due to the success of the base game, but because his wife Danielle had fully completed the base game, the first game he had written in which she had shown significant interest.<ref name="postmortem"/> The expansion adds 70% more content to the original, and contains more than 10 bosses, over 100 items, over 40 unlocks, two additional endings, and two additional optional levels.<ref name="GIdlc">{{cite web|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2012/05/07/huge-binding-of-isaac-expansion-coming-in-may.aspx|title=The Binding of Isaac Expansion Dated|publisher=[[Game Informer]]|first=Jeff|last=Marchiafava|date=May 7, 2012|access-date=May 7, 2012|archive-date=May 8, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508230754/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2012/05/07/huge-binding-of-isaac-expansion-coming-in-may.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> This expansion added new "alternate" floors, which can replace the normal floors, creating an alternate route through the game. These floors contain harder enemies, and a different set of bosses.  Other features include a new item type, Trinkets, which have a variety of passive or triggered effects when carried, as well as new room types.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://gamasutra.com/view/news/129312/McMillen_details_The_Wrath_Of_The_Lamb_as_Binding_Of_Isaac_sells_450k.php | title = McMillen details The Wrath Of The Lamb, as Binding Of Isaac sells 450k | work = [[Gamasutra]] | date = January 30, 2012 | access-date = April 14, 2016 | first = Lewie | last = Proctor | archive-date = September 14, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160914141228/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/129312/McMillen_details_The_Wrath_Of_The_Lamb_as_Binding_Of_Isaac_sells_450k.php | url-status = dead }}</ref> McMillen had plans to release a second expansion beyond ''Wrath of the Lamb'', but was constrained by the limits of Flash at this point.<ref name="postmortem"/> In May 2015, Florian Himsl released a final 'Eternal Edition' update for the [[Adobe Flash Player|Flash]] version, which introduced an 'Eternal' difficulty mode and rebalanced several items, serving as the final content expansion for the 2011 title before the developer shifted focus entirely to the [[The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth|''Rebirth'']] engine.<ref>{{Cite news |last=published |first=Tom Sykes |date=2015-05-03 |title=The Binding of Isaac: Eternal Edition out now |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-binding-of-isaac-eternal-edition-out-now/ |access-date=2026-05-29 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref>

=== ''The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth'' ===
{{Main|The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth}}

Sometime in 2012 after ''Isaac''{{'s}} release, McMillen was approached by Tyrone Rodriguez of [[Nicalis]] who asked if McMillen was interested in bringing the game to consoles. McMillen was interested, but insisted that they would have to reprogram the game to get around the limitations of Flash and to include ''Wrath of the Lamb'' and the second planned expansion, remaking the game's graphics in 16-bit instead of vector-based Flash graphics. Further, McMillen had wanted nothing to do with the business aspects of the game, having recounted the difficulties he had in handling this for ''Super Meat Boy''.<ref name="postmortem"/> Nicalis agreed to these, and began work in 2012 on what would become ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth]]'', an improved version of the title.<ref name="postmortem"/> It was released on November 4, 2014, for [[Microsoft Windows]], [[OS X]], [[Linux]], [[PlayStation 4]], and [[PlayStation Vita]],<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.vg247.com/2014/11/04/the-binding-of-isaac-rebirth-out-now-on-steam-psn/ | title = The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth out now on Steam, PSN | first = Brenna | last = Hillier | date = November 4, 2014 | access-date = April 20, 2016 | work = [[VG247]] | archive-date = August 25, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160825231932/https://www.vg247.com/2014/11/04/the-binding-of-isaac-rebirth-out-now-on-steam-psn/ | url-status = live }}</ref> with versions for the [[Wii U]], [[New Nintendo 3DS]], and [[Xbox One]] released on July 23, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://arstechnica.co.uk/gaming/2015/07/sacrilegious-binding-of-isaac-rebirth-finally-launches-on-nintendo-systems/ | title = Sacrilegious Binding of Isaac: Rebirth finally launches on Nintendo systems | first = Sam | last = Machkovech | work = [[Ars Technica]] | date = July 23, 2015 | access-date = April 20, 2016 | archive-date = May 13, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160513000300/http://arstechnica.co.uk/gaming/2015/07/sacrilegious-binding-of-isaac-rebirth-finally-launches-on-nintendo-systems/ | url-status = live }}</ref> The game introduced numerous new playable characters, items, enemies, bosses, challenges, and room layout seeds for floors. A content pack, entitled ''Afterbirth'' was released for ''Rebirth'' starting October 2015, adding new alternate chapters, characters and items, as well as wave-based Greed mode.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-09-08-the-binding-of-isaacs-meaty-afterbirth-expansion-pushes-out-a-release-date | title=The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth's meaty Afterbirth expansion pushes out a release date | work=[[Eurogamer]] | publisher=Gamer Network | first=Tom | last=Phillips | date=September 8, 2015 | access-date=September 8, 2015 | archive-date=September 11, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150911002054/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-09-08-the-binding-of-isaacs-meaty-afterbirth-expansion-pushes-out-a-release-date | url-status=live }}</ref> A second update, ''Afterbirth+'', added further additional content and support for user-created [[mod (video gaming)|modifications]], and was released on January 3, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-12-08-the-binding-of-isaac-to-receive-mod-tools-dlc | title = The Binding of Isaac to receive mod tools DLC | first = Jeffrey | last = Matulef | date = December 8, 2015 | access-date = December 8, 2015 | work = [[Eurogamer]] | archive-date = December 11, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151211034949/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-12-08-the-binding-of-isaac-to-receive-mod-tools-dlc | url-status = live }}</ref> A third and final update, ''Repentance'' added a lot of new content and bug fixes, including most of the content from ''Antibirth'', one of the biggest fan-made expansions, such as a new alternate path through the whole game as well as numerous character variations and new final bosses. This expansion was released on March 31, 2021.

=== Other games ===
McMillen collaborated with James Id to develop ''[[The Legend of Bum-bo]]'', which was released on November 12, 2019, for Windows and later for iOS and Switch.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.destructoid.com/the-legend-of-bum-bo-trailer-reveals-november-release-date-for-pc-565772.phtml | title = The Legend of Bum-Bo trailer reveals November release date for PC | first = Chris | last = Moyse | date = September 4, 2019 | access-date = September 4, 2019 | work = [[Destructoid]] }}{{Dead link|date=August 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> ''Bum-bo'' is described as a prequel to ''Isaac'', and Isaac and [[Gish (video game)|Gish]] appear as characters in the game.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.destructoid.com/binding-of-isaac-prequel-on-target-for-a-2017-release-459165.phtml | title = Binding of Isaac prequel on target for a 2017 release | first = Kevin | last = Mersereau | date = September 5, 2017 | access-date = September 5, 2017 | work = [[Destructoid]] | archive-date = September 8, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170908122606/https://www.destructoid.com/binding-of-isaac-prequel-on-target-for-a-2017-release-459165.phtml | url-status = live }}</ref> Isaac also appears as a playable character in the fighting game ''[[Blade Strangers]]'' and the puzzle game ''[[Crystal Crisis]]''.

On June 27, 2018, Edmund McMillen announced and later released a card game adaptation in cooperation with [[ProSiebenSat.1 Media|Studio 71]] titled ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/edmundmcmillen/status/1011368569332887553|title=The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls Announcement|website=Twitter|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-27|archive-date=November 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109015553/https://twitter.com/edmundmcmillen/status/1011368569332887553|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Reception ==
{{Video game reviews
| title = The Binding of Isaac
| MC = 84/100<ref name="MC"/>
| EuroG = 9/10<ref name="eurogamer review"/>
| Edge = 8/10<ref name="edge review"/>
| GI = 8/10<ref name="gi review"/>
| GSpot = 8/10<ref name="gamespot review"/>
| GSpy = 4.5/5<ref name="gspy review"/>
| IGN = 7.5/10<ref name="ign review"/>
| Destruct = 9.5/10<ref>{{cite web |last1=Devore |first1=Jordan |title=Review: The Binding of Isaac |url=https://www.destructoid.com/reviews/review-the-binding-of-isaac/ |website=[[Destructoid]] |date=12 September 2021 |access-date=12 September 2021 |archive-date=September 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210912151449/https://www.destructoid.com/reviews/review-the-binding-of-isaac/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
}}

''The Binding of Isaac'' received generally favorable reviews from game critics. On [[Metacritic]], the game has an average of 84 out of 100 based on 30 reviews.<ref name="MC">{{cite web|url=http://www.metacritic.com/game/pc/the-binding-of-isaac|title=The Binding of Isaac for PC Metacritic Score|access-date=November 3, 2011|publisher=CBS Interactive|work=Metacritic|archive-date=May 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510012035/http://www.metacritic.com/game/pc/the-binding-of-isaac|url-status=live}}</ref>

''The Binding of Isaac'' has been received by reviewers as a game with high replayability with the extensive range and combinations of power-ups that the player can encounter during a run-through, while providing an accessible ''Zelda''-inspired framework that most video game players would recognize and easily come to understand.<ref name="eurogamer review"/><ref name="dtoid review"/><ref name="gspy review"/> John Teti for ''[[Eurogamer]]'' praised the game for its replayability through the randomization aspects, calling it "the most accessible exploration of the roguelike idea" that he had seen.<ref name="eurogamer review">{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-10-07-the-binding-of-isaac-review|title=The Binding of Isaac Review|first=John|last=Teti|access-date=November 3, 2011|date=October 7, 2011|work=[[Eurogamer]]|archive-date=June 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170614155809/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-10-07-the-binding-of-isaac-review|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Edge (magazine)|Edge]]''{{'}}s similarly commented on the lure to replay the game due to its short playthrough time, calling it "an imaginative and quick-witted arcade experience that manages to be both depraved and strangely sweet by turn".<ref name="edge review">{{cite magazine | url = http://www.next-gen.biz/reviews/binding-isaac-review | title = The Binding of Isaac Review | date = October 7, 2011 | magazine = [[Edge (magazine)|Edge]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20111008084139/http://www.next-gen.biz/reviews/binding-isaac-review | archive-date = October 8, 2011 | access-date = April 14, 2016 }}</ref> ''[[GameSpot]]''{{'}}s Maxwell McGee stated that the game smartly has removed extraneous features such that "what remains is a tightly focused game that continues to feel fresh even after multiple completions".<ref name="gamespot review">{{cite web | url = http://www.gamespot.com/reviews/the-binding-of-isaac-review/1900-6346463/ | title = The Binding of Isaac Review | first = Maxwell | last = McGee | date = November 21, 2011 | access-date = April 14, 2016 | work = [[GameSpot]] | archive-date = August 5, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160805061212/http://www.gamespot.com/reviews/the-binding-of-isaac-review/1900-6346463/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Though the game is considered to be accessible to new players, reviewers found the game to be a difficult challenge, often set by the randomness of what power-ups the player happened to acquire during a single run.<ref name="dtoid review"/><ref name="gspy review"/><ref name="gi review"/> Writers for ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' rated the game an A on a grading scale, and favorably compared the title to McMillen's ''Super Meat Boy'', requiring the player to have "masochistic patience in the face of terrible odds".<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.avclub.com/article/october-10-2011-63022 | title = Sawbuck Gamer, October 10, 2011 | work = [[The A.V. Club]] |author=Anthony John Agnello |author2=Noah Cruickshank |author3=Russ Fischer |author4=Steve Heisler |author5=Rowan Kaiser |author6=Gus Mastrapa |author7=Samantha Nelson |author8=Tasha Robinson |author9=John Teti | date = October 10, 2011 | access-date = April 14, 2016 | archive-date = March 6, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160306170220/http://www.avclub.com/article/october-10-2011-63022 | url-status = live }}</ref> This difficulty was considered mitigated by the large number of possible power-ups that the game offers, most would not be seen by players until they have replayed the game many times.<ref name="eurogamer review"/> McGee noted that while players can review what items they have discovered prior to a run-through, this feature does not explain what each item does, leaving the effect to be determined by the player while in game.<ref name="gamespot review"/>

''[[Game Informer]]''{{'}}s Adam Biessener noted that while ''The Binding of Isaac'' had a number of software bugs on release that may briefly detract from the experience, "McMillen's vision shines through" in the game's playability, art style, and story.<ref name="gi review">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/games/the_binding_of_isaac/b/pc/archive/2011/10/03/equal-parts-gross-disturbing-and-fun.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005094818/http://www.gameinformer.com/games/the_binding_of_isaac/b/pc/archive/2011/10/03/equal-parts-gross-disturbing-and-fun.aspx|url-status=live|archive-date=October 5, 2011|title=Equal Parts Gross, Disturbing, And Fun&nbsp;– The Binding of Isaac&nbsp;– PC| magazine = [[Game Informer]] |date=October 3, 2011|access-date= November 3, 2011|first=Adam|last=Biessener}}</ref>  Neilie Johnson for ''[[IGN]]'' found that some players may be put off by the game's crudeness but otherwise "it's totally random, highly creative and brutally unforgiving".<ref name="ign review">{{cite web|first=Neilie|last=Johnson|url=http://pc.ign.com/articles/119/1199423p1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111013174314/http://pc.ign.com/articles/119/1199423p1.html|archive-date=October 13, 2011|title=The Binding of Isaac Review&nbsp;– PC Review at IGN|publisher=IGN Entertainment|work=[[IGN]]|date=October 11, 2011|access-date=November 3, 2011}}</ref> Similarly, Nathan Muenier for ''[[GameSpy]]'' noted the game had some shock value that one must work past, but otherwise was "imaginative" and "utterly absorbing".<ref name="gspy review">{{cite web|url=http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/the-binding-of-isaac/1197645p1.html|title=GameSpy: The Binding of Isaac Review&nbsp;– Page 1|publisher=IGN Entertainment|work=[[GameSpy]]|date=September 30, 2011|access-date=November 3, 2011|first=Nathan|last=Meunier|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052905/http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/the-binding-of-isaac/1197645p1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Alternatively, Jordan Devore for ''[[Destructoid]]'' considered the visual style of the game one of its "biggest selling points", following from McMillen's past style of [[dark comedy]] from ''Super Meat Boy''.<ref name="dtoid review">{{Cite web | url = http://www.destructoid.com/review-the-binding-of-isaac-212806.phtml | title = Review: The Binding of Isaac | work = [[Destructoid]] | first = Jordan | last = Devore | date = October 2, 2011 | access-date = May 9, 2016 | archive-date = April 18, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160418165748/http://www.destructoid.com/review-the-binding-of-isaac-212806.phtml | url-status = live }}</ref> Baranowsky's soundtrack was found by reviewers to well-suit the themes of the game, and used appropriately to avoid extensive repetition during a playthrough.<ref name="gamespot review"/><ref name="dtoid review"/> Kirk Hamilton of ''[[Kotaku]]'' called the soundtrack as the combination of several genres and the musical styles of [[Danny Elfman]], [[Muse (band)|Muse]], and ''[[Music of Final Fantasy|Final Fantasy]]'' that created something "dark and unique".<ref name="kotaku soundtrack"/>

''The Binding of Isaac'' was nominated in the Best Independent Game category at the 2011 [[Spike Video Game Awards]], but lost to ''[[Minecraft]]''.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.gamesradar.com/2011-spike-vga-nominees-announced-zelda-become-first-hall-famer/ | title = 2011 Spike VGA nominees announced, Zelda to become first Hall of Famer | first = Matt | last = Bradford | date = November 17, 2011 | access-date = May 10, 2016 | work = [[GamesRadar]] | archive-date = December 31, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151231202451/http://www.gamesradar.com/2011-spike-vga-nominees-announced-zelda-become-first-hall-famer/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

McMillen had only expected the game to sell a few hundred copies when he released it on Steam. For the first few months of its release, sales were roughly a few hundred per day, but shortly thereafter, McMillen found sales suddenly were boosted, a fact he attributed to numerous [[Let's Play (video gaming)|Let's Play]] videos that had been published by players to showcase the game and drove sales.<ref name="pcgamer end">{{cite web | url = https://www.pcgamer.com/how-mods-made-the-binding-of-isaac-a-phenomenon-and-why-edmund-mcmillens-laying-it-to-rest/ | title = How mods made The Binding of Isaac a phenomenon, and why Edmund McMillen's laying it to rest | first = Anthony | last = McGlynn | date = June 5, 2018 | access-date = June 5, 2018 | work = [[PC Gamer]] | archive-date = April 19, 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210419164609/https://www.pcgamer.com/how-mods-made-the-binding-of-isaac-a-phenomenon-and-why-edmund-mcmillens-laying-it-to-rest/ | url-status = live }}</ref> This popularity also drew interest by players that wanted to create [[Mod (video gaming)|custom mods]] for the game, which would become a factor in the design of the sequel to better support modding.<ref name="pcgamer end"/>

By November 2012, the game sold over one million copies, with at least one-quarter of those having purchased the "Wrath of the Lamb" extension.<ref name="postmortem"/> As of July 2014, the game has sold over 3 million copies.<ref name="ign roguelike">{{cite web | url = http://www.ign.com/articles/2014/07/04/roguelikes-the-rebirth-of-the-counterculture | title = Roguelikes: The Rebirth of the Counterculter | first = Mike | last = Mahardy | date = July 4, 2014 | access-date = December 23, 2015 | work = [[IGN]] | archive-date = September 3, 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140903073824/http://www.ign.com/articles/2014/07/04/roguelikes-the-rebirth-of-the-counterculture | url-status = live }}</ref> By July 2015, following the release of ''Rebirth'', the combined games had over 5 million units sold.<ref name="goodtimes">{{cite web | url = http://www.gtweekly.com/index.php/santa-cruz-news/good-times-cover-stories/6746-the-binding-of-edmund-mcmillen.html | title = The Binding of Edmund McMillen | first = Sam | last = Working | publisher = [[Good Times (newspaper)|Good Times]] | date = July 22, 2015 | access-date = February 11, 2016 | archive-date = February 16, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160216064257/http://www.gtweekly.com/index.php/santa-cruz-news/good-times-cover-stories/6746-the-binding-of-edmund-mcmillen.html  }}</ref> ''The Binding of Isaac'' is said to be a contributing factor towards the growth of the [[roguelike]] genre since around 2010, with its success paving the way for later games that used the roguelike formula, such as ''[[FTL: Faster Than Light]]'' and ''[[Don't Starve]]''.<ref name="ign roguelike"/><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2015/07/before-spelunky-and-ftl-there-was-only-ascii.html | title = Before Spelunky and FTL, There Was Only ASCII | first = Mark | last = Johnson | work = [[Paste (magazine)|Paste]] | date = July 22, 2015 | access-date = April 14, 2016 | archive-date = July 28, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150728171247/http://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2015/07/before-spelunky-and-ftl-there-was-only-ascii.html | url-status = live }}</ref>

'''''Vampire Survivors''''', also known as '''''Vampire Survivors — First Survivaton''''', is a 2022 independent [[roguelike]] [[shoot 'em up]] [[video game]] developed and published by poncle. Following an [[early access]] period that began in December 2021, it was released for [[macOS]], [[Windows]], [[Xbox One]], [[Xbox Series X/S]], [[Android (operating system)|Android]], and [[iOS]] in late 2022. A [[Video game port|port]] for [[Nintendo Switch]] was released on August 17, 2023, and on August 29, 2024, a port was released for [[PlayStation 4]] and [[PlayStation 5]]. A [[virtual reality]] port for the [[Meta Quest]] was released in November 2025.

Players control an automatically attacking character while battling continuous waves of monsters, aiming to survive the onslaught for as long as possible and unlock additional characters, weapons, and relics for future sessions. The game was initially a small project Galante made while unemployed and released at a very low cost. It drew far greater sales than Galante expected, leading to him bringing on additional developers to improve the engine and expand the game. It has had several free and paid expansions, including a pack based on ''[[Castlevania]]'', a series Galante had used for inspiration. 

''Vampire Survivors'' received accolades at the [[Golden Joystick Awards]], [[New York Game Awards]], and [[D.I.C.E. Awards]]. The game was nominated in five categories at the [[British Academy Games Awards]], winning two: [[British Academy Games Award for Game Design|Game Design]] and [[British Academy Games Award for Best Game|Best Game]]. The game is considered one of the first "bullet heaven" games and has led to [[Vampire Survivors–like|numerous titles with similar auto-combat mechanics]]. A spin-off [[roguelike deck-building game|roguelike deck-builder]], ''[[Vampire Crawlers]]'', was released on April 21, 2026.

== Gameplay ==
The player selects one of multiple characters, each with different starting weapons and bonuses, and control them on an endless stage featuring an auto-generated, repeating layout. The player's weapons attack automatically, and the goal is to survive as long as possible against constant waves of monsters that inflict damage upon contact. Defeating monsters and exploring the stage allows to collect experience gems, which are used to level up; "floor chicken", which restores the player's [[health (video gaming)|health]]; and other helpful items. Each level increase gives the choice of three or four weapons and power-ups named "passives". Once players have collected six weapons and six power-ups and upgraded them fully, any further levels gained will offer only gold coins or floor chicken.

Another way to upgrade weapons and passives is by opening chests, which are dropped by particularly powerful monsters and may contain one, three, or five random items. Most weapons have an ultimate (or "evolved") form that can be attained by opening a chest after fully upgrading them and meeting other specific conditions, typically having a specific passive or that passive at max level.<ref name="rps">{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Graham |date=January 25, 2022 |title=Vampire Survivors is a pure hit of dopamine |work=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]] |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/vampire-survivors-is-a-pure-hit-of-dopamine |access-date=January 30, 2022 |archive-date=February 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201204654/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/vampire-survivors-is-a-pure-hit-of-dopamine |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="polygon">{{Cite web |last=Carpenter |first=Nicole |date=January 27, 2022 |title=Vampire Survivors is no thoughts, just spells |url=https://www.polygon.com/22905166/vampire-survivors-steam-indie-hit |access-date=January 30, 2022 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |archive-date=March 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220331085102/https://www.polygon.com/22905166/vampire-survivors-steam-indie-hit |url-status=live }}</ref>

Sessions of ''Vampire Survivors'' have a soft time limit of 15, 20, or 30 minutes, depending on the selected stage. When the time limit is reached, all enemies are cleared from the stage, and a final powerful enemy named The Reaper spawns. One additional Reaper will appear every consecutive minute thereafter to ensure the player's eventual demise. A session that meets or exceeds the stage's time limit is considered a successful completion and rewards bonus gold coins. Between sessions, accumulated gold coins can be spent to unlock characters and persistent power-ups. Additionally, by completing challenges, players can unlock stages, weapons, and characters, as well as various game modifiers, such as an endless mode that removes the soft time limit, a hyper mode that increases player and enemy speed, and a limit break mode that allows players to continue enhancing weapon attributes after fully leveling them. The player can obtain golden eggs by defeating certain enemies or purchasing them from an in-game vendor, which provide permanent attribute improvements to the selected character.

== Plot ==
''Vampire Survivors'' is nominally set in rural Italy in 2021. Hordes of monsters summoned by the evil Bisconte Draculó (a villain inspired by [[Count Dracula]]) ravage the land, prompting the Belpaese family and other heroic survivors to take it upon themselves to hunt down and defeat Draculó.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vampire Survivors by poncle |url=https://poncle.itch.io/vampire-survivors |access-date=May 11, 2022 |website=itch.io |archive-date=October 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021010637/https://poncle.itch.io/vampire-survivors |url-status=live }}</ref> This quest takes them through monster-infested locales such as a cursed forest, a haunted library, an abandoned dairy plant, an ominous tower, and an otherworldly chapel, culminating in a battle against an Eldritch otherworldly being referred to as "The Directer". Despite the game's title, the characters do not fight any vampires in the story.<ref>{{cite web | last=Valentine | first=Rebekah | title=Will Vampire Survivors Ever Have an Actual Vampire? We Asked the Creator | website=IGN | date=2022-12-29 | url=https://www.ign.com/articles/will-vampire-survivors-ever-have-an-actual-vampire-we-asked-the-creator | access-date=2025-04-14}}</ref>

== Development ==
[[File:Vampire_Survivors_gameplay.png|right|thumb|Gameplay screenshot.]]
Italian developer Luca "poncle" Galante began developing ''Vampire Survivors'' in 2020 using the [[Phaser (game framework)|Phaser]] framework while he was unemployed.<ref name="news.com.au" /><ref name="Barclays Games and Esports 2022">{{Cite web |date=August 10, 2022 |title=How Vampire Survivors became a hit when creator poncle was ready to give up |url=https://games.barclays/resource-hub/games/industry-insights/how-vampire-survivors-became-a-hit-when-creator-poncle-was-ready-to-give-up/ |access-date=January 4, 2023 |website=Barclays Games and Esports |archive-date=June 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603070426/https://games.barclays/resource-hub/games/industry-insights/how-vampire-survivors-became-a-hit-when-creator-poncle-was-ready-to-give-up/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He aimed to create ''Vampire Survivors'' to manage a community, drawing from his past experience as an administrator for an ''[[Ultima Online]]'' server. The game was inspired by ''[[Magic Survival]]'', a 2019 mobile game that also featured a character that automatically attacks enemies.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stanton |first=Rich |date=March 30, 2022 |title=Vampire Survivors creator 'didn't have a vision' when he started making the game that allowed him to quit his job |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/vampire-survivors-creator-didnt-have-a-vision-when-he-started-making-the-game-that-allowed-him-to-quit-his-job/ |access-date=April 12, 2024 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref> 

Development of the initial early access version took about a year, during which Galante spent around £1,100 on assets, art, and music.<ref name="vice">{{Cite web |last=Klepek |first=Patrick |date=January 27, 2022 |title=How 'Vampire Survivors' Went From Obscurity to 27,000 People Playing at Once |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/how-vampire-survivors-went-from-obscurity-to-27000-people-playing-at-once/ |access-date=January 30, 2022 |website=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |archive-date=February 23, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220223023853/https://www.vice.com/en/article/z3nyze/how-vampire-survivors-went-from-obscurity-to-27000-people-playing-at-once |url-status=live }}</ref> Galante was inspired by the ''[[Castlevania]]'' games, and one of the art asset packs included sprites in a similar style to the characters in the early ''Castlevania'' games.<ref name="pcgamer Castlevania DLC" >{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/action/please-try-not-to-binge-it-vampire-survivors-finally-releases-a-castlevania-dlc-with-20-new-characters-40-new-weapons-and-a-monstrously-large-stage |title='Please try not to binge it': Vampire Survivors finally releases a Castlevania DLC with 20 new characters, 40 new weapons, and 'a monstrously large stage' |first=Elie |last=Gould |work=PCGamer |date=October 21, 2024 |access-date=May 21, 2025}}</ref> Prior to developing ''Vampire Survivors'', Galante worked in the gambling industry, using his knowledge of flashy graphics for slot machines as part of the appeal for the game's chest-opening animations.<ref name="news.com.au">{{Cite web |last=Chung |first=Frank |date=February 23, 2022 |title=Creator of addictive $4 game Vampire Survivors was gambling industry programmer |url=https://www.news.com.au/technology/gaming/creator-of-addictive-4-game-vampire-survivors-was-gambling-industry-programmer/news-story/3a58941869837cd1b03b73c07798f050 |access-date=December 10, 2022 |website=[[news.com.au]]}}</ref>

Galante released his initial version of ''Vampire Survivors'' on [[itch.io]], but did not see much engagement. He decided to release it on [[Steam (service)|Steam]] before the end of 2021, keeping the cost low since the game had minimal art aesthetics. The low price meant that his game could reach a larger audience. However, on the same day, he contracted [[COVID-19]] and focused his attention on his recovery rather than on how his game was selling. In early 2022, he learned that the game had caught the attention of some YouTube creators, which led to an increase in Steam sales.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XQVdR8mJrds |title=The Making of Vampire Survivors - Documentary |date=July 17, 2023 |last=O'Dwyer |first=Danny |publisher=[[Noclip]] |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>  

The success exceeded Galante's expectations and allowed him to quit his job in February 2022 to focus entirely on its development. He was informally assisted by "a few friends" in their spare time. Planned content included additional weapons, characters, stages, and an "endless mode". Galante's intent was to bring ''Vampire Survivors'' out of early access by the end of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Andy |date=February 3, 2022 |title='Vampire Survivors' creator Luca Galante talks quitting his job to fulfil his promise |url=https://www.nme.com/features/gaming-features/vampire-survivors-creator-luca-galante-talks-quitting-his-job-to-fulfil-his-promise-3153107 |access-date=March 6, 2022 |website=[[NME]] |archive-date=March 26, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220326101919/https://www.nme.com/features/gaming-features/vampire-survivors-creator-luca-galante-talks-quitting-his-job-to-fulfil-his-promise-3153107 |url-status=live }}</ref> 

In March 2022, Galante hired multiple freelancers to expand the ''Vampire Survivors'' team and accelerate development. In addition to outlining the scope of the promised new content with a roadmap, he explained that a major milestone slated for mid-2022 would be porting ''Vampire Survivors'' to an "industry-standard" game engine to improve its overall performance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 24, 2022 |title=Development Roadmap Overview and updates on the plan for Early Access |url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1794680/view/3131696199131643254 |access-date=March 29, 2022 |website=[[Steam (service)|Steam]] |archive-date=October 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005121816/https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1794680/view/3131696199131643254 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As part of a free update in June 2026, the game's name was expanded as ''Vampire Survivors — First Survivaton''.<ref name=Survivaton/> This came as Poncle began to release other bullet heaven style games that it had developed. The term "Survivaton" is a play on the phrase "survive a ton", and was added to establish ''Vampire Survivors'' as the flagship title in these games.<ref>https://www.eurogamer.net/vampire-survivors-new-name-first-survivaton-bloodmoon-dlc</ref>

===Downloadable content===  
The first paid [[downloadable content]] (DLC) expansion, ''Legacy of the Moonspell'', was announced on December 6, 2022. Inspired by [[Japanese folklore]] and [[anime]], it adds thirteen weapons, eight characters, and a stage featuring enemies designed after ''[[yōkai]]'' and ''[[oni]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Graham |date=December 6, 2022 |title=Vampire Survivors is getting DLC inspired by Japanese folklore next week |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/vampire-survivors-is-getting-dlc-inspired-by-japanese-folklore-next-week |access-date=December 9, 2022 |website=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]] |archive-date=March 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316012648/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/vampire-survivors-is-getting-dlc-inspired-by-japanese-folklore-next-week |url-status=live }}</ref> The expansion was released on December 15, 2022, for macOS, Windows, and Xbox platforms, with a mobile release in early 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orland |first=Kyle |date=December 15, 2022 |title=Vampire Survivors' first DLC offers some enjoyable (but diminishing) returns |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2022/12/vampire-survivors-first-dlc-offers-some-enjoyable-but-diminishing-returns/ |access-date=December 15, 2022 |website=Ars Technica |archive-date=March 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328161059/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2022/12/vampire-survivors-first-dlc-offers-some-enjoyable-but-diminishing-returns/ |url-status=live }}</ref> A second paid expansion, ''Tides of Foscari'', was released in April 2023. It introduces 13 weapons, 8 characters and a passive only obtained with some of the characters and in both stages. In addition, ''Tides of Foscari'' features two stages inspired by [[fairy tale]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Sean |date=March 31, 2023 |title=Vampire Survivors Reveals Second DLC With New Characters, Weapons, And Music |url=https://www.thegamer.com/vampire-survivors-dlc-tides-of-foscari/ |access-date=April 16, 2023 |website=The Gamer |archive-date=June 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603211321/https://www.thegamer.com/vampire-survivors-dlc-tides-of-foscari/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Purchese |first=Robert |date=April 14, 2023 |title=Vampire Survivors is revived by new DLC Tides of the Foscari |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/vampire-survivors-is-revived-by-new-dlc-tides-of-the-foscari |access-date=April 16, 2023 |website=Eurogamer |archive-date=May 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230516064710/https://www.eurogamer.net/vampire-survivors-is-revived-by-new-dlc-tides-of-the-foscari |url-status=live }}</ref> A third original expansion, ''Legacy of the Bloodmoon'', released on August 28, 2026. It adds 12 characters, 18 new weapons, 1 new passive item, and a stage described as the "evil twin" of ''Legacy of the Moonspell''.<ref name=Survivaton>{{cite web | last=LeBlanc | first=Wesley | title=Poncle Reveals Vampire Survivors: Legacy Of The Bloodmoon Expansion, New Japanese Studio Led By DMC Artist, And More | website=Game Informer | date=June 6, 2026 | url=https://gameinformer.com/sgf-2026/2026/06/06/poncle-reveals-vampire-survivors-legacy-of-the-bloodmoon-expansion-new-japanese | access-date=June 6, 2026}}</ref>

The game has released expansions featuring elements from other video games. ''Emergency Meeting'', based on Innersloth's ''[[Among Us]]'', was released on December 18, 2023, with 15 weapons, 9 characters and 8 passives. It features a stage based on the ''Among Us'' map Polus.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.ign.com/videos/vampire-survivors-emergency-meeting-dlc-feat-among-us-official-trailer |title=Vampire Survivors: Emergency Meeting DLC feat. Among Us - Official Trailer |date=December 6, 2023 |language=en |access-date=August 8, 2024 |via=[[IGN]]}}</ref> ''Operation Guns'', based on [[Konami]]'s ''[[Contra (series)|Contra]]'', was released on May 9, 2024, with 12 characters, 22 weapons and 2 stages, as well as a passive.<ref name="ps4"/> ''Ode to Castlevania'', based on Konami's ''[[Castlevania]]'' series, was released on October 31, 2024, coinciding with Halloween. It is the largest DLC, with 80 characters on release, and was updated to add 16 more, over 100 weapons, with weapons being added later, and one huge stage, with more weapons and characters than the  base game. Galante said that ''Ode to Castlevania'' was a "full circle moment" for him with the game.<ref>{{cite web | last=Scullion | first=Chris | title=Vampire Survivors is getting Castlevania DLC later this month | website=VGC | date=October 21, 2024 | url=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/vampire-survivors-is-getting-castlevania-dlc-later-this-month/ | access-date=October 21, 2024}}</ref><ref name="pcgamer Castlevania DLC" /> The ''Ode to Castlevania'' includes voicework from [[Neil Newbon]] as [[Dracula (Castlevania)|Dracula]] and [[SungWon Cho]] as [[Richter Belmont]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.gamesradar.com/games/roguelike/after-3-years-and-over-30-updates-vampire-survivors-finally-has-vampires-and-even-baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-actor-is-here-as-dracula/ | title = After 3 years and over 30 updates, Vampire Survivors finally has vampires - and even Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion actor is here as Dracula | first = Kaar | last = Sarin | date = November 2, 2024 | accessdate = November 2, 2024 | work = [[GamesRadar+]] }}</ref> ''Emerald Diorama'', based on [[Square Enix]]'s ''[[SaGa: Emerald Beyond]]'', was released for free on April 10, 2025, adding 16 characters, 35 weapons, a stage and a 'glimmer' mechanic.<ref>{{cite web | last=Hagues | first=Alana | title=Vampire Survivors And Square Enix Team Up For Free DLC, But It's Not The Series You'd Expect | website=Nintendo Life | date=April 10, 2025 | url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/04/vampire-survivors-and-square-enix-team-up-for-free-dlc-but-its-not-the-series-youd-expect | access-date=April 10, 2025}}</ref> ''Ante Chamber'', a small expansion based on LocalThunk's ''[[Balatro]]'', was released for free on October 28, 2025, with 4 characters, 8 weapons, a stage based on ''Balatro''{{'}}s UI and a passive.<ref name=ante>{{cite web | last=Bonk | first=Lawrence | title=Balatro comes to Vampire Survivors in the form of a free expansion | website=Engadget | date=October 28, 2025 | url=https://www.engadget.com/gaming/balatro-comes-to-vampire-survivors-in-the-form-of-a-free-expansion-183005013.html | access-date=November 15, 2025}}</ref>

===''Vampire Crawlers''===
{{main|Vampire Crawlers}} 
In 2025, Poncle announced a spinoff of ''Vampire Survivors'', named ''Vampire Crawlers'', developed by Nosebleed Interactive, released on April 21, 2026.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.eurogamer.net/vampire-crawlers-turns-vampire-survivors-into-a-dungeon-crawling-card-game-with-mixed-success | title = Vampire Crawlers turns Vampire Survivors into a dungeon-crawling card game with mixed success | first = Robert | last = Purchase | date = February 28, 2026 | accessdate = February 28, 2026 | work = [[Eurogamer]] }}</ref> ''Vampire Crawlers'' is a [[roguelike deck-building game]], with the player traveling between encounters, using a deck of cards they build up to fight enemies and gain rewards. While it uses the same approach as traditional deck-builder games where the player has time to think about how to play their cards, ''Vampire Crawlers'' also allows the player to rapidly play cards for different effects.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/vampire-crawlers-a-first-person-deck-building-vampire-survivors-spin-off-is-coming-next-year/ | title = Vampire Crawlers, a first-person deck building Vampire Survivors spin-off, is coming next year | first = Jordan | last = Middler | date = November 20, 2025 | accessdate = November 21, 2025 | work = [[Video Games Chronicle]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/vampire-crawlers-a-first-person-deck-building-vampire-survivors-spin-off-is-coming-next-year/ | title = Vampire Crawlers Is The Next Game From The Vampire Survivors Team | first = Brian | last = Shae | date = November 20, 2025 | accessdate = November 21, 2025 | work = [[Game Informer]] }}</ref> According to Galante, work on ''Vampire Crawlers'' had started shortly after ''Vampire Survivors'' had become a success around 2021. Galante had considered talking to other studios to make spin-offs of ''Vampire Survivors'', one prototype from Nosebleed which became ''Vampire Crawlers''. With all the assets that Poncle had developed for ''Vampire Survivors'', they reused most of the same characters, weapons, creatures, and other assets with ''Vampire Crawlers'', in part to avoid having to develop a new narrative angle while also simplifying development.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2025/11/20/vampire-crawlers-xbox-partner-preview/ | title = Xbox Partner Preview {{!}} Vampire Crawlers: Breaking Down the Surprise Vampire Survivors Spin-Off with its Creator  | first = Joe | last = Skrebels | date = November 20, 2025 | accessdate = November 21, 2025 | work = [[Xbox Wire]] }}</ref>

===Film adaptation===  
An animated ''Vampire Survivors'' television series was announced in April 2023, to be produced by Story Kitchen in partnership with Luca Galante.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shanklin |first=Will |date=April 28, 2023 |title='Vampire Survivors' is getting an animated television series |url=https://www.engadget.com/vampire-survivors-is-getting-an-animated-television-series-165532824.html |access-date=April 28, 2023 |website=[[Engadget]] |archive-date=June 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625020659/https://www.engadget.com/vampire-survivors-is-getting-an-animated-television-series-165532824.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=April 30, 2023 |title='Vampire Survivors' Video Game In Works As Animated Television Series From Story Kitchen |url=https://deadline.com/2023/04/vampire-survivors-video-game-animated-television-series-story-kitchen-luca-galante-poncle-trailer-1235340337/ |access-date=April 30, 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=July 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230731030319/https://deadline.com/2023/04/vampire-survivors-video-game-animated-television-series-story-kitchen-luca-galante-poncle-trailer-1235340337/ |url-status=live }}</ref> However, in January 2025, it was confirmed that the project was being reworked into a live-action film, with Story Kitchen still involved in the production.<ref>{{cite web | title=Vampire Survivors Dev Poncle Outlines Challenges of Film Adaptation: 'The Game Has No Plot' | website=IGN | date=January 20, 2025 |first=Ryan |last=Dinsdale | url=https://www.ign.com/articles/vampire-survivors-dev-poncle-outlines-challenges-of-film-adaptation-the-game-has-no-plot | access-date=April 14, 2025}}</ref>

===Comic series===
A four-issue comic series will be published by [[Titan Comics]] starting in September 2026. The series will be written by [[David Hazan]] and illustrated by [[Jimmy Kucaj]].<ref>https://www.ign.com/articles/vampire-survivors-comic-book-adaptation-launches-this-fall</ref>
